News.title: Chilling new UFO footage released as ‘sightings’ caught by special forces & mystery govt agent who saw ‘black hot craft’
News.content:
EERY footage released by the Pentagon captures multiple unexplained flying objects with one special agent recalling an encounter with a “black-hot” craft.

The 41-file dump posted to the U.S Department of War website on Friday disclosed a mix of documents, images and videos dating as far back as 1953.



Under an executive order President Trump directing the military and other agencies to produce more documents related to UFOs, this release comes as the fifth since January.

One video captured by a mystery government agent in western US last year shows “two, slow-moving ‘black-hot’ areas of contrast, visible in infrared imaging.”



The FBI report said: “He saw a black object in the sky.

“It was not moving fast. He took pictures using the optical device.



“While observing he saw a second object to the right of the first and took additional photos/videos.

“The objects were moving together at the same speed.



“Both were black hot. He lost view of the objects when they traveled a distance out of view.

“Total observation time was approximately 5 – 10 minutes.”

8 Credit: The Pentagon

In military sensor terminology, “black hot” is a thermal imaging display mode where warmer objects – like engines or human bodies – appear dark or black.



Also among the clips is footage filmed over the Gulf of Oman in 2021, appearing to show a dark orb moving in irregularly through the sky.

The object, described as a “cold orb”, was reportedly about 4ft in width.

An accompanying intelligence report sheds more light on the footage.



The report said the forces onboard the gunship “observed approximately 25 instances of UAPs while conducting a live fire exercise in the Gulf of Oman.”

It said: “The UAPs were observed as cold orbs flying at lower altitudes between 250 to 1300 MPH in different formations as well as manoeuvring aggressively. UAPs also appeared to react to the aircraft firing its main cannon.”

Another video, captured by a US military sensor at an undisclosed location in the Middle East in 2025, appears to show a round sphere travelling in a straight line over a built-up residential area.

Much of the videos are comprised of grainy footage that is not dissimilar to other past disclosures.

All of the images in the latest release are artistic recreations based on witnesses’ first-hand descriptions of alleged extraterrestrial encounters.



One image from a 2011 sighting shows a large triangular object in the sky with lights on each point.

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said on Friday: “The Department of War is in lockstep with President Trump to bring unprecedented transparency regarding our government’s understanding of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena.

“These files, hidden behind classifications, have long fueled justified speculation, and it’s time the American people see it for themselves.

“This release of declassified documents demonstrates the Trump Administration’s earnest commitment to unprecedented transparency.”

In June, another Pentagon released shared several accounts of orbs moving across the sky.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The witnesses separately described seeing a bright orange “mother orb” that appeared to create “smaller red orbs” over the course of several hours.

The sightings began in 2021 and have occurred multiple times at an irregular pace.

News.title: Andy Burnham has got cop killers’ release badly wrong – now he must listen and put it right
News.content:
Listen, PM

PM Andy Burnham is at last said to be considering a U-turn over the early release of the killers of PC Andrew Harper.

It’s not a moment too soon. Our new Prime Minister likes to paint himself as a champion against injustice.



So how on earth did he ever end up on the side of two cop-killers?

His original decision not to exempt Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole from Labour’s early prisoner release scheme has infuriated Andrew’s family and widow Lissie who have endured years of grief.



Senior police officers — including the Chief Constable of Thames Valley Police, the Met Commissioner and the senior detective who put Andrew’s killers behind bars — all say ordinary cops are being badly let down.

Then there is the huge outpouring of public anger.



That is crystal clear in the 700,000 signatures on a petition demanding Cole and Bowers stay locked up.

Burnham’s strategy was to blame prison overcrowding on the Tories and hope the problem goes away.

But HE raised the hopes of Andrew’s family by pausing early releases entirely in response to their case.

Officials are now apparently exploring a way to keep the PC’s killers locked up.



Leadership is about more than putting out TikToks about scampi fries. It’s about doing the right thing, however difficult it is to get done.

Burnham has got this badly wrong and it’s right that he reverses his mistake.

Real danger

THE last week has shown again the huge dangers to our society of failing to control our borders.

Hundreds more unvetted migrants broke into Britain in the last seven days.

Riots have broken out in normally sleepy Thetford, sparked by local unhappiness at illegal asylum seekers being housed in flats in the town.



The weak-minded open borders mob within Labour loves to belittle the small boats crisis as an obsession whipped up by far-right racists.

In fact, it’s a very real threat to our national security and, increasingly, to the safety of women and girls.

Or don’t they care about that?

What resolve?

THE next time Andy Burnham shares a pint and pork scratchings with his Chancellor for the cameras perhaps they could find time to discuss defence spending?

While the PM refuses to commit to a proper programme of re-arming, US intelligence believes Putin could attack a Nato country within weeks.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Pentagon fears Moscow wants to test Nato’s strength with a possible raid on Poland.

Brits cannot afford, should Putin test Burnham’s resolve, for him to be found wanting.

News.title: Brave, witty, populist and mischievous… Rod Liddle was a rebel genius who could reduce someone to rubble in 15 words
News.content:
SCOTLAND were a man down and losing 4-0 to Germany when my phone pinged, inside Munich’s Allianz Arena, and a legend appeared.

“Rod Liddle.”

Probably not the exact person I wanted to hear from at that moment, but I read the message anyway and started laughing.



“Mate, I still believe in you. I STILL BELIEVE.”

I started chuckling so much, in fact, that a fellow Scotland supporter demanded to know what was so funny.



So I showed him the message and he started laughing as well.

Rod had that effect on people.

He was a Zen master at flagging up human folly, whether it was cultural, ­political, economic or spending £770 to watch your beloved football team get spanked 5-1 at the 2024 Euros.

Thanks to our burgeoning friendship, I also knew very well, by that point, there was no malice to Rod’s words or any higher purpose than comedy when he ­subsequently told Spectator readers he was “devastated” to discover a DNA test had shown he was nearly 70 per cent Scottish.

The only consolation, for Rod, apparently being that: “Henceforth I shall expect everybody else in England to subsidise me through their taxes while simultaneously demanding total independence from them.”

I was so confident of his goodwill, in fact, I took some of my Tartan Army mates to meet Rod at one of the curry nights we held regularly with his great friend and fellow journalist Mick Hume, from online website Spiked.

It was a riotous success built, I’d like to think, on some form of mutual respect. And a lot of alcohol.



Rod admired us because we’d just been to Kazakhstan to see Scotland lose 3-0, which appealed to the Millwall-supporting masochist in the man.

And we all really liked Rod because he was funny, kind, fascinating and much gentler than anyone expected, with a ­generous Christian spirit and a surprising number of insecurities about his ­astonishing talents.

He’d no need to have concerns, of course. Once free of the BBC straitjacket and able to write what he actually thought about the self-righteous liberal London Left, Rod very quickly established himself, at The Sunday Times, Spectator and The Sun, as one of the greatest and most ­versatile columnists who’s ever lived.



He was alarmingly prolific as well and (full disclosure) I was slightly unnerved when he told me, not long after lockdown lifted, that he was going to become The Sunday Times’ TV critic.

I’ve seen them come and go, of course and know that it takes most TV critics about two years just to stop being awful. Not Rod.

A natural God-given talent, like his ­predecessor, AA Gill, meant he was ­brilliant immediately.

His gift lay also in the fact Rod had barely an ounce of pretension about him and no qualms about being populist.

Indeed, when he was put on the spot, he listed his two favourite TV programmes of all time as Fawlty Towers and David Lammy’s epic failure on Celebrity Mastermind, where he identified “Marie Antoinette” as “The Polish woman who discovered radium” and “Henry VII” as Henry VIII’s successor.



He referenced it endlessly, in columns as well. And, like anything Rod wrote at length, it had to be read at least twice, just so you could savour the full savagery.

The true mark of Rod’s genius, though, which set him apart from everyone else, I think, was the fact he could reduce ­someone to rubble in less than 15 words.

It’s become part of Spectator folklore that Rod broke the magazine’s online ­traffic records with a single mischievous question: “I hear Owen Jones was on Question Time, last night. Was he any good . . . ?”



He also once reviewed a Justin Bieber album with the verdict: “The rancid meanderings of a long spent w**kpuffin.”

My own favourite, however, was the three-word description he attached to environmentalist Greta Thunberg.

“Swedish doom goblin.”

It’s so perfect my friends use “Swedish doom goblin” as a short-cut to laughter if a night in the pub ever feels like it’s flagging.

The trouble with devotion to a columnist as talented and addictive as Rod, though, is it’s never good news when they’re absent for a long period.



Rod was missing before I went to this year’s World Cup and worryingly, still hadn’t reappeared by the time I returned. Then came the worst news of all.

There is, ­naturally, some comfort to be had from the outpouring of love displayed by ­readers of The Sun, The Spectator and The Sunday Times in response to Rod’s death, earlier this week.

He would also, I think, have been beside himself with glee at the holier-than-thou obituaries delivered, in self-consciously disapproving style, by a pair of Guardian hacks.

Empty words which, apart from probably confirming all of his darkest thoughts about humourless left-wing ­journalists, said nothing about the great man other than the fact his glorious anti-woke prose will live free of charge, inside their heads, from now until kingdom come.

His death, though, has left an unimaginable chasm in the lives of his friends and family, who are in all our thoughts, and an endless void in the media where, in normal circumstances, I’d have been craving to read his thoughts on the DEI plagiarism scandal that’s engulfed ­Professor Jason Arday and Cambridge University this week.



On a personal level, there’s also eternal regret that I didn’t see my mate before he passed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Although I did receive a message from Mick Hume that Rod wanted me to know he had been greatly cheered by Scotland’s abject performance at the World Cup.

It made me laugh, of course. But I still believe, Rod. I STILL BELIEVE.

News.title: Smugglers could ‘rapidly’ change tactics and undo migrant crackdown gains, warns new border chief
News.content:
CRIMINAL gangs could rapidly change tactics and wipe out progress on cutting small boat crossings, the Government has admitted.

Crossings are down 43 per cent year on year because of a crackdown on dinghies reaching beaches and increased enforcement on smugglers running the routes.



But the new Border Security Commander Duncan Capps, a former Army officer, has admitted in his first annual report that the progress is “not definitive”.

Despite the dip in crossings, the number of migrants in northern France ready and waiting for a chance to come to the UK has not changed.



Maj Gen Capps wrote: “Recent numbers are positive.

“But this could change rapidly.

“Particularly given the likelihood that organised criminal gangs will adapt their tactics and seek to drive renewed flows.

“Especially over the summer months when conditions are more favourable.

“We have steadily forced organised crime groups into a less advantageous position.

“But we should be prepared for them to innovate to protect their profits.”



So far this year 14,561 people have crossed the Channel in small boats.

A Home Office source insisted that new policies were “beginning to bear fruit” but “we are not complacent”.

News.title: Burnham ‘weighs U-turn on releasing PC Harper’s killers’ after devastated widow slammed PM over planned early release
News.content:
ANDY Burnham is considering a dramatic U-turn by blocking the release of PC Andrew Harper’s killers, it emerged last night.

The PM is preparing to “explore every option” to keep Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers in prison despite previously saying he was powerless to stop their release, a government source said.



Downing Street has been approached for comment following reports of the move.

Ministers plan to release 5,000 offenders from prison starting in October as part of plans to reduce jail overcrowding.



The decision to allow them to be eligible for release has sparked public outcry with nearly 700,000 people signing a petition against the move.

A final decision has yet to be made but Whitehall officials are looking at a special exemption for the pair who killed the hero cop, The Telegraph reported last night.

A targeted exemption was previously thought to be unlawful.

Another option would be to free up prison places so when the two men are due to be released – expected in January – those convicted of manslaughter would remain in prison.



Possibilities include sending foreign offenders back to their home country or allowing more men to serve in women’s prisons.

The PM expressed his frustration that he could only block the release of those serving time for rape, serious child sex offences and grooming convictions.

He said: “The truth is I wanted to go even further. I know there will be concerns about who will still be released early for other offences.”

Matthew Barber, the Police and Crime Commissioner for Thames Valley, said the possible move was “welcome news”.

This comes after PC Harper’s widow, Lissie Harper, told Mr Burnham: “You should be ashamed.”



She described the planned early release of two of his killers as a “punch in the gut”.

Petition to stop the early release from jail of PC Andrew Harper's killers Aileen O'Connor, Thames Valley Police Federation Chair, has launched a petition demanding a stop to the early release of PC Harper's killers. The petition has already soared past 100,000 signatures after it was posted earlier on Tuesday. Hundreds more have taken to the comments to show their support after the Government’s decision on PC Harper’s killers sparked outrage across the country. O’Connor said in the petition that she was “absolutely outraged” at both the Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, and Justice Secretary. She challenged them to “explain why those responsible for killing a police officer should still be eligible for early release”. The decision, she said, “is an insult to Andrew’s family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family”. O’Connor added they have watched a “justice system that they trusted” fail to recognise the sacrifices made by those who “serve and protect the public”. It sends a “deeply troubling message” about the value the Government places on people who have made those sacrifices, she continued. O’Connor concluded with a defiant message, saying: “I will not stand by while the voices of Andrew’s family, his colleagues and police officers across this country continue to be ignored.” To sign the petition click here.

And she has thrown her weight behind an online Thames Valley Police Federation petition to stop his killers being freed, which more than 400,000 people had signed on Wednesday evening.

PC Harper died while investigating the theft of a £10,000 quad bike near Sulhamstead, Berks, in August 2019.

Bowers and Cole, then 17, tried to escape in a car driven by Henry Long, 18.



The 28-year-old officer’s ankles got caught in a heavy-duty tow strap and he suffered ­catastrophic ­injuries as he was dragged in the dark for more than a mile at an average 43mph.

Bowers and Cole were sentenced to 13 years in July 2020, meaning they could be released by October.

Long, the main perpetrator, who pleaded guilty, got 16 years and is not eligible for release under the scheme.



Lissie, who had married PC Harper just four weeks before the tragedy, said: “Hopefully we can make the current Government come to their senses and realise we cannot put people like this back on our streets.

“Justice should mean justice and serving the sentence given.

“The Government has punched us in the gut . . . they should be ashamed of themselves.”

Lissie, of Wallingford, Oxfordshire, said: “Please sign our petition . . . we will never give up.”

The detective who led the probe into PC Harper’s death and put his killers behind bars has said he is “appalled” the pair could be freed early.



Ex-Det Supt Stuart Blaik spoke of his fury at plans to release Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole, who showed “no remorse” for their role in the killing.

Speaking on BBC Breakfast, he said: “Neither of them showed any remorse during their time in police custody or during their subsequent trial.

“I hope the Government takes account of the strength of public feeling on this issue, which has been both clear and widespread.

“I just really don’t understand why the Early Release Scheme is being used in these sort of circumstances, it just doesn’t feel right.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mr Blaik, who left the force in 2023, told how the smirking killers showed “no remorse whatsoever” throughout legal proceedings.

News.title: Teen motorbike rider who left boy, 7, scarred for life after crashing into him when he sped through red light faces jail
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

E-BIKE YOB Teen motorbike rider who left boy, 7, scarred for life after crashing into him when he sped through red light faces jail

A TEENAGE motorbike rider who left a boy of seven scarred for life when he sped through a red light is facing jail.

Callean Wyburn was riding the electric vehicle at between 20mph and 30mph with dodgy brakes when he ploughed into the lad.

The boy, who can’t be named, was knocked off his scooter on a pelican crossing in front of his mum in June last year.

A court heard he suffered a cut to his cheek, which has left a permanent scar.





His jaw was fractured and he lost a tooth.

His mum said: “I carry a huge amount of guilt.

“I told him it was safe to cross.”

Wyburn, 17 at the time, and two pals fled in Christchurch, Dorset.

He handed himself in to police the following day.

In May, he admitted causing serious injury by dangerous driving and was due to be sentenced on Friday.

But Poole magistrates decided a custodial sentence of 12 months was “appropriate” and sent the case to crown court in October.

In a letter, business student Wyburn said his actions were “completely stupid and unforgivable” and apologised to the boy and his family.

News.title: Will Andy Burnham’s decisions be any better if he’s holed up in No10 North? No. What a fabulous waste of taxpayers’ cash
News.content:
ANDY BURNHAM was only in power for two weeks before he went on holiday and, obviously, that wasn’t long enough to explain in any great detail what he plans to do.

So far, all he’s told us is that he likes football and beer and that he intends to set up a new power base in Manchester which will be called Number 10 North.





Hmmm. I wonder if that’s a good idea. Obviously it will cost many lumps of our money to ­create this ecky thump outpost, and even more will have to be spent on train fares every day shipping people to and from ­London.

And to what end? Will decisions taken in the North be different to those taken in the South? Will they be better?

To answer that, it’s sensible to look at what happened when the BBC did a similar thing 15 years ago. Back in 2011, they announced that a huge number of their radio and TV shows would now be made in Salford.

But the man put in charge of encouraging staff to relocate decided that he himself would be staying in London.

They were very diligent about the decision, though. When I pitched the idea of doing a farming show to a BBC commissioner way back when, he only had one question about it: “Where would it be produced?” I told him London, and he said: “Well, we don’t want it then.”

It’s still going on today. There was an awful brouhaha recently when it emerged that for two days every week Naga Munchetty would be hosting her Salford-based 5 Live morning show from . . . London.

But do you care about that? I’m not sure I do.

All I can say for sure is that I bet the guests on her show will be quietly thrilled that they don’t have to drag themselves to Euston Station at crikey o’clock in the morning.





Who Wants To Be A Millionaire? is made in Salford. And do you think the people of the North West are proud of that? Do they even know?

We all know what’s going on here. Big political operations like the Government and the BBC think that if they have some offices in Manchester, people in the North will feel included.

But I’m from Yorkshire so actually, I have a deep distrust of anything made on the drizzly side of the Pennines.

Let’s not forget that until TVR came along, the only car made in Lancashire only had three wheels.

Number 10 North then might please the people of Manchester, but it will annoy people in Leeds and Newcastle and Norwich and everywhere that isn’t Manchester. It certainly annoys me because here we are in a country that doesn’t have enough money to mend its potholes or keep convicted murderers in jail.

But somehow there is enough cash to build a swish new palace up North.

Where was this decision taken? I don’t know and it doesn’t matter.

I’ve made some of the best decisions of my life while ­sitting on the lavatory.

And some of the worst while lying in the sunshine by an Italian swimming pool.

The Government has its headquarters.



It doesn’t need another one.

STELLA JOB ON ADVERT

I AM not ordinarily given to singing the praises of a rival brewer but credit where credit’s due: This week Stella Artois took out a full-page newspaper advert – in The Times no less – to tell everyone that beer is great.

It pointed out that when someone says “let’s grab a beer” it means so much more than drinking a cold one.

They argued, quite rightly, that it’s an invitation to talk, to celebrate, to reconnect.

Or maybe have a moan about your boss.

And they went on to say that all this magnificence comes from just four simple ingredients. Hops. Barley. Yeast. And water.

They concluded by saying “here’s to a future with more”.

But that’s going to be a problem, I’m afraid, because thanks to the Government’s weird hatred of anyone with a field, British farmers planted a lot less barley than usual this year.

And thanks to the heatwaves and drought, up to two-thirds of it is not good enough to be malted.



It’s nothing more than hen food.

FLIES? MUCH MORE SCARY THINGS COME OUT OF SKY

FEW things in life are as irritating as a persistent fly.

I can hear one now, pointlessly whizzing about and crashing into the windows, and I just know it won’t be long before it decides to have a look in my ear.

This summer, there’s an absolute plague of the damn things.

Doubtless global warming is to blame. Or Donald Trump. But whatever, I’ve been very busy with the sprays and my electric table tennis bat that nukes them.

What else can you do?

Well, it seems that the answer to that is “moan”.

In Congleton, a town in Cheshire, one woman has started a petition, calling on the council to take some kind of action.

She says the toll the flies place on her daily life is “tremendous”. Diddums.



One of her neighbours says: “Imagine never being able to open your doors or windows.”

What??!!? It’s Congleton, love, not Bhopal.

Others, meanwhile, say that children cannot play outside and one is actually selling her house and moving because there are too many flies in it.

Where’s she moving to? I hope it’s Australia.

Then she’d learn what a real swarm feels like.

What the bloody hell has happened to this country? They’re flies, for God’s sake not German bombers.

Yes, the noise they make is annoying but it’s nowhere near as annoying as the noise made by people who go all to pieces at every little thing.

HOW TO FRY MY BRAIN

IT’S not often I’m stopped dead in my tracks by a fact, but while listening to the extremely excellent Professor Hannah Fry on her science podcast this week, I discovered that the lithium-ion batteries in your electric car are basically useless.

Hannah explained that firewood produces quite a lot of energy, around 16 megajoules per kilogram.



Olive oil is even better. You get 37 from that and 39 from your belly fat.

Petrol is pretty much the king though, churning out a whopping 47.

Whereas the amount of megajoules per kg you get from the lithium-ion batteries in your beloved Tesla is – wait for it – less than one.

I’m surprised the damn thing has enough energy to even start in a morning.

I’VE missed Rod Liddle’s column these past few weeks and now I shall have to get used to missing them for ever. It won’t be easy. RIP Rod.

News.title: Bristol Airport closed live: Mass cancellations as runway shut for hours
News.content:
Passengers have had their travel plans wrecked after Bristol Airport closed

Bristol Airport is closed due to emergency runway repairs, with departures cancelled and inbound flights diverted

All flights to and from Bristol Airport have been cancelled this evening, throwing weekend travel plans into chaos.

Bristol Airport said it has suspended operations until 6am tomorrow in order to repair a "defect" on the runway.

"We apologise for any inconvenience. Safety is always our number one priority," the airport said. "Customers should refer to their airlines with any flight queries."

A number of inbound flights have been diverted to London, Birmingham and Cardiff. Passengers have reported chaos at the airport, with some saying the "tannoy system" has also gone down.

News.title: Drought-hit UK's sixth heatwave in just three months starts with scorching 36C highs
News.content:
Drought-hit UK's sixth heatwave in just three months starts with scorching 36C highs

Met Office weather forecasters have bad news for anyone hoping for cooler temperatures with yet another heatwave is on the way in the coming days and this one will stick around

View 4 Images Brits are bracing for a sixth heatwave inside three months (Image: ANDY RAIN/EPA/Shutterstock)

The sixth heatwave of the summer already is just days away as some area's wait for a drop of rain passes the seven-week point.

‌



Drought-hit Brits are set for more sweltering conditions after relentless record-breaking temperatures and what feels like no respite at all, with wildfires raging and hosepipe bans in place. Fresh Atlantic air has brought a cooler climate in recent days, but that will soon come to an abrupt halt.

‌



The UK Health Security Agency has issued yellow heat health alerts across the south of England and Midlands from tomorrow until Tuesday, as experts warn there is a good chance they could be extended. Thursday was the first time in 36 days that nowhere in the country had been in a heatwave - but things are about to warm up again.

‌



View 4 Images The UK Health Security Agency's latest yellow heat health alerts (Image: UK Health Security Agency)

South West Water announces strict hosepipe ban for millions across five areas READ MORE :

Should the government introduce water rationing? Take our poll and have your say READ MORE :

Another baking period is expected to begin on Sunday, hitting a scorching 37C by next week. Netweather maps forecasted temperatures will start to climb this weekend, soaring above 30C - and that's not the only bit of bad news for those who have had enough on the heat - the hot conditions are expected to stay for six days.

It will only get warmer as the week goes on, too. WXCharts maps show highs of 34C in areas of the south on Wednesday, August 12. Its weather maps turn red in the south and east of England, as well as areas of Wales.

‌



Temperatures above 30C stretch from Sussex up to Lincolnshire, with temperatures in the high 20s stretching to areas like Yorkshire and Devon. Meanwhile, the Met Office says that mixed weather conditions are expected for the period between Monday, August 10 and Wednesday, August 19.

View 4 Images Drought has been declared across large parts of England and the whole of Wales (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

It predicts a "relatively settled start to the period, with mainly dry conditions on Monday, although with scattered showers across northern areas".

‌



"Then through the following week, more changeable conditions are likely across northwestern parts, with some spells of rain and stronger winds interspersed by drier periods," the forecast adds. "Whilst southeastern areas will generally see more settled and drier conditions. Further into August, lower pressure may start to track further south or east.

"This means there is a greater chance of frontal systems or thundery interludes to affect southern and eastern areas in comparison to recent weeks, though rainfall amounts could be quite variable, with some areas still seeing relatively little. For the most part, temperatures look to remain above average, especially in the south, and perhaps turning very warm or hot."

View 4 Images It's about to heat up from Sunday, Met Office maps show (Image: Met Office)

‌



Half of England is currently under official drought conditions after some areas recorded almost no rainfall in the entire month of July.

In May and June, temperature records were broken during spells of scorching weather, and Brits regularly faced days of 30C or more. Meanwhile, the Met Office has described July as a 'historic' month in terms of dryness, sunshine, and exceptional warmth.

Met Office meteorologist Aidan McGovern said in a forecast bulletin: "It's not good news - we really need the rain... You obviously need soil moisture for those plants to continue to thrive and we are seriously lacking in soil moisture across a large part of England and Wales.

Article continues below

"I've just picked a point there, but it's representative of a large area of England or Wales, 1% soil moisture in that top 40 centimetres, less than 30% supposedly over a long period time. It really isn't good news for plants and all sorts of wildlife that need plant life and so on."

News.title: Donald Trump really doesn't want to tell the BBC his bank balance
News.content:
Donald Trump really doesn't want to tell the BBC his bank balance

In this week's US Dispatch newsletter, find out why Donald Trump doesn't want to tell the BBC his bank balance, what Ed Miliband got up to in Washington this week, and why the President has gone all the way to Vegas

View Image Trump filed an emergency motion to stop the beeb getting a look inside his bank accounts (Image: Getty Images)

This week Trump's lawyers filed an emergency motion to change his ridiculous lawsuit against the BBC.

‌



Quick recap: Trump is suing Auntie Beeb over an episode of Panorama that aired during the 2024 campaign, in which they edited a few sentences from his January 6th speech together. The BBC have apologised for the edit, which they say didn't meet their standards and might lead people to think the sentences were said one after the other, which they weren't. Crucially, though, they haven't admitted that it might wrongly lead a viewer to think Trump was encouraging his supporters to march on the capitol building and try to prevent the lawful certification of his election loss to Joe Biden. They can't admit to that. Because that's exactly what he was doing. Countless legal bodies - courts, committees and congress - all reached that conclusion. It's not at all controversial.

‌



But Trump decided to sue the BBC for $10 billion, a truly Dr Evil amount of money, claiming his "brand, properties and businesses" had been damaged by the programme... which was not broadcast in the United States.

‌



"Well," the BBC's lawyers said (I'm paraphrasing here), "if you're saying it caused you financial damage, we'll be taking a look at your financial records." And during the phase of the lawsuit known as "discovery", Trump was told he had to hand over information about the financial performance of hundreds of his companies.

Trump did not like this turn of events one little bit. So on Wednesday his lawyers submitted an emergency motion to change the lawsuit.

The proposed new complaint is still under wraps for now, but Trump's lawyer Alejandro Brito has said it "focuses on President Trump's damages allegations on the reputational harm that he has suffered, which is at the core of this defamation action" and on "personal reputational harm as the primary compensatory injury."

‌



And the Judge let him off the hook, agreeing on Thursday afternoon that he can re-word his complaint and keep his financial performance under wraps. But hey, it was worth a shot.

You can get more stories, analysis and gossip like this straight to your inbox by signing up to The U.S. Dispatch with Mikey Smith newsletter, exclusively available to Mirror+ subscribers.

Click here to subscribe to Mirror+ now As a Mirror + subscriber, you’ll have:

‌



Unlimited access to the Mirror's app

Cleaner, faster reading online with fewer adverts

Access to exclusive newsletters only for subscribers

These will include unique insight from our writers alongside thought-provoking opinion

Exclusive in-depth features and unmissable columnists for Mirror+ members

Click here to subscribe to Mirror+ now

Ed Miliband's first trip to Washington could have gone worse.

Ed Miliband, the newly minted Foreign Secretary, sensibly ignored shouted questions from reporters on whether he still thought Donald Trump was a "an idiot, a racist and a misogynist" on his way to meet Secretary of State Marco Rubio. He wouldn't want have to lie on camera in front of his host, that simply wouldn't do.

‌



Afterward, the readouts of the meeting from the two sides were different in exactly the ways you'd expect. The 90-minute meeting was productive and warm, our side said. They talked about the special relationship and NATO, Ukraine and the Strait of Hormuz, just as you'd expect.

The US State Department's note of their chat was a little more curt, and had different highlights - particularly urging us to spend more on defence, a frequent bugbear of the President and a thorny subject for Andy Burnham. Spokesperson Tommy Pigot said: "The two discussed the importance of Europe taking on a greater role in its own security."

We understand Ed also met with top members of the Senate Foreign Relations committee while he was in town. I deeply hope he also had time to try a half-smoke from Ben's Chilli Bowl and had a cocktail in Off The Record, as all visitors to DC should.

‌



Tone Deaf in Vegas

Trump gave a speech in Las Vegas the other night. And that location alone tells you a lot.

It's the third time he's been back to Vegas since his second inauguration - and the second since April. So is he secretly slipping out and hitting the slots? Nah, it's just the only place his economic message is landing. Well, one bit of it. Maybe.

It's kind of understandable that people in Las Vegas like his "no tax on tips" policy. Vegas has such a big hospitality industry that there's a third rush hour at about midnight, because that's when casino shift changes tend to be. The other thing Vegas has a lot of, which Trump doesn't seem so keen to talk about is undocumented workers. If Trump carried out his promise of mass deportations in Sin City, it would most likely sink into the desert.

Article continues below

Anyway, if Trump's going to Vegas for the second time in four months, it means someone in his team has decided to try and get him on message again. Their third shot at a reboot as the Republican Party stares down a severe drubbing in November's midterm elections. All he needs to do is get up on that stage, say "NO TAX ON TIPS" and then shut up.

Of course he didn't. He said "NO TAX ON TIPS" a few times, then it was all "the communists are coming" and "I want to fire the Supreme Court", and "the radical left want to ban gasoline". And that's why he has a 38% approval rating.

News.title: 'Gunman' bursts into US hospital sparking lockdown and huge police response
News.content:
'Gunman' bursts into US hospital sparking lockdown and huge police response

The lone male suspect remains contained inside the emergency department at Bonney Lake Hospital, near Seattle, authorities have said

View 2 Images Armed police officers rushed to the scene at Bonney Lake Hospital (Image: Komo News)

A man has walked into the emergency department at a US hospital then claimed to be armed and issued threats, triggering a hospital lockdown and a massive police response.

‌



The incident at MultiCare Bonney Lake Hospital began to unfold at around 9:20 am local time (5.20pm UK time) when the man entered the emergency room and made the threats, Bonney Lake Police Chief Mark Berry said.

‌



The hospital was immediately placed on lockdown with Bonney Lake police officers and Pierce County Sheriff's Office deputies rushing to the scene. Patients were evacuated from the building, Berry said.

‌



The lone male suspect remains contained within the emergency department, authorities have said. SWAT officers and crisis negotiators are at the scene and are actively in talks with the man. Berry said there is no threat to the public outside the immediate vicinity and that authorities are hopeful for a peaceful resolution.

View 2 Images SWAT negotiators are at the scene (Image: Komo News)

‌



Man fights for life after plunging from Majorca flats onto pair drinking at bar READ MORE :

In an official statement, MultiCare confirmed that all staff and patients are safe and that no injuries have been reported.

It said: "We are currently responding to a security incident in the MultiCare Bonney Lake Emergency Department. All staff and patients are safe, and there are no reported injuries," the statement read. "Bonney Lake Police are on site and working with a negotiator. The safety and well-being of our patients, staff, and community remain our highest priorities. We are closely coordinating with law enforcement and will share additional information when available."

The hospital confirmed that the Bonney Lake Emergency Department has been closed and is not accepting patients.

Article continues below

Authorities have yet to release further details regarding the suspect or a possible motive. Negotiations were still ongoing on Friday.

News.title: Man fights for life after plunging from Majorca flats onto pair drinking at bar
News.content:
Man fights for life after plunging from Majorca flats onto pair drinking at bar

The man fell from a 12-storey building near Palma's Barcelona Square before reportedly hitting a tree then two other people

View 2 Images A man is fighting for his life after a horror fall in Majorca (stock image) (Image: MDM)

A man is fighting for his life after plunging from a Majorca apartment block and landing on two people he left seriously injured.

‌



The pair he hit as he reached the ground were sat at a bar terrace in the island's capital Palma having a drink.

‌



The drama happened just before 4pm this afternoon below a 12-storey building near the city's Barcelona Square.

‌



Unconfirmed local reports said the man had rowed with his partner shortly before the horror incident. He reportedly collided with a tree near the ground which slightly cushioned his fall before landing onto a table where the men at ground-level were sitting.

View 2 Images The injured were taken to the Son Espases University Hospital in Palma (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Brit pensioner gored by bull and rushed to hospital after taking part in San Fermin festival READ MORE :

A witness said: "He fell onto the table but he seems to have hit one of them almost full-on, who ended up laid out on the floor and appeared to be in very serious condition."

Police and ambulances raced to the scene and paramedics performed life-saving CPR on the man who had plunged from the apartment block before taking him to hospital.

Cops escorted the ambulance rushing him to Son Espases Hospital in Palma so they could help clear traffic along the way and make sure he got there as soon as possible.

Article continues below

Another local, describing the scene, said: "The table was broken and the chairs crushed, I saw how they were resuscitating the man who landed on the other two. He was on the floor and four paramedics were trying to revive him. It was very intense."

The nationalities of the three men has not yet been made public.

News.title: Fresh UFO files released by Trump show '500ft triangle that swooped over US base'
News.content:
Fresh UFO files released by Trump show '500ft triangle that swooped over US base'

Fresh UFO files have revealed a military pilot's bizarre account of a 500ft triangular object that is said to have 'silently' hovered over Bagram Airfield in north-east Afghanistan

View 4 Images A new batch of UFO files was released on Friday (Image: US DEPARTMENT OF WAR)

Fresh UFO files released by the Trump administration have revealed a military pilot's account of a bizarre 500ft triangular object that he said swooped over a US base in Afghanistan.

‌



The new batch of documents, images and videos related to UFOs - officially known as unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) - were released on the US Department of Defence's UFO website on Friday.

‌



The files mark the fifth release under an executive order signed by President Donald Trump in January, directing the military and other agencies to release more records relating to UFOs.

‌



Among the documents is a notable FBI report detailing a 2024 interview with a former military pilot, who described seeing a mysterious object while serving in Afghanistan in 2002.

View 4 Images An FBI rendering of the object the military pilot recounted seeing (Image: US DEPARTMENT OF WAR)

The pilot said he saw the large object moving "silently" over Bagram Airfield in north-east Afghanistan - once the largest US military base in the country - at a consistent speed of around 173mph.

‌



"At approximately 4:30 AM local time, [redacted] noticed that the stars were getting blacked out over Bagram. It appeared as if something huge went overhead, from west to east, and was an equilateral triangle shape. The object was moving silently, at a consistent speed and altitude, possibly 150 knots, with no lights visible," an FBI agent wrote in the report.

The pilot "estimated it was 500 feet in size, but he could not fully see the shape of the object", according to the report. He claimed that the pilot he was with "also observed the triangle, and when it passed over stated, 'did you see that?'" The FBI produced an artist's rendering of the object described by the pilot.

In the same report, the pilot told the FBI agent he saw strange lights in the sky during a flight from Massachusetts to Ireland in October 2023.

‌



View 4 Images Royal Marines from 45 Commando RM pictured at Bagram Airfield in April 2002 (Image: Daily Mirror)

"[Redacted] was at an elevation of 37,000 feet and believed the lights were higher than him, probably at 50,000 feet or higher. The lights were white in color, would start out as dim, and get brighter before they eventually faded out," the report stated. "The full cycle of the lights would range from 10 seconds to one minute." The pilot said he saw the lights around 10 times after that first experience.

Another document summarises a Brazilian radio broadcast from Rio de Janeiro claiming that a "large metal sphere" crashed into the town of Conde, Bahia, in November 1963, "gouging a hole four meters deep".

‌



The declassified US Foreign Broadcast Information Service (FBIS) document stated: "The mysterious sphere has window shaped openings covered with thick glass. Inside is a human body dressed in heavy clothing bearing inscriptions which cannot be deciphered. The population of Conde is intrigued, and the authorities have been informed."

View 4 Images One document says a 'large metal sphere' crashed into the town of Conde in Bahia, north-east Brazil, in 1963 (Image: US Department of War)

Following the latest disclosure, the Pentagon said the department would "release additional files on a rolling basis".

Article continues below

Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Friday: "The Department of War is in lockstep with President Trump to bring unprecedented transparency regarding our government’s understanding of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena.

"These files, hidden behind classifications, have long fueled justified speculation, and it’s time the American people see it for themselves. This release of declassified documents demonstrates the Trump Administration’s earnest commitment to unprecedented transparency."

News.title: Murderer caught on pet cam brutally killing sister's boyfriend in row over dogs
News.content:
Murderer caught on pet cam brutally killing sister's boyfriend in row over dogs

Anthony Junior Murray used a combat knife to attack Joe Burton on New Year's Eve at the killer's flat in Bury, Greater Manchester

View 3 Images Anthony Junior Murray stabbed Joe Burton with a combat knife (Image: GMP)

A murderer who plunged a knife into the back of his sister's boyfriend after a row over a dog was caught in the act on a pet camera.

‌



Anthony Junior Murray, 25, stabbed Joe Burton, 23, with a combat knife on New Year's Eve then told police he was "not aware of the happenings" in an attempt to cover his crimes. But he was caught out when it emerged the attack had been filmed by a camera installed in his flat.

‌



The incident took place at 11.49pm on December 31 last year at a flat on Tarn Drive in Bury, Greater Manchester. Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Murray's sister, Kayleigh, had been in an on-off relationship with Mr Burton but this was "sadly blighted by alcohol abuse on both sides", prosecutor Rob Hall told Murray's trial.

‌



Although the pair had a child together in 2024, their "issues with alcohol continued". Murray invited his sister to the flat, who arrived with Mr Burton.

View 3 Images Joe Burton was stabbed in the back (Image: MEN Media)

Mr Hall told the trial, which concluded last month: "On the evening of New Year's Eve 2025, a time that should have been about socialising and welcoming in 2026, in a first floor flat in Bury, this defendant, Anthony Junior Murray, 25, lost his temper and stabbed Joe Burton, 23, the boyfriend of the defendant’s sister, to death.

‌



"He did that with a combat knife that he owned. The one stab wound that was inflicted with that knife was to Joe Burton’s left upper back area. The stab wound penetrated to a depth of approximately 18cm, which is almost to the full extent of the blade of that knife."

Manchester Evening News reports that Murray lived alone in his flat with his two dogs called Zarla and Beau Beau. He installed a camera in the flat to monitor the pets.

On New Year's Eve, Kayleigh is understood to have been "particularly intoxicated" and "appeared to be struggling to stand," the court heard. After the four let off some fireworks, "tensions started to rise".

‌



Mr Hall told the court: "There are a number of things in the mix by this stage, intoxication, lateness of the hour, the state of Kayleigh Murray and the tensions between the Murray family and Joe Burton." Before the stabbing, Murray and Mr Burton had been fighting over the dogs.

Mr Burton said: "F*** off dog, doing my head in." Later he said: "Shut up Beau I’ve had enough of you." Murray said: "What do you want me to do, put my dogs in a cage for you?"

"No I don’t," Mr Burton replied. "What do you want me to do, you f****** idiot," Murray replied. He continued: "Get the f*** out of my house kn******, why should I have to cage my dogs because of you?"

‌



He continued: "I don’t give a f***, I never trusted you from day one. I never trusted you. Why is Kayleigh like that? It has always been about you." Murray told Mr Burton "I’ll slit your f****** throat".

Mr Burton said: "I haven’t done anything wrong Anthony." A "struggle followed, after which Murray stabbed Mr Burton once to the back.

View 3 Images Police at the scene of the stabbing on Tarn Drive in Bury (Image: MEN Media)

‌



His reaction was "Not to help Joe Burton or call 999" but to call his family instead, being "selective" in telling his father, Anthony Senior, and his siblings about what he had done. The selective story telling then turned into a series of lies once officers arrived to the scene, the court heard.

A call to 999 was made by Kayleigh "out of concern for him [Murray]", with his family then driving to the flat and arriving moments before the police. At 12.07am, Murray claimed that "another person had stabbed" Mr Burton, later saying he had "been out all day" at the Bridge Tavern pub in nearby Radcliffe before coming home to find Mr Burton "bleeding to death".

In a later account, Murray said he didn't know who had been stabbed, claiming it may be to do with issues he had previously had with his downstairs neighbours. Murray was arrested at 12.30am, while Mr Burton was pronounced dead at 12.43am.

‌



In a written statement the next day, Murray accepted he had present at the flat and that a "fight" had started between Mr Burton and a man he didn't wish to name. He claimed he tried to intervene but left the flat, finding Mr Burton injured upon his return.

In a second statement, he accepted that the knife used in the stabbing belonged to him. Mr Hall told the court the attack was captured on the dog camera in a "remarkable stroke of luck".

When he was played the footage in a police interview, Murray said: "I cannot give an account of what went on in the footage or what I was thinking at the time as I blanked this out and I am not aware of the happenings." He said his previous statements represented his memory of what happened that night.

‌



During the trial, Murray, of Tarn Drive, Bury, claimed he acted in self-defence and didn't mean to stab Mr Burton. Today, he was ordered to serve a minimum of 18 years behind bars before he can be considered for parole.

Sentencing, Judge Maurice Greene told Murray: "It is not my task to put a value on Joe Burton’s life because no sentence can do that. Criminal law can not restore him to his family. But the court must recognise the seriousness of the harm caused, and I do."

Mr Hall said: "The Crown says that Mr Murray’s actions and the lies after the stabbing are the clearest evidence that he knew only too well what he had done and the seriousness of the consequences for him if that was discovered." Jurors found Murray guilty of murder by a majority of 11 to one after eight hours of deliberations.

Article continues below

Defending, Bernard Richmond KC paid tribute to the "quiet dignity" displayed by Mr Burton’s family during the case. Mr Richmond said that Murray recognised that the "life sentence he knows you are going to pass is not just a life sentence on him, but a life sentence on all of those who have been affected by this".

He said that the single blow inflicted by Murray was "horrific", but pointed out it was one blow and was not a more sustained attack. Mr Richmond said Murray’s lies "do him no credit" but that "none of them stand scrutiny at all".

News.title: Blue Flag beach sewage crisis as HUNDREDS of tourists fall sick at some of UK's best beaches
News.content:
Blue Flag beach sewage crisis as HUNDREDS of tourists fall sick at some of UK's best beaches

EXCLUSIVE: New figures from Surfers Against Sewage revealed hundreds of people started feeling unwell after visiting Blue Flag UK beaches that have officially been rated the best in the country

View 6 Images Blue Flag beaches across the country have seen reports of sickness in 2026 (Image: PA)

Dozens of people have fallen ill at award-winning British Blue Flag beaches, new figures revealed, despite water quality being rated "excellent" by the Environment Agency and Natural Resources Wales this year.

‌



Marine conservation charity Surfers Against Sewage (SAS) received more than 700 reports of sickness across 406 areas, including some of the most picturesque beaches in the UK - among them beaches favoured by celebrities and former Prime Ministers. Many of them have been given top status as a Blue Flag location, meaning they have the highest water quality, minimal waste, good biodiversity, and are safe and accessible.

‌



But data reveals that some of them may also contain harmful pathogens, with visitors reporting falling unwell with gastrointestinal, ear, nose and throat, viral, respiratory and skin conditions.

‌



View 6 Images Croyde Bay had the most reports of any one beach in England (Image: Keep Britain Tidy / SWNS.com)

SAS revealed to the Mirror that it received 765 sickness reports across 406 locations in the UK in 2026 so far, with nearly half - 322 - coming in the months since May 1, as people flocked to the coast in the extreme heat. The majority of those reports came from Bournemouth, where 16 people said they fell unwell after visiting the coast.

Another 13 came from Croyde Bay in Croyde, North Devon, with Polzeath, the stunning stretch of sand in North Cornwall and the favourite of former PM David Cameron, coming third on the list.

‌



Cameron bought a £2million home near the beach, which he has been frequently pictured enjoying alongside his wife Samantha, in 2017. Polzeath was also one of the beaches where royals like Princes William and Harry grew up surfing, and other celebrities, including Coldplay frontman Chris Martin and renowned UK super chef Gordon Ramsay have made their homes there.

View 6 Images David and Samantha Cameron are fans of Polzeath (Image: PA)

But 13 people have reported feeling unwell after a trip to the beach this year so far, according to the SAS figures, and before visits reached their height in the middle of the summer holidays.

‌



Polzeath is followed by Rest Bay, in Porthcawl, in Bridgend, Wales, where 12 people said they were unwell after a visit to the beach. In Exmouth, the port town south of Exeter in Devon, another 10 people said they fell ill, with nine submitting reports in Portreath, another picturesque town on the north Cornwall coast.

Eight people said they were unwell after visiting Saunton Sands, a UNESCO-protected biosphere in North Devon's Braunton Burrows, Swanage Central in Dorset and Ogmore by Sea in Barry, Wales. Seven were recorded in Woolacombe Village, also in North Devon.

The hundreds of additional cases and their locations can be seen on the map below:

‌



The majority of those areas and beaches included in the top 10 SAS figures - six - are either areas with beaches that have been given Blue Flag awards, or beaches that have previously won the prize. For instance, in Bournemouth, from where 13 sickness reports were submitted, three came from Durley Chine beach, which won the prize in 2026.

The ones in the top 10 that didn't win the prize this year, Portreath, Saunton Sands and Woolacombe Village, were still in sparkling condition, according to the Environment Agency. Each of the trio were rated as having "excellent" quality of water in its latest ratings, which were handed down in 2025.

‌



The outlier among the group was Ogmore-by-Sea in Barry, which according to Natural Resources Wales, had "failed to meet water quality standards in the past few years".

Bathing quality ratings across the UK can be seen on the map below:

‌



While the service said it was not sure why water quality has consistently dipped in the area, it said storm overflows and drainage, ageing infrastructure, road and urban pollution, misconnected pipes and farmland pollution could play a role. There is no indication what could be behind sickness at the Blue Flag locations, but sewage dumping by water companies, the SAS says, is "making us sick".

Jo Morley, Head of Campaigns at SAS said in a statement to the Mirror: "Sewage dumping by water companies is making us sick. It has been for decades.

"Thousands of water users are reporting this to us, and this is likely just the tip of the iceberg. From gastroenteritis and ear infections, to weeks off work and hospitalisations. This is a public health crisis. We know that sewage is pouring into our waters, even during this summer's exceptionally dry weather, and it's totally unacceptable that people are getting ill in any case, especially after using bathing waters rated as 'excellent.'"

‌



View 6 Images Surfers Against Sewage are campaigning to end water privatisation in the UK (Image: PA)

"Our sickness reports are the only data showing the scale of sickness from sewage. There is no official Government data, and no legal protections for people using the water.

"This is symptomatic of a totally broken system that has put profits first for too long, allowing polluters to cash in in whilst dumping sewage without punishment, and this has to change. We should not have to worry about getting sick before diving in, any time of year, especially the summer.

‌



"If you're heading to the beach or your local swim spot, make sure you check the Safer Seas and Rivers Service for pollution alerts."

View 6 Images Thousands of Brits have flocked to beaches across the country during a record-breaking hot summer (Image: Getty Images)

SAS has received thousands of sickness reports since 2019, when it started recording, with a total of 8,313 in the last seven years. Most of those cases have come from Exmouth, which recorded 203, with Hove recording 140, Polzeath 117, Harlyn Bay 101, Westward Ho! 98, Tankerton 94, Gyllyngvase 85, Shoreham Beach 82, Worthing 78, and Summerleaze, for which 76 were recorded.

‌



SAS has urged Brits to use its Safer Seas and River Service to check for real-time pollution alerts if they head to the coast this summer.

View 6 Images Hundreds of reports came as people tried to cool off for the summer this year, and before the summer holidays (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

The charity hosts the service both on its website and via its own app, via which it tells people to report whether they become unwell after using UK water. The charity has also urged the Government to end privatisation in the water industry, and has championed the Clean Water Act as a path forward for the industry that protects both public health and the environment.

‌



It urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to take control of failing water companies, remove their profit motive and pursue restructuring, starting with Thames Water.

The Mirror has contacted Keep England Clean and Keep Wales Clean, which administer the Blue Flag Awards to beaches in England and Wales. An Environment Agency spokesperson said: "We urge members of the public to follow UKHSA advice on swimming safely and to check Swimfo before visiting any of the country's 464 designated bathing waters.

"There are a range of sources of bacteria in our rivers, lakes and seas. These can include runoff from fields containing farm animals, as well as sewage treatment works and storm overflows, particularly following periods of heavy rainfall. Some bacteria can make people unwell."

‌



"Our waters are also home to a wide variety of wildlife, including birds and other animals, which naturally contribute bacteria to the environment and can affect water quality." A Natural Resources Wales spokesperson said: “We want people to enjoy Wales’ rivers, lakes and coastlines safely this summer.

"We monitor water quality at Wales' designated bathing waters throughout the bathing season, with results published online to help people make informed decisions about where and when to enter the water. Anyone who sees potential pollution should report it directly to us on 03000 65 3000 or online at naturalresources.wales/reportit, so our officers can respond.

“Natural water bodies can contain bacteria and other contaminants from a range of sources that are not always visible and can sometimes cause illness. We investigate reports of suspected pollution affecting rivers, lakes and coastal waters and work with partners, including water companies and local authorities, to establish the cause of incidents.

Article continues below

"Where there is evidence of environmental harm or breaches of environmental legislation, we take appropriate regulatory action. We encourage people to take sensible precautions when using open water, including avoiding swallowing water, washing or sanitising hands before eating, and seeking medical advice if they feel unwell after water activities. You can find advice here: Staying safe in outdoor water in Wales - Public Health Wales”

News.title: Police failings revealed as sex offender left free to murder and attack women
News.content:
His first victim was attacked was on a busy Tube in central London.

Levy boarded and positioned himself directly in front of the woman, before leaning his elbow on her. She moved away.

A few minutes later, she felt something touch her, over her clothes, on her vagina. Such was the force Levy used, that she felt like it was an attempt to push his fingers inside her through clothing.

She grabbed Levy's hand and asked what he was doing, but he did not respond.

When other passengers asked if she was all right, Levy protested his innocence.

"What are you talking about - look my hand is covered," he said, pointing to the jumper draped over his arm.

Levy then called her "crazy" and "stupid" and got off the tube at Westminster station.

The woman got off at the next stop, upset and crying.

She went on to report the assault to BTP. There was CCTV available of Levy, but police did not identify him. He would only be linked to the case two years later, after more women had been attacked.

A year after his first Tube assault, he assaulted three more women in quick succession and was arrested.

After being assaulted herself, the first of those three victims then filmed Levy sexually assaulting a second, unidentified woman, travelling in the same carriage.

The first woman immediately reported what had happened to BTP and provided the footage. Levy assaulted a third woman a week later.

After he had been questioned and had denied the three offences, BTP officers said they did not have enough evidence to charge, and he was released on bail.

The subsequent BTP investigation was full of delays. It was weeks before identity parades were arranged, and BTP did not approach the CPS for six months.

When it did, in May 2025, a CPS team had to scramble to make an emergency charging decision overnight, because BTP had again arrested Levy and wanted him in court the next day. This was highly unusual - BTP had known about the initial offences for six months.

In a statement, BTP Assistant Chief Constable Charlie Doyle said: "It is clear that opportunities to expedite the investigation were missed and we have amended our procedures to address these issues to ensure that repeat offenders are dealt with expeditiously and that linked offences are prioritised more effectively."

News.title: Serial sex offender guilty of murdering two women and raping third
News.content:
Earlier this year, Levy, 40, was found guilty by a jury at Inner London Crown Court of groping 10 women on the Tube and an 11th while in prison.

Details of this trial can now be reported after his conviction at the Old Bailey.

The offences took place between April 2022 at the prison, followed by the Tube assaults between 24 October 2023 and May 2025.

He had already been convicted of sexually assaulting two women in 2018, which was why he was in prison in 2022.

The sex offender had lost sight in one eye in an attack in May 2024 and played on this, claiming that his partial sight made him unsteady on his feet and all contact was accidental on these crowded trains.

Levy's tactic was to tie a jumper or hoodie around his waist, strap his arm down, and then back towards his victim with his hand fully or partially covered so he could grope them.

One of the Tube assault victims told the court: "It wasn't long before I learned that my attacker was already known to the police for sexual violence and is a convicted sex offender.

"You could not begin to understand the horror I felt at hearing this.

"How could a male who does this so often and so brazenly be allowed to repeat his attacks?

"Knowing this made me feel even more unsafe, the possibility that I could encounter Simon Levy again made me fearful and the idea that he would harm more women and that there would be many more victims was unthinkable."

During the sentencing hearing in June for the Tube attacks, Judge Michael Evans told Levy : "You were on the Tube for one purpose only, to sexually assault women."

Levy was convicted of 11 counts of indecent assault, including grabbing the prison guard in 2022, and given an extended sentence consisting of a six-year jail term plus a three-year period on licence.
