News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

Sports.title: Arsenal ready to hijack Liverpool’s £130million Bradley Barcola transfer from PSG after missing out on Vinicius Jr
Sports.content:
ARSENAL could look to hijack Liverpool’s swoop for Bradley Barcola after missing out on Vinicius Jr.

The Gunners had been plotting a blockbuster move for the Real Madrid winger, only for him to pen a new six-year deal at the Bernabeu.



Arsenal chiefs were committed to completing a big-money transfer for the Brazilian, who had one year remaining on his previous contract.

But Vinicius Jr instead opted to sign a new £480,000-a-week extension to stay put, ruling the Gunners out of the race.



Mikel Arteta‘s side remain desperate to land a new left winger, particularly after letting Leandro Trossard join Besiktas.

According to the Independent, Barcola is an “attractive option” for the Gunners.

But they will have to play “catch up” to Liverpool, who have already been negotiating personal terms.

The Reds are eager to land the Paris Saint-Germain winger as they seek a new star winger following Mo Salah’s departure.

Andoni Iraola‘s side have identified Barcola as a key target and have been working on the transfer for weeks.

But PSG’s asking price remains a stumbling block for all interested suitors, with Luis Enrique‘s men said to be demanding around £130million.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

And, according to French outlet Canal Plus, the Reds have told PSG they do not have the means to match their sky-high asking price.

That could now leave the door open for the Gunners to swoop.

Barcola, 23, has played 152 times for the French giants since joining from Lyon in 2023, scoring 39 goals and contributing towards two Champions Leagues and three Ligue 1 titles.

The winger came on as an 83rd minute substitute as PSG beat Arsenal in last season’s Champions League final back in May.



Given PSG’s summer business, he may be about to fall down the pecking order at Parc des Princes.

Following permanent exits for Lee Kang-in, Goncalo Ramos and Randal Kolo Muani, PSG signed French international attacker Maghnes Akliouche on Friday.

They are also keen on Ajax attacker Mika Godts, with Barcelona‘s World Cup final hero Ferran Torres also linked.



In addition to Barcola, Arsenal admire Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez.

A deal will be very difficult to accomplish, however, with the former Manchester City forward more likely to stay in LaLiga.

Another option is Everton ace Iliman Ndiaye.

The impressive Toffees star’s future on Merseyside looks uncertain, with Saudi side Al-Hilal also in the mix.

Arsenal gave a lacklustre display as they were beaten 3-1 by Real Betis in Dublin earlier this week.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Quizzed about the mood in the dressing room after the match, Arteta pulled no punches.

The Spaniard said: “They are very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Sports.title: Arsenal should sign Man Utd star Marcus Rashford after both sides had transfer dreams scuppered by El Clasico giants
Sports.content:
BOTH Marcus Rashford and Arsenal have seen their transfer dreams scuppered by the Clasico giants this summer.

Rashford, 28, was first to suffer when Barcelona snubbed the chance to land him in a £26million permanent deal after last season’s loan at the Nou Camp.



Instead the Catalans decided to splash out £69m on his England team-mate Anthony Gordon from Newcastle.

Arsenal’s own blow arrived on Thursday evening when top transfer target Vinicius Jr ended his flirtation with them by signing a new deal at Real Madrid worth a staggering £480,000 a week.



So, with both the Gunners and Rashford left licking their wounds, is it time they came together to solve each others’ problems?

Rashford is set to reunite with his Manchester United team-mates on Sunday for the first time in 18 months.



The forward is due to travel to Dublin for United’s pre-season training camp after completing his mandatory three-week post-World Cup break.

Rashford has not trained with United since January 2025 after loan spells with Aston Villa and then Barca.

Rashford and Alejandro Garnacho – now on loan at Villa from Chelsea – were part of a five-man ‘bomb squad’ isolated at United’s training ground last summer.

They were ordered by then-boss Ruben Amorim to report for separate training times to the main squad.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Although Amorim was sacked in January and head coach Michael Carrick has stabilised United, the imminent reunion is still awkward for all parties.

Rashford publicly declared his wish to join Barcelona permanently in May and doubled down on his desire to leave permanently during the World Cup.

But the England international’s £325,000-a-week salary – signed before Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Old Trafford involvement – has effectively blocked a permanent departure.

On the eve of the World Cup, Rashford posted a brief message on his Instagram page thanking Barcelona, Villa, England and their respective coaches.



There was no mention of United, the club he has been at since the age of seven.

United are also conspicuous by their absence on the bios of Rashford’s social media accounts.

Senior United figures were surprised by Barcelona’s decision not to buy Rashford, which has left them out of options.

United sources have repeatedly stressed they will not let Rashford leave on another season-long loan.

The academy graduate is under contract until 2028.



Rashford’s first appearance back at United could be in their final pre-season friendly against AC Milan, who are now managed by Amorim.

Arsenal wanted Brazilian ace Vinicius as their marquee signing to launch their first Prem title defence in 22 years.

They were led down the garden path and ended it with the sight of the Brazilian scrawling his signature on a new six-year Real contract.

But there are alternative left wingers on the market and Rashford is one of them.

Arsenal have been here before, with Raheem Sterling two years ago.



What appeared a canny deal turned out to be anything but.

Sterling’s slide has been so steep he is currently without a club and was arrested on suspicion of drug-driving in May.

Rashford is a downgrade on Vinicius – well, who isn’t? – but he ticks a lot of boxes for Arsenal: Premier League pedigree, Champions League clout, big-club nous, winners’ medals, international experience and with a point to prove.



Rashford has incentives aplenty to show he is too young for the riches of Turkey or Saudi Arabia.

He has hopes of representing England again at the Euros in 2028 as well as the 2030 World Cup.

When Rashford first steeled himself to leave United, he was insistent on playing for a Champions League club.

That would rule out Tottenham – but don’t bet against them making their own move, with boss Roberto Di Zerbi promising a “bomba” signing.

Spurs nor Rashford’s entourage have dampened speculation.



Tottenham have spent more than £200m on signings already, blowing United out of the water to buy Mateus Fernandes.

If they wanted to, Tottenham could foot the bill for Rashford’s £325,000 weekly salary.

Spurs are also lacking dynamism in attack, with James Maddison, who missed most of last season with an ACL injury and then sustained a minor problem in pre-season and Dejan Kulusevski on his way back from a patella injury he suffered in May 2025.

It suits Rashford to be linked with two of the Premier League’s biggest clubs after Barcelona deemed Gordon a better investment.

Well-placed sources have said a move to Arsenal for Rashford, however fanciful, is not a total non-starter.



Rashford has kept a low profile during his summer break but preparations have been made for his return to Manchester.

The circumstances aren’t ideal but he at least has a club.

Jadon Sancho, another winger now off the books at United, put non-league minnows Flixton on the map by using their training facilities.

Sancho is a free agent, at least.

For Rashford, he is running out of time in a transfer window that closes in less than four weeks.



Even with his steep salary, Rashford is more appealing than Sancho.

He started matches for England at the World Cup, scored in the 4-2 group stage win against Croatia and contributed to a Barcelona title triumph last season.

When push comes to shove, something can happen out of nothing in the final days of a transfer window.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Rashford’s temporary move to Villa materialised with less than 72 hours until it closed.

For now, there will be much to ponder for him and Arsenal as the new season rapidly approaches.

Sports.title: Friends with tyrants, wants royal treatment & World Cup sale bid failed… so is Infantino now too toxic to run football?
Sports.content:
WELCOMING Fifa boss Gianni Infantino to the splendour of the Oval Office, Donald Trump anointed him the “king of soccer”.

Once the target for childhood bullies, the football bureaucrat from humble beginnings was now being feted by the world’s most powerful man.



It was likely a giant ego boost for someone not already lacking in that department — a TV contract at the 2022 World Cup stipulated that Infantino must be pictured onscreen at every game he attended.

Yet, has the floundering Fifa chief’s puffed-up self-importance now chronically clouded his judgement?



Believing he had the backing of enough of football’s power brokers across the globe, he attempted to sell off stakes in the World Cup for £15billion last month.

But he had drastically overplayed his hand. Europe’s governing body Uefa threatened a boycott of the 2030 World Cup.



And despite Infantino’s plans being hastily dropped, the Europeans remain hell-bent on forcing a vote of no confidence in the Fifa president.

Trump’s cringeworthy flattery of Infantino as footballing royalty at the White House in March 2025 was ­perhaps not so ludicrous.

For the most powerful man in the world’s most popular sport enjoys all the gilded trappings of a head of state.

Dripping in wealth — he earns around £4.5million a year in salary and bonuses — Infantino, 56, likes to travel the globe by private jet, glad-handing presidents and princes.



Before he arrived in Vancouver for a Fifa conference in April, the organisation had demanded a ­presidential-style full motorcade for the football administrator.

The level four escort — which can ignore red lights and block other vehicles — is used for visiting US presidents and surpasses security measures laid on for Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney.

Vancouver’s police denied the request.

So how did Infantino become football’s arch power broker? And is he now too toxic to run the ­beautiful game?

He was born to Italian immigrant parents in the pretty Swiss Alpine village of Brig in March 1970.



A base for nearby ski slopes and summer hiking trails not far from the Italian border, it is a world away from the cauldrons of international football.

As the youngest of three and known as Piccolo — meaning little one — Infantino suffered health ­complications as an infant and required a blood transfusion.

He would later tell reporters that he received blood from donors in Bristol and Serbia, adding: “I would love to meet them.



“I survived with English blood and 46 years later I am the Fifa president. It’s a personal story, but I am happy to share it.”

His father Vincenzo was from Calabria — the “toe” of Italy — while his mother Maria was originally from Lombardy in its north.

They moved to Switzerland in search of a better life.

Vincenzo worked night shifts on trains while Maria was employed at a newspaper kiosk at the station.

Infantino’s cousin Daniel Nellen, who owns a hair salon in Brig, described Vincenzo’s drive to provide for his family: “Work three days, go, stay one night and come back. When he had days off, he worked in the kiosk at the station with Gianni’s mother. Then he would go again with the train to Rome, Paris, Brussels.”



Yet, despite being grafters, Daniel says the family faced discrimination because of their Italian background.

The salon boss told The Athletic last year: “From the Swiss, we felt this racism. Gianni had red hair and his skin had freckles. This was not too much of a big problem. The problem more was being Italian.”

Infantino touched on the bullying when he made his infamous speech on the eve of the 2022 Qatar World Cup.

Reacting to the criticism of the Gulf state’s human rights record, he said: “Today I feel Qatari. Today I feel Arab. Today I feel African. Today I feel gay. Today I feel disabled. Today I feel a migrant worker.

“I feel like them because I know what it feels like to be discriminated, to be bullied as a foreigner in a country. At school I was bullied because I had red hair and freckles. I was bullied. I didn’t speak good German. What do you do then? You lock yourself in your room, you cry and then you try to make some friends.”



The comments were described as “crass” and “clumsy” by one human rights group.

His cousin Daniel said that growing up, Infantino’s intelligence was “crazy,” adding: “Learning was so easy for Gianni.

“He came home from school and the first thing he would do was open up Gazzetta dello Sport, the Italian sports newspaper — the results of the games, the matches, sport, sport, sport, football, football, football.”



Inter Milan fan Infantino was not much of a player, his career reached only as far as the third team for local amateur club FC Brig-Glis. Another cousin, Renato Vitetta, revealed: “Let’s just say he wasn’t the best player.”

Any hopes that Infantino had of a career on the pitch were over when he was still a primary school pupil. In a school assignment he wrote that he had set his heart instead on becoming a football lawyer.

Cousin Daniel added: “I don’t think that when you are 20 years old, you think about becoming Fifa president.

“But he said, ‘If I’m not good enough [to be a footballer], I want to be the lawyer of the footballer’. Always, his idea was to make ­something with football.”

Aged 18, Infantino stood in FC Brig-Glis’s election for a new ­president.



He promised new sponsors and revenue streams and that his mum Maria would wash the ­players’ kit for as long as he remained president.

Shocking club veterans, he won the vote. It showed an astute grasp of electioneering that Infantino would use in the future.

Studying law at the University of Fribourg, he then won a job as legal counsel and general secretary of the International Centre for Sports Studies in the Swiss city of Neuchatel. Then, aged 30, he landed a ­position in Uefa’s legal department.

Dan O’Toole, Uefa’s former brand manager, remembers him as an “amiable” colleague.

He said last year: “In the early years, we used to go out socially and go around to his house. He was quiet, if anything. Not shy, just sort of quiet.”



Strait-laced Infantino, who speaks seven languages, became best known to football fans as the suit who drily oversaw the Champions League draw.

Rising quickly through the ranks, he became Secretary General in 2009, overseeing the expansion of the Uefa Euro 2016 tournament to 24 teams.

In 2001 he married Leena Al ­Ashqar, who once worked for the Lebanese FA. They have four daughters.



In 2016 he defied expectations and won the Fifa presidential ­election to replace disgraced Sepp Blatter. With a typically sharp- elbowed campaign, he promised to expand the World Cup to 40 teams.

A workaholic, he began his tenure by flying from Geneva to Bristol on a no-frills easyJet flight to attend a meeting in Cardiff.

He told reporters: “It was the ­easiest and best option for me. We are normal people and we have to behave like normal people.”

Today his travel tastes are a little different.

At this summer’s World Cup it was reported he flew at least 31,144 miles by Qatari private jet, watching the likes of Lionel Messi and Jude ­Bellingham work their magic.



Reportedly somewhat aloof while at Fifa’s offices in Zurich, he was said to come alive when mixing with the rich and powerful.

An anonymous source told news site Politico: “He loves dictators and billionaires. When he sees people with money, he melts.”

Nick McGeehan, from the human rights group FairSquare, said last year:

“He clearly thinks of himself as a statesperson. If you don’t think that power can be challenged, you start to behave like an authoritarian and feel at home with others with the same power.”

In 2019 Infantino accepted an Order of Friendship medal from Vladimir Putin and moved his family to Qatar before the 2022 World Cup there.

He faced widespread criticism after he took a selfie close to Pele’s open coffin at the Brazil legend’s 2023 wake.



He claimed Pele’s teammates and family members had asked him to take the photo.

In December 2025 he personally presented Donald Trump with the much-mocked inaugural Fifa Peace Prize.

By February, the US was at war with Iran. Shortly before this summer’s World Cup final, Infantino told Trump: “The American dream, Mr. President, came to reality. We united the world.”

In the tournament, when the US’s star striker Folarin Balogun was red-carded in the Round of 32, it should have triggered an automatic one-match ban, but Trump personally called up his buddy Infantino and lobbied for a review.

In a move that caused widespread anger, Fifa suspended the ban and Balogun played in the next knockout match against Belgium.



Uefa said the decision “crossed a red line” and had undermined “the integrity of the game”. Many felt ­justice was done on the pitch when the US were thrashed 4-1.

The tournament delivered record attendances and $15billion in ­revenue, with 1.5billion fans around the world watching the final itself.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Infantino, desperate for re-election next March, made his move when he considered himself at his most powerful. Yet, his plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup was a ­cataclysmic blunder.

Now, the pompous king of soccer may soon be booted off his Fifa throne.

Sports.title: FA order major change to all English stadiums after tragic death of ex-Arsenal kid Billy Vigar
Sports.content:
'TAKE ACTION' FA order major change to all English stadiums after tragic death of ex-Arsenal kid Billy Vigar

THE FA have banned solid brick walls around pitches in the wake of Billy Vigar’s tragic death last September.

The former Arsenal academy striker died aged 21 after suffering a brain injury while in action for Chichester City against Wingate & Finchley in the seventh tier.



Vigar’s fatal injury was sustained in a collision with a pitchside wall.

The awful incident prompted a petition for all such walls to be removed from football grounds.



Government and PFA chiefs had already called for a safety inquiry in June 2023.

This followed Alex Fletcher’s November 2022 collision with a hoarding while playing for Bath, which saw him suffer a fractured skull.



A safety review by health and safety experts was launched by the Football Association following Vigar’s death.

And ahead of the new campaign, the FA have made their decision.

The ruling states that it “no longer permits solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers around pitches across the National League System for men [Steps 1-6], and the Women’s National League [Tiers 3-4].”

The FA’s statement goes on to add: “Any existing solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers must be removed as soon as reasonably practicable, or covered with suitable protection if they cannot be removed for structural reasons.



“We have informed the clubs at this level that will be required to take action as a result of these changes.



“Matches may continue to be played at affected grounds during this period; however, clubs should assess the safety of their pitch perimeter barriers on an ongoing basis, and where alterations to these structures have been recommended during this review, they should develop a plan to complete any such alterations within a reasonable timeframe.”

Money will be made available to help clubs make the vital changes.

The statement concludes: “To support this important work, The FA and the Premier League will provide funding to facilitate these changes, which will be administered by the Premier League Stadium Fund.

“The initial phase of the programme is already underway, and we will continue to provide full support to the clubs involved in this process.”

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes’ £75million Arsenal transfer DELAYED despite already training with new Gunners team-mates
Sports.content:
BRUNO GUIMARAES’ £75million transfer to Arsenal has reportedly been delayed.

That is despite the Brazilian, 28, allegedly already training with his new Gunners team-mates.



The Premier League champions agreed the £75m fee with Newcastle on Wednesday.

That would see the North Londoners pay the full amount with no add-ons across 24 months.



However, reports surfaced on Friday evening that there has been a hiccup in the move.

According to Diario AS, the hold-up is due to “bureaucratic issues” – essentially the paperwork.

Arsenal will be hopeful the administrative creases can simply be ironed out quickly before the official announcement and unveiling.

Even so, the AS report adds that Guimaraes had his first pre-season session with Mikel Arteta’s squad earlier on Friday.

Guimaraes arrived at Newcastle’s pre-season training camp in Spain to ask new head coach Matthias Jaissle for a move away.

Once permission was granted, he flew to London for his Arsenal medical.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Arsenal initially had a £75m offer rejected due to the make-up of the deal featuring various add-ons.

But once they guaranteed the entire transfer fee, the Toon relented and agreed to sell their influential captain.

Lyon will pocket between £7m and £8m as part of the sell-on clause inserted when the Magpies signed Guimaraes in January 2022 for £40m.

In his four-and-a-half years on Tyneside, the midfielder made 195 appearances, scoring 31 and assisting 32.



Crucially, he was part of the team that ended Newcastle’s 70-year wait for a trophy by winning the Carabao Cup last year.

Guimaraes’ exit adds to another turbulent transfer window for the Toon, who also sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, while manager Eddie Howe left.

Their recruitment faltered, too, with targets Johan Manzambi and Victor Munoz opting to sign for Aston Villa and Liverpool respectively.

Sports.title: One of Ukraine’s largest stadiums bombed by Putin ‘missile’ on eve of top-flight match leaving hole in roof as 2 injured
Sports.content:
ARENA ATTACK One of Ukraine’s largest stadiums bombed by Putin ‘missile’ on eve of top-flight match leaving hole in roof as 2 injured

ONE of Ukraine’s largest sports stadiums has been blitzed by Putin on the eve of a top-flight match.

Russian forces struck in southern Ukraine today, August 7 at around 3pm, targeting Odessa’s Chornomorets Stadium, the largest arena in the south of the country.



The stadium, which can hold more than 34,000 fans, is home to both Chornomorets Odessa and Seasters.

The next game scheduled to be played there is August 8 between Chornomorets and Kolos, although this is now in doubt.



Ukrainian politician Oleksiy Honcharenko first reported the attack on his Telegram channel, showing footage from the impact site.

The blast damaged the arena’s load-bearing structures and blew out windows around the building’s perimeter, as well as damaging the stands.



A large hole was also made in the roof.

Head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration Oleh Kiper confirmed a 29-year-old woman sustained shrapnel wounds in the attack.



He said: “The injured woman is being provided with all necessary assistance.

“All relevant services are working at the scene.”

Although according to local media two people were injured.

Stadium director Serhiy Burka said that the injured were most likely employees of the club.

The explosion also caused dry grass to ignite on land next to the stadium but this was quickly dealt with by rescuers.



The Chornomorets Stadium is situated in Shevchenko Park in Odessa’s historic centre and regularly hosts Ukrainian Premier League matches.

Meanwhile, savage Russian forces carried out a sickening double-tap strike in the Zaporizhzhia region.

Two rescuers were wounded in the attack, according to the head of the regional military administration Ivan Fedorov.

A double tap strike a military tactic where the initial bombing, missile, or drone attack is followed intentionally by a second strike on the same location minutes later.

The secondary blast is intended to maximise casualties by hitting emergency crews and civilians who have rushed to the scene to help any rescue.



In the Zaporizhzhia strike, the second attack hit a fire truck as crews were attempting to put out a fire caused by the first hit.

An outbuilding of a private home was also damaged and subsequently caught fire.

Russian forces have repeatedly carried out double-tap strikes in the Zaporizhzhia region, reports claim.

On July 13, guided bombs initially struck residential areas in Zaporizhzhia which were then targeted a drone attack as police, rescuers and medics attended to the injured.

The Dnipropetrovsk region, in the south-east of the country was also targeted, with strikes killing two people and injuring six, according to the regional governor.



Oleksandr Hanzha, writing on Telegram, said Russian forces had launched nearly 50 attacks on five districts in the region, deploying drones, artillery and aerial bombs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Two people were killed near Nikopol, a frequent Russian target on the western bank of the Dnipro River, opposite the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant.

One of the wounded was in a serious condition, Ganzha said.

Sports.title: Do Carabao Cup 1st round ties go to extra time or straight to penalties if it ends as a draw after 90 minutes?
Sports.content:
CLUB football returns with the first round of the Carabao Cup!

Sides from the Championship, League One and League Two will be looking to get their seasons off to a perfect start.



Some first round ties look too close to call and could still be level at the end of normal time.

If the match ends all square, the question at the front of everyone’s mind is whether there is extra time and penalties.



SunSport brings you all the information you need.

Do Carabao Cup 1st round ties go to extra time or straight to penalties if it ends as a draw after 90 minutes?

Carabao Cup first round ties go straight to penalties if the score is level after 90 minutes.

Ahead of the 2018/19 season, organisers scrapped extra time to reduce “additional fatigue issues” following a vote by English Football League clubs.

Extra time is used only in the Carabao Cup in the second leg of the semi-finals (if the aggregate score is level) and in the final.

What happened in last year’s Carabao Cup final?

Manchester City are the Carabao Cup holders after they beat Arsenal 2-0 in last year’s final.

Nico O’Reilly scored twice in four second-half minutes to fire his side to Wembley glory.



City’s triumph meant that Pep Guardiola became the first manager to win the League Cup five times.

The legendary gaffer left his post at the Etihad at the end of last season.

Sports.title: Mo Salah looks stunned as he’s offered very unusual gift by mayor after signing for Trabzonspor
Sports.content:
EGYPTIAN icon Mo Salah was left awkwardly scratching his beard after receiving an unconventional signing bonus from the mayor of his new Turkish home.

The Liverpool legend looked baffled after a promotional video for Trabzonspor took an unexpected political turn.



Many were stunned when 2024’s Premier League Player of the Season signed for Turkey‘s fourth biggest team on a free transfer.

But a new twist in Salah’s transfer saga has surprised even the superstar himself.



After 25,000 Trabzonspor fans overwhelmed Salah with flares and an electric show of support yesterday, the 34-year-old was greeted with an entirely different prospect on Friday morning.

Trazbon district mayor Huseyin Avni Coskun Cebi met Salah for a commercial shoot, but the local administrator suddenly began speaking to the marquee signing about the climate crisis.

Salah picked at his facial hair as mayor Cebi informed him: “Global warming is threatening the world.”

“In the future, it will become difficult to live in Egypt during the summer. Our district will be very liveable in those years. It will be among the places least affected by global warming.”

After advertising Trazbon’s eco credentials, Cebi followed up with an unprecedented gift to try and tempt Salah to stay in the city in long term.

In a gesture that seemed to shock Salah, the right winger was bestowed with a “beautiful piece of land” in the city.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Having expected promotional duties, Salah was instead given “a wonderful place for your children and grandchildren, with no water problems and unaffected by global warming.”

The latest offering comes on top of a £363,000 a week salary after tax at Trabzonspor.

Salah snubbed interest from the Saudi Pro League and Istanbul giants Bekistas before signing an eye-watering deal in the Black Sea city.

Sports.title: Stevenage down Wycombe with stoppage-time winner to book place in Carabao Cup second round
Sports.content:
Stevenage down Wycombe with stoppage-time winner to book place in Carabao Cup second round

Stevenage scored in the dying embers of Friday's Carabo Cup first round draw with fellow League One side Wycombe to claim a 2-1 victory.

View 3 Images Stevenage manager Alex Revell saw his side claim a stoppage-time victory over Wycombe in the Carabao Cup on Friday

Stevenage debutant Josh Magennis scored an injury-time winner to secure a 2-1 victory over Wycombe and book Alex Revell's side's place in the Carabao Cup second round.

‌



The Northern Irish international, 35, who signed from Exeter City this summer, headed it home in the fifth minute of injury time to break Wycombe hearts at Adams Park on Friday, ensuring it would be a winning start to the competitive season for The Boro.

‌



On the same night, Wolves comfortably saw off League Two side Port Vale 3-0 at Molineux while Middlesbrough defeated Wrexham 1-0 in an all-Championship affair in the other two Carabao Cup games.

‌



Carabao Cup first round TV guide: How to watch every match live this weekend READ MORE :

Both Wycombe and Stevenage welcomed fresh faces into their starting XI's following relatively busy summers, with the hosts giving competitive debuts to goalkeeper Conor Hazard, winger Silko Thomas, right back Sam Parker, and veteran defender Steve Cook, while the visitors started former Burton defender Terence Vancooten from the off.

It took a while for the game to get going, with nothing much to shout about inside the opening 25 minutes as both sides failed to convert several crosses into the box.

However, it was the experienced Dan Kemp in midfield for Stevenage who finally broke the deadlock just before the half-hour mark, pouncing on a poor touch from Wycombe defender Connor Taylor before taking the ball round his man and burying it into the near bottom corner.

‌



View 3 Images Wycombe Wanderers manager Michael Duff saw his side fall to a 2-1 defeat on home soil

The visitors could've doubled their lead within a minute as they countered at pace and caught Wycombe sleeping, though winger Phoenix Patterson could only fire low and hard into Hazard's arms.

Much to the relief of the home fans, however, Wycombe finally dragged themselves back into the game and leveled the scores in the 39th minute, with Scottish midfielder Ewan Henderson playing a neat one-two with Thomas before finding the bottom left corner.

‌



Wycombe ended the first half the better of the two sides, though Kemp came so close to doubling his and Stevenage's tally with a piledriver from the edge of the penalty area that smacked the underside of the crossbar before bouncing back out.

The Chairboys continued their positive play into the second half as the lively Fred Onyedinma caused plenty of problems down the right, while several penalty shouts for the hosts were also waived away by referee Jamie O'Connor.

View 3 Images Stevenage midfielder Dan Kemp opened the scoring in the first half

Article continues below

On the opposite flank, debutant Thomas was also causing problems for Stevenage's defense, but Wycombe just couldn't carve out an opening that would give them the lead in the tie.

Both teams pushed for a winner in the final embers of the game, but neither could find the winner they so desperately craved, until Magennis, fresh off the substitutes bench, popped up with a header in the dying seconds to win the game for Stevenage and book their spot in Monday's second round draw.

Both sides are next in action on the opening day of the League One season next weekend, when Wycombe travel to face Blackpool and Stevenage face Burton, both on Saturday, Aug. 15 (3 p.m.).

Sports.title: Liverpool prepare blockbuster offer for PSG star Bradley Barcola - but there's a catch
Sports.content:
Liverpool prepare blockbuster offer for PSG star Bradley Barcola - but there's a catch

Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's top transfer target this summer and the Reds are now ready to move forward with trying to sign the Paris Saint-Germain winger

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's top transfer target (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool are ready to make their opening offer for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola, but their bid will be rejected by the French giants.

‌



Barcola has emerged as Liverpool's number one transfer target this summer, with new manager Andoni Iraola desperate to strengthen in wide areas. The France international has entered the final two years of his current contract with PSG, who have softened their stance on a deal.

‌



The reigning Champions League champions had initially been firm in their stance that the 23-year-old was not for sale at any price. But, having lined up potential replacements, a deal can now be done - if their asking price is met.

‌



Liverpool have found it slow going in the transfer window this summer, with a £35million deal for Osasuna winger Victor Munoz the only significant piece of business done, as the £55m arrival of Jeremy Jacquet was sealed in January.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

But the Reds are now ready to step up negotiations with PSG for Barcola, according to L'Equipe. They will submit an official offer in the region of €115million (£98m) in the expectation that it will be rejected.

‌



PSG don't want to lose Barcola, who has contributed heavily to their success under Luis Enrique's management. Yet they are also unwilling to keep a player against his will, so have slapped a €150 million (£128.5m) price tag on their star player.

Their resolve has likely be strengthened by the £120m fee RB Leipzig got from Real Madrid for Yan Diomande - a player four years younger and with far less experience than Barcola.

Barcola has 39 goals in 152 appearances for the club since joining from Lyon three years ago. He has combined well with Ousmane Dembele and Desire Doue under Enrique's management, but is keen to join Liverpool.

‌



View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is desperate for a new winger (Image: Michael Miller/ISI Photos, ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Barcola has already agreed personal terms with Liverpool and it seems likely that a deal can be done. Liverpool sporting director Richard Hughes is leading discussions, with Luis Campos representing PSG and agent Moussa Sissoko speaking on behalf of Barcola.

L'Equipe says that Liverpool are not actively pursuing any alternative to Barcola, which is a measure of their determination to land the Frenchman. Iraola spoke publicly about the need for a winger, even after Munoz was signed.

‌



"There are obvious situations that we know where we need to sign players," he said last month. "A winger, for example – we definitely need to sign a winger.

"But there are other situations that we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what’s the cost, how we also see the players we have. We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust but is still not the ideal situation. So, it will depend on a lot of things."

Sports.title: Arsenal could break unwanted transfer record as Mikel Arteta green lights two deals
Sports.content:
Arsenal could break unwanted transfer record as Mikel Arteta green lights two deals

Arsenal are still chasing a blockbuster signing in the summer transfer window and Mikel Arteta's side need to lay the groundwork first by making space in the squad

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta knows that sales are needed this summer (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal could finally eclipse their record sale with Gabriel Martinelli attracting interest from Turkey. The Gunners' focus recently has been on Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior, but exits are also in the pipeline.

‌



Guimaraes is poised to join Mikel Arteta's side for £75million after a compromise was reached with Newcastle. But the pursuit of Vinicius has ended in defeat, with the Brazilian forward set to sign a new contract with Real Madrid.

‌



Arsenal will now turn their attention to other targets as they chase a blockbuster deal, and while the identity of their alternative signing is not yet known, the groundwork is being laid. Leandro Trossard (Besiktas), Jakub Kiwior (Porto), Karl Hein (Werder Bremen) and Christian Norgaard (Everton) are currently the only players to leave and bring in transfer fees this summer.

‌



It is something that sporting director Andrea Berta knows he must address, especially if a world-class forward like Julian Alvarez and a centre-back to cover for the injured William Saliba is to arrive before the deadline passes on September 1.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool's firm stance on Djed Spence transfer as Reds battle defensive injury crisis READ MORE :

Martinelli has entered the final year of his contract with Arsenal, posing the possibility of his exit, over seven years after he joined the club. The 25-year-old has 62 goals in 278 appearances for the club since his £6million move in 2019, but his time may have come.

‌



Arsenal are reportedly considering a sale to Galatasaray, who are interested in landing the Brazil international. And were a move to come to fruition it could see Martinelli become Arsenal's record sale, with the £35m earned for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's move to Liverpool in 2019 surprisingly still the high-water mark for the club.

Their inability to sell well has become an issue for Arsenal, who have often seen their rivals out-perform them. Trossard pulled in £17m from Besiktas, while Norgaard earned just £7m from Everton. If Arsenal are to achieve their goals in terms of incomings then Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus could become facilitators.

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus could both be sold (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Jesus has become a fringe player at Arsenal, with Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz ahead of him in the pecking order and is attracting interest from Napoli and AC Milan. The 29-year-old's contract expires in June 2027, meaning this window is Arsenal's last realistic chance to earn a decent fee.

Arsenal are understood to be seeking a fee in the region of the £17m they got for Trossard, but as time ticks by in August they could be forced to compromise.

Arteta knows that Arsenal must strengthen their squad this summer if they are to stand any chance of defending their Premier League title in 2026/27. "We are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear," he said in a post-match press conference after facing Girona on the weekend.

Article continues below

"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else. And you can just see it. The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing, we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do."

Sports.title: UEFA could boycott 5 tournaments in next 11 months after new Gianni Infantino statement
Sports.content:
UEFA could boycott 5 tournaments in next 11 months after new Gianni Infantino statement

Gianni Infantino is determined to cling onto power as FIFA president and his refusal to resign in the wake of the World Cup private investment scandal could force UEFA into action

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino is ready for the fight (Image: AP Photo/Martin Meissner)

UEFA could be forced to carry out their threat of boycotting FIFA tournaments in less than a month after Gianni Infantino refused to give in to the mounting pressure on him to resign.

Rather than fall on his sword, Infantino has made moves to solidify his position as FIFA president. Following seven hours of crisis talks in Morocco on Wednesday, FIFA released a statement saying Infantino had their "full support" after his botched attempt to invite private investment into tournaments.

FIFA have opted to close ranks and go on the offensive, saying they will "no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation".

The battle lines have been drawn, with UEFA leading the backlash against Infantino. The Football Association has followed in Wales' footsteps by formally withdrawing their support of the Swiss, but with the pressure yet to tell, UEFA and their allies may have to follow through with their threat.

Gianni Infantino state of play as 211 nations decide desperate FIFA president's fate READ MORE :

Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

In a statement on Thursday, UEFA said FIFA's words following their meeting "changes nothing" and that their threat of a boycott stands. It means FIFA have been put on notice ahead of their next international tournament, the Under-20 Women's World Cup, which is scheduled to be hosted in Poland, beginning on September 5.

After that comes the Under-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco in October and the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar in November and December. Next summer comes a much bigger fish: the Women's World Cup in Brazil. If it came to it, boycotting that would send a strong message - and it is a sacrifice England star Lucy Bronze is willing to make.

FIFA tournaments UEFA could boycott FIFA Under-20 Women's World Cup (Poland) - September 2026 FIFA Under-17 Women's World Cup (Morocco) - October 2026 FIFA Under-17 World Cup (Qatar) -November/December 2026 FIFA Women's Champions Cup (Miami) -January 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup (Brazil) - June/July 2027

“The message that we stand by … is ‘for the good of the game’. The players who play in those competitions, the European players, we stand by our beliefs and what the right thing is for our game,” Bronze said ahead of a Chelsea pre-season friendly in New Zealand.

“If that means boycotting competitions, then that has to happen. It’s for the future of the game and not just for me today and tomorrow, it’s for all the little girls or little boys who come after us to make sure that they’re in a good place, when the game is moving forward in decades to come, not just tomorrow.”

With Infantino not willing to resign, UEFA may have to back a rival candidate in the upcoming FIFA presidential election. Infantino has been in charge for 10 years and was set to stand unopposed for a fourth term next year, but the events of the past week have changed everything.

View 2 Images UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin is leading the effort to oust Gianni Infantino (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

A UEFA statement shared on Thursday afternoon read: "UEFA's associations were very clear about the conditions attached to the non-participation in FIFA competitions.

"First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn, and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

"These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino's presidency. That position holds.

"Yesterday's (Wednesday) announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing."

Sports.title: England star Ivan Toney charged with assault at London nightclub
Sports.content:
England star Ivan Toney charged with assault at London nightclub

Ivan Toney, who represented England at this summer's World Cup, has been charged with assault following a police investigation into an incident at a Soho nightclub last year

England footballer Ivan Toney charged with Soho nightclub assault

Ivan Toney has been charged with assault causing actual bodily harm following an incident at a Soho nightclub in December last year.

The England striker, 30, was charged on July 31 relating to the alleged assault on December 2025 on Wardour Street, London. He is due to appear in court on September 24.

A statement from the Met Police said: "A man has been charged with assault following a Met investigation.

"Ivan Toney, 30 (16.03.1996), of Northampton, was charged on Thursday, 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm.

"He will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday, 24 September.

"The charge relates to an assault, which reportedly took place on 6 December 2025 at a nightclub on Wardour Street, W1."

Tottenham respond as Arsenal consider shock transfer for Spurs skipper Cristian Romero READ MORE :

View 2 Images Ivan Toney has been charged with assault (Image: Javier Garcia/Shutterstock)

A spokesperson for Toney said: "Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court."

Toney was part of England's squad at the recent World Cup in the USA, Canada and Mexico. He helped the Three Lions to a third-placed finish, their best performance since 1966.

His selection came as something of a surprise to many and attracted widespread criticism due to Toney playing his football in Saudi Arabia, despite plundering 42 goals last term.

Toney didn't feature until the semi-final defeat by Argentina, where he came on as a late substitute. But he started the third-place playoff win against France, playing 78 minutes.

Toney began his career with hometown club Northampton before signing for Newcastle in 2015. From there, he went out on loan to Barnsley, Shrewsbury, Scunthorpe and Wigan.

View 2 Images Toney played twice for England at the World Cup (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

It was at Peterborough where his goal-scoring form first caught the eye, leading to a move to Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals in 141 appearance for the Bees before his money-spinning Saudi switch, including 36 in the Premier League, leading to a first England call-up in 2022 and a debut in March 2023.

Article continues below

In all, Toney has played 10 times for his country, scoring once in a friendly against Belgium at Wembley in March 2024.

Sports.title: Aston Villa stars 'think they know what's happening next' with Arsenal target Ezri Konsa
Sports.content:
Aston Villa stars 'think they know what's happening next' with Arsenal target Ezri Konsa

Arsenal are targeting Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa in a £60m deal - and his team-mates think they know where he'll end up before the transfer window closes

View 2 Images Arsenal are reportedly keen on signing Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa this summer. (Image: (Photo by Sarah Stier - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

Aston Villa stars are reportedly 'resigned to losing' Ezri Konsa this summer, with Arsenal interested in signing the England international. The Gunners are looking to bounce back from a disappointing setback in their pursuit of Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior.

‌



It's claimed the Gunners are eyeing the Villa star, as they look to bolster their backline following an injury to William Saliba and concerns over Jurrien Timber and Ben White. The Mail says both Arsenal and Liverpool are keen on securing the England international, with his Aston Villa colleagues worried that Konsa will depart the club.

‌



However, the Gunners will need to raise their offer, having already seen a bid much lower than Villa's £60m valuation swiftly rejected earlier this summer. It was claimed earlier this week that the Premier League champions will go back in with an improved offer before the window closes on September 1.

‌



Konsa has been among the main transfer targets for Mikel Arteta's side this summer, behind Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior, but Arsenal are reluctant to overspend. While Arteta will now look to find an alternative attacking option to Vinicius, signing Konsa would be a huge coup and soften the blow of missing out on the Brazilian.

Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer saga reaches conclusion as Real Madrid star strikes agreement READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

However, Villa have already seen several key players exit this summer, with Morgan Rogers departing for Chelsea and Youri Tielemans joining Manchester United, meaning they are under no financial pressure to cash in.

‌



Defender Lucas Digne is also expected to complete a move to PSG, but there is still said to be some anxiety within the Villa Park dressing room about Konsa's future, with the defender having just two years remaining on his contract.

Guimaraes is on the brink of switching to the Emirates Stadium for a reported £75m transfer from Newcastle United.

View 2 Images Vinicius Junior has made his decision (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

‌



Yet, the Gunners suffered a setback earlier this week, with Vinicius poised to pen a new contract with Real Madrid.

Arsenal had been ready to table a blockbuster contract for the Brazilian winger in a bid to tempt him to the Premier League champions this summer, with the 26-year-old locked in a stalemate with Los Blancos over fresh terms.

However, Jose Mourinho's outfit enhanced their contract proposal, and Vini Jr has now committed his future to the Bernabeu.

Article continues below

The Gunners will now put that setback behind them and are reportedly set to pursue Konsa as they prepare to defend their Premier League crown this season.

Arteta is also determined to go one step further and claim Champions League glory, having suffered defeat to PSG on penalties in the final back in May.

Sports.title: New Zealand begin South Africa tour with flattering win over Stormers
Sports.content:
New Zealand's first full-scale tour of South Africa in 30 years began with an underwhelming 38-21 win over the Stormers.

The scoreline flattered a scratch All Blacks side which was favoured to win comfortably.

The makeshift Stormers - in pre-season mode - rallied twice to tie the score, which was knotted at 14-14 until 13 minutes to go.

When the Stormers lost their second scrum-half and had no more reserve backs, the patched-up backline was ruthlessly exposed by New Zealand, who scored three tries in the last eight minutes.

The good news for the All Blacks was they appeared to finish with no major injuries, seven players made their first appearance in the black jersey this year, and two more made their debuts off the bench; prop Siale Lauaki and inside back Josh Jacomb.

Sports.title: Flintoff steps down as England Lions head coach
Sports.content:
Andrew Flintoff has stepped down as head coach of the England Lions.

Flintoff began in the role in September 2024, meaning he leaves just under two years in.

In June it was announced Flintoff would become head coach of Sydney Thunder in Australia's Big Bash League.

On the decision, Flintoff said: "Unfortunately I've made the decision to step away from my role with the Lions. Not only have I enjoyed my time having the opportunity to work with the best young cricketers in the country, but have taken great pride in seeing them develop.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive the top highlights from Andrew Flintoff's seven-game stint with Brisbane Heat in 2014/15.

"I'd like to thank the coaches and staff for all their passion, tireless work and support they give every day. In particular, Ed Barney who I've loved working with and was so lucky to have as a performance director, and obviously Rob (Key) for trusting me with one of the most important roles in English cricket.

"I can't wait to get started with the Thunder later in the year and see where coaching takes me."

Ed Barney, ECB men's performance director, said: "Fred has helped to transform the Lions environment into a programme that has had a major impact on young players. By creating an environment that both supports and pushes excellence at all times he has helped bring forward a new generation of young players.

"Coaches have also flourished alongside him, whether early in their coaching journey or with decades of experience, and he has consistently maximised the expertise around the group. We wish him the best in the next stage of his coaching career and look forward to a time he returns to the English game."

Mike Yardy will step in as head coach for the four-day Professional County Club Select XI match against Pakistan Men, which begins at Beckenham on Wednesday August 12.

Barcola is not the only PSG winger Liverpool are interested in, with Andoni Iraola's side having explored the conditions of a deal for Ibrahim Mbaye.

The 18-year-old, who predominantly plays off the right, is believed to be interested in moving to Anfield.

Iraola sees his wide men as being key to his philosophy, which is why this area of the squad is the big focus in his first window on Merseyside, especially after the exit of Mohamed Salah.

Barcola has two years left on his PSG contract and has indicated he will not be signing a new one amid frustrations at a lack of game time.

The opportunity to join Liverpool is said to appeal to the France international.

The key to getting any deal moving will be PSG's willingness to reduce the price tag on the man they bought for around £40m from Lyon in the summer of 2023.

Image: Barcola has two years left on his PSG contract

The success of Iraola's teams at Bournemouth and Rayo Vallecano centred around the pace, energy and work-rate from his wingers, so Barcola could be a key piece of the Spaniard's new Liverpool jigsaw.

The fact that Barcola has won nine major trophies in the last two years, including two Champions League titles, shows the calibre of player they are trying to bring to Anfield.

Arsenal, who missed out on signing Vinicius Junior following his Real Madrid contract extension, also hold an interest in Barcola.

Sports.title: White: I know where the Fury-AJ venue is - I did the deal!
Sports.content:
The long-awaited heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will take place "where the money is", says Dana White.

White, who founded the UFC and new promotion Zuffa Boxing, is a major figure in combat sports. He revealed that he knows where Fury vs Joshua will take place.

"We're the ones that have done all the deals for this fight. I did the deal for the venue, that's why I know where the venue is. I did the deal. We at TKO [the company which owns UFC, WWE and Zuffa Boxing] did the deal for television and we did everything," White told Sky Sports.

White told Sky Sports: "At the end of the day, here's the truth, you're going to go where the money is."

"It's just been such a [mess]. It's unbelievable what a [mess] this thing has been," White said.

"It goes to show why boxing has been so [messed] up for so long. Look at this. It's definitely not about the money. The Saudis are paying for this fight. So they're making [a lot] of money. And what I've noticed is in the boxing business since I've been in it for a very short period of time, six months, the promoters' egos are actually more important than the fights themselves and giving the fight fans the fights they want to see.

"It's all about ego with the promoters. It's fascinating. These guys are all really weak, some of the weakest people I've ever encountered in the fight game. It's fascinating."

Sky Sports has contacted Matchroom and Queensberry, the promoters of Joshua and Fury, for comment.

Fury was a guest at White's UFC event at the White House and the promoter has known both fighters from before he launched his own boxing business.

"I've talked about Anthony Joshua after he beat (Wladimir) Klitschko and I was like that's what boxing needs, good looking, charismatic, good speaking heavyweight champion. So I've always really liked Anthony Joshua," White said.

"There was a point in time where Tyson was stagnant and trying to get fights so he started talking [trash] about UFC fighters, trying to get a payday one way or another and that was around the time that I met him and I've always liked him.

"Tough as hell, when he was dropped by (Deontay) Wilder [and] he gets right back up like a zombie and finishes the fight. He's a fun guy to watch. He's one of the best ever."

Wycombe 1-2 Stevenage (Henderson 39; Kemp 27, Magennis 90+5)

Kim Hellberg – the most miffed man in English football at the end of last season after Spygate – allows himself a smile. Disappointing for Wrexham to exit at the first hurdle after reaching the fourth round last season. 16m ago 16.49 EDT 90+1 min: Doyle is shown a yellow card for holding back Whittaker on a Middlesbrough break. Share

17m ago 16.47 EDT 89 min: Joseph holds the ball up well for Boro deep in the Wrexham half. Share

26m ago 16.39 EDT 81 min: Lankshear is withdrawn to ovation but he soaks it up a little too much … 19-year-old Fin Cartwright has to wait a minute to come on because Lankshear took more than 10 seconds to get off the pitch. 31m ago 16.34 EDT 76 min: Whiteman has already brought more control to the Wrexham midfield. They’ve managed to get up the pitch for the first time in a while. Broadhead makes way for Davis Keillor-Dunn. Share

33m ago 16.32 EDT 74 min: Edmundson stretches to connect with Berhalter’s free-kick into the box but can only direct his header wide from inside the six-yard box. Share

34m ago 16.30 EDT 72 min: Subs for Wrexham: On: Kieffer Moore, Bailey Cadamarteri, Ben Whiteman.

36m ago 16.29 EDT 71 min: Good chance for Boro. Lankshear is played through by Joseph but he lifts his left-footed shot over the bar as he approaches the penalty area. Smith sends a hopeful volley wide for Wrexham at the other end. Share

38m ago 16.27 EDT 69 min: Hyam grapples with a Middlesbrough player or two as the corner is taken. Ward rises to take it and the whistle goes as well – Lankshear is shown a yellow for delaying the restart. Share

44m ago 16.21 EDT 63 min: Boro get their reward for being on the front foot pretty much the whole game – and dominating the second half in terms of possession (59%) and shots at goal (six to one). Share

45m ago 16.19 EDT GOAL! Middlesbrough 1-0 Wrexham (Lankshear 61) What a way to get off the mark for Will Lankshear! 49m ago 16.16 EDT 58 min: Berhalter is asked to shoot by the home crowd and obliges, twice. Both shots are blocked. Share
