Sports.title: Infantino’s World Cup sell-off debacle has rocked football but Fifa’s crisis has deep and rotten roots
Sports.content:
There are decades in which nothing happens, and weeks in which decades happen, and those weeks tend to result in leaders being toppled. Not even a fortnight ago, Gianni Infantino was taking his victory lap on Instagram, attacking “those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours” who had dared to question elements of his World Cup, which had generated a record $15bn in revenues. But the next day came the revelation of his plan to sell the World Cup to outside investors and a backlash that has him scrabbling to save his presidency.

It has been a remarkable few days, but this is a story whose roots stretch way back, to the decision in Zurich in 2010 to award the 2022 World Cup not to the US but to Qatar, to a furious Bill Clinton hurling an ashtray across the room and demanding action, to an FBI inquiry into corruption, and to the flipping of the larger-than-life Concacaf general secretary Chuck Blazer, who had two apartments in Trump Tower, one for himself and one for his cats.

Blazer now appears as the cheery, bearded, acceptable face of Fifa corruption. He drove about on a mobility scooter with his parrot, Max, on his shoulder and once high-fived Vladimir Putin after the Russian president suggested he looked like Karl Marx. But it was Blazer’s evidence that led to the arrests at Zurich’s Baur au Lac hotel in 2015 and the resignation of Sepp Blatter six days later.

The overwhelming favourite to replace Blatter was the president of Uefa, Michel Platini. He, though, was unacceptable to the US, because it was his decision to switch his vote to Qatar, following – although he maintains not as a result of – a meeting at the Élysée Palace with the then French president Nicolas Sarkozy and the crown prince and prime minister of Qatar.

Conveniently, evidence was found of a payment he had received from Fifa in 2011 leading to his suspension. The Berne federal prosecutor, Michael Lauber, broke protocol to name Platini as something “between a witness and a suspect”. It was enough: Platini stepped aside and Infantino stepped in as Uefa’s candidate. Lauber subsequently became attorney general of Switzerland only to resign after secretly meeting Infantino while investigating Fifa. Platini was subsequently cleared and is suing both Fifa and Infantino.

View image in fullscreen Chuck Blazer’s evidence led to the resignation of Sepp Blatter (left) in 2015. Photograph: Fabrice Coffrini/AFP/Getty Images

At the time, Infantino was the secretary general of Uefa, notable largely for his comical earnestness while conducting Champions League draws. He was elected Fifa president in February 2016, defeating the Bahraini Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, the president of the Asian Football Confederation, an avid hunter of wild boar who denied allegations of complicity in the torture of pro-democracy campaigners. Key had been a late change of mind by the Caribbean bloc: Sunil Gulati, the president of the US Soccer Federation, took credit for his persuasiveness.

With an ally elected, the US, Mexico and Canada won the right to host the 2026 World Cup. “You wanted to have it there and I wanted to have it there, and we really did it before we came to office,” Donald Trump, performing his classic trick of supervillain exposition, told Infantino at a dinner in Davos in 2020. The order of events is worth reiterating: Infantino was elected in February 2016, Trump was inaugurated in January 2017, the World Cup hosting decision was taken in May 2018.

The US has been a constant in Infantino’s presidency. He took power at a time when the US attorney general, Loretta Lynch, was promising to swill corruption out of Fifa but in terms of decisive action that has amounted to little more than a handful of cases involving dodgy South American broadcast rights deals. In May 2019 Fifa appointed as legal representatives the US law firm Paul Weiss. A few weeks earlier Paul Weiss had named a new senior partner: the former US attorney general Lynch. The following year, she praised Fifa’s newfound “transparency and ethical behaviour”.

Few would agree with her. Infantino arrived promising reform, yet within a year he was removing two leaders of Fifa’s ethics commission. The same weekend that Trump sacked James Comey as head of the FBI, in part for investigating Russian interference in US politics, Infantino fired Miguel Maduro, the chair of the governance and review committee, for blocking the re-election as a Fifa vice-president of the head of the Russian Football Union Vitaly Mutko on the grounds that as Russia’s sports minister he breached guidelines on political involvement.

View image in fullscreen Loretta Lynch promised to swill out corruption from Fifa during her time as US attorney general but there was minimal decisive action. Photograph: Saul Loeb/AFP/Getty Images

Infantino repeatedly bypassed the Fifa council, ducked the scrutiny of press conferences and came increasingly to rule by fiat. The plan to sell off a chunk of the World Cup is just the most egregious example. Why would he keep a plan of such revolutionary significance from his senior staff? Why would he give his members 53 days to consider such a plan, offering them a cash bonus to acquiesce? Why would he undermine his own tournament with hydration breaks and a half-time show in the final? Why override disciplinary protocols so the right players will be on the field, seemingly to highlight the tournament’s commercial appeal to potential investors?

The people who were in on the deal were connected to the Trump family, specifically Joshua Kushner, the brother of the president’s son-in-law. Again, questions immediately arise. Why would you sell off 21% of all future revenues for only 28% of what this World Cup made? Infantino’s relationship with Trump – awarding him the inaugural Fifa Peace Prize, appearing with him at world events, giving him a Club World Cup trophy, renting an office for Fifa in Trump Tower that is seemingly barely used – had already brought criticism.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Uefa’s robust and united response, the threat to boycott Fifa tournaments, was evidently not anticipated. The plan is dead, at least for now. Infantino, damaged, clings on, having rallied at least some senior Fifa staff at an emergency meeting in Rabat this week. The chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, one of the two members of the five-man inner council who voted against the plan when informed about it the day before the World Cup final, was, notably, not there. Plans to expand the World Cup to 64 teams, rallying Infantino’s base, have been accelerated.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino’s relationship with Donald Trump has attracted plenty of criticism. Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images

Letters of support that had looked as if they would ensure Infantino a further term unopposed are being withdrawn. On Friday, perhaps impressed by the promise of the 2030 World Cup final being in Casablanca, the Confederation of African Football pledged its support, joining Mexico, Argentina, Qatar, the UAE, Lebanon, Kuwait, Bhutan and Sri Lanka in backing Infantino.

Perhaps there will be an election, as scheduled, next March. Perhaps Infantino can muster a majority among Fifa’s 211 members. But Uefa has vowed to “paralyse” Fifa until he is gone. The first tournament that might be boycotted is the Under- 20 Women’s World Cup, which begins in Poland on 5 September. Poland has made significant investment in infrastructure and is keen for the tournament to go ahead as scheduled but its football federation would be unlikely to step outside the Uefa bloc.

The politicking goes on although already the discussion seems more about who might challenge or defeat Infantino than about how to change Fifa, where clientelism has reigned since João Havelange won the 1974 presidential election. The institution itself is rotten; it may be that it is irredeemable.

It’s very hard to know how genuine Infantino’s attempt to reform Fifa was, but it quickly foundered. And so Fifa’s attempt to move on from the crisis caused by the executive who rented an apartment for his cats in Trump Tower has wound up back in Trump Tower, with a president who rents an office there.

Sports.title: Jay-Z’s Roc Nation Sports making waves in European football transfer market
Sports.content:
In the end there was a clear winner. And Jay-Z’s latest victory came only 24 hours after the first record featuring him actually rapping for four years had been released by his wife, Beyoncé, on an extended remix pack of Morning Dew (Donk).

These days, the man who remains one of the most influential artists in hip-hop has his fingers in many pies, from the streaming service Tidal and his own streetwear brand, to champagne and cognac. But it is Roc Nation Sports – an offshoot of his entertainment company of the same name founded in 2008 – making headlines in the summer transfer window.

Established five years later in partnership with Creative Artists Agency, it began mainly representing players from the NBA, NFL and MLB, including Kevin Durant. Bayern Munich’s Jérôme Boateng was the first football client, in 2015, before Roc Nation Sports International (RNSI) was established four years later with a focus on stars at big European clubs.

Based in London, it now has more than 100 players on its books, including Vinícius Júnior – the Brazil forward who signed a lucrative new contract with Real Madrid this week believed to be worth around €25m. That came after Arsenal had been linked with a blockbuster move for the 26-year-old.

In July 2023 RNSI took over the successful Brazilian agents TFM – who already represented Vinícius, Gabriel Martinelli, and Endrick – and renamed it Roc Nation Sports Brazil.

In negotiations that have lasted two years, it had hoped to persuade Real to increase their star asset’s salary to €30m a year to match Kylian Mbappé, and allowed his contract to enter its final 12 months in an effort to drum up interest elsewhere. While Arsenal – now exploring other attacking options including Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye – are believed to have been willing to pay a big fee for Vinícius, it is understood that they thought signing him on a free transfer next season was more likely.

Nonetheless, Real upped their offer and Vinícius stayed. It is a decision that looks likely to cost them the chance to sign Rodri from Manchester City after Barcelona stole a march on their great rivals.

View image in fullscreen A phonecall from Vinícius Júnior reportedly led to Yan Diomande signing with Roc Nation Sports. Photograph: Kirsty Wigglesworth/AP

On the same day as the new six-year contract for Vinícius was announced, Yan Diomande flew to the Spanish capital to complete his record £115m transfer from RB Leipzig. The 19-year-old – who has made only 46 appearances at senior level for the German club and for Leganés in the Spanish second division but is already the most expensive African player in history – was pictured with his agents, Nathan Campbell and Kareem Gbaja on a private jet. RNSI has been reported to have been paid up to £17m in commission and fees.

A long-running saga that began when Liverpool had a £70m bid rejected by Leipzig in June ended with Diomande signing a seven-year deal at the Bernabéu on Thursday. It has provided a telling insight into the mechanisms of a modern transfer, with every week bringing a fresh twist. Having been told they must pay in excess of £100m to sign Diomande, Paris Saint-Germain withdrew from the race at the end of July after releasing a statement that said the European champions “will not engage in the inflationary and manipulative games of certain player agents”.

RNSI has also had to fend off two legal challenges, including one from the former Bournemouth winger Max Gradel who claims that his agency, Maxidel Management, had an existing agreement with Diomande. Gradel has filed a complaint with Fifa, although world football’s governing body did not block the player’s move to Real. Dez Bamba – who is president of Diomande’s first club, AFI Sud Comoé in Côte d’Ivoire – has said that the winger was persuaded to join RNSI after receiving a call from Vinícius. RNSI has not commented on the case.

Meanwhile, the Rainbow World Group instigated proceedings at the high court in London and the British Virgin Islands against Diomande in mid-June “to enforce binding image rights and intellectual property agreements tied to his early career development”. It is claimed Rainbow invested significant resources in the winger, including taking him for trials at Chelsea, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Newcastle before he was signed by Leganés. RNSI has not commented on the case.

Given Diomande’s meteoric rise, perhaps it is no surprise that clubs are flocking to invest in African academies.

Jeff Luhnow – the former general manager of the Astros and St Louis Cardinals who won three World Series baseball titles and owns Leganés as part of his Blue Crow network of clubs – told the Guardian last year Diomande was expected to be the first of many after they set up recruitment and development programmes in several African countries, including Ghana and Zambia, in the past several years. “We’ve got more players like that in our pipeline,” said Luhnow.

RNSI announced in November that it has signed eight young African stars, including the Ghana Under-17 midfielder Joseph Narbi and Francis Gomez, a Gambian winger currently at AC Horsens in Denmark. “We believe Africa is a hotbed of untapped footballing potential, and our expansion here is a natural progression of our global vision,” said Campbell.

In the dog-eat-dog world of football agents Jay Z’s new kids on the block are certainly making their presence felt.

Sports.title: Tottenham and Atlético in talks over Romero with Van de Ven set to sign new deal
Sports.content:
Tottenham are in talks with Atlético Madrid over the sale of Cristian Romero after categorically rejecting Arsenal’s approach for the Argentina defender and are expected to agree a new five-year deal with Micky van de Ven.

Romero has made no secret of his desire to leave Spurs despite signing a new four-year contract at the start of last season and had looked set to join Inter for a fee of around £35m. But Atlético are long-term suitors of the 28-year-old and are thought to be his preferred destination, with Diego Simeone’s side understood to be prepared to match Inter’s bid.

Reports in Spain on Friday suggested that personal terms have already been agreed with Romero, although his move may have to wait for Atlético to free up space in their squad before they can complete the transfer. Nahuel Molina, Romero’s Argentina teammate, is expected to join Roma while Aston Villa are hoping to sign Matteo Ruggeri.

Arsenal had also made their interest known as they search for a replacement for William Saliba, with the Frenchman out for an extended period due to a back issue. However, Tottenham – who have signed defenders Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi this summer – insisted that they did not want to sell to another Premier League club, least of all their north London rivals. Arsenal are also interested in Villa’s Ezri Konsa.

It is understood that Van de Ven had been considering his future in north London at the start of the summer after Tottenham narrowly avoided relegation last season. But the impact of the new manager, Roberto De Zerbi, has persuaded the Netherlands international to commit his future to the club after talks with his representatives.

Tottenham have already spent more than £200m on six new players this summer and are still in the market for a new attacker. Last week, De Zerbi said that they had “completed 60% of our project in the transfer market”.

Sports.title: Boardroom struggle deepens gloom as West Ham prepare for life on the outside
Sports.content:
There have been 10 summers of West Ham’s London Stadium tenancy and a number of winters of discontent. As the Hammers kick off the new season on Saturday, a Carabao Cup first-round fixture with Portsmouth is a stark reminder of reduced circumstances, further confirmation of last season’s relegation from the Premier League. The summer has been as bleak as any of those winters, with a number of factors colliding to deepen the gloom of relegation.

Certain clubs, including West Ham back in 2011-12 when promotion was achieved at first time of asking under Sam Allardyce, have used the Championship to take a beat, to refresh and replenish. Can this be the case at West Ham 2026? The Hammers are short-odds favourites for promotion but behind the scenes it has been a summer of turbulence, particularly in the boardroom, where a power struggle is being fought.

Portsmouth will bring 9,000 supporters on Saturday but will David Sullivan be present? This week it was revealed the operators of London Stadium had recommended the former joint-chair (but still co-owner) stay away, because of the “potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators”.

It is expected that Sullivan will turn up, despite a fans’ advisory board statement that his attendance would cause “offence and upset”. It has been suggested that he wants to enjoy the coming season as a fan and is happy to bide his time before any consideration of selling his 38.8% stake. Considering his personal circumstances, his attendance would be a brazenly unpopular act. On 25 May, when relegation was confirmed despite a home win over Leeds, Sullivan was forced to leave the stadium early for his own safety.

View image in fullscreen Daniel Kretinsky wants to increase his shares in West Ham to just under 50.1%. Photograph: David W Černý/Reuters

Sullivan continues to deny allegations of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour towards women over several decades made by the BBC’s Panorama documentary in early June, though he stepped down from his role on the eve of the broadcast “to avoid disruption to the club while he addresses the matter privately”.

Even before those allegations became public, Sullivan was a lightning rod, lambasted for his stewardship of a club in vertiginous decline since winning the Europa Conference League in May 2023. The £100m fee received for Declan Rice that summer was frittered away. Fellow Prague hero Jarrod Bowen, the club captain, has pledged to stay on, tasked with leading the club back up.

Until his defenestration Sullivan had acted as the club’s de facto director of football, often to the frustration of those in the football department. His chief ally, Karren Brady, stepped down in April as storm clouds gathered, severing a working relationship that dated as far back as 1990.

Among the club’s support, 50,000 season tickets have been sold for the attempt at re-entry to the Premier League. The overriding desire among fans is for Sullivan to completely depart the scene. His announced departure had installed a modicum of optimism.

Potential new sheriffs are circling but the picture is complicated, any future direction opaque as a result. As Sullivan stepped down the expectation was that Daniel Kretinsky, the Czech billionaire owner of Royal Mail who has owned 27% of West Ham since 2021, would make his move. Instead, this week, he cut that share down to just under 25%, though this was part of a strategy.

Last weekend, the familiar face of Amanda Staveley entered the picture. In July 2024 she departed Newcastle, after her leading role in bringing in the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, but now Staveley wants to return to football. Last September, she was linked with a takeover at Tottenham, and it is suggested she will use a similar source of funding to engineer her move for West Ham. Among Newcastle fans, with their club faltering this summer, Staveley’s energy is lamented. With her connections, some Hammers fan hope she could have a similar galvanising effect.

View image in fullscreen David Sullivan’s closet ally, Karren Brady, left the club in April. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

The key is the 25% that belonged to the late David Gold, Sullivan’s former joint-chair. As Staveley loomed, Kretinsky appeared ready to take up his first refusal on purchasing that 25% from Vanessa Gold, David’s daughter and current co-chair. Adding that to his 27% would take him beyond 50.1%, leaving him liable for a formal takeover offer. But shifting 2% to a Czech ally, the entrepreneur Jakub Havrlant, now means he would be short of that obligation should he cut across Staveley’s ambitions by buying Gold’s stake. Sullivan’s shares also hold the balance of power and Staveley’s next move is keenly awaited.

While that plays out, what of football? The arrival of free agent, the former Brighton and Ajax defender, Joël Veltman, was the first addition of a summer where the sales of Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham and Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal fetched a collective £140m, commensurate to a year of Premier League TV money. Youth product Freddie Potts’ departure to Club Brugge for £10m disappointed some fans. Needs must if further players are to arrive. There is interest in Ireland’s World Cup playoff hero Troy Parrott, the striker at AZ Alkmaar, though attracting players to the Championship has its difficulties.

View image in fullscreen West Ham have cashed in on key players, such as Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham, to cushion their descent into the Championship. Photograph: Phil Walter/Getty Images

In the dugout remains Nuno Espírito Santo, who stayed when his departure had been expected. Nuno’s zen-like calm is required at a club where panic regularly sets in. The vacuum created by Sullivan’s situation, relegation and lack of transfer business heightens anxieties. A new season has arrived, with uninviting league fixtures against Burnley, Charlton, Watford and Wolves by 1 September. Karim Virani, previously a club employee who departed in 2020, more recently at Glasgow Rangers, has returned as interim chief executive. Attempts are being made to stitch West Ham into a semblance of unity.

This summer, the London Stadium played host to concerts from Take That and Metallica, and staged the Diamond League athletics meet in July, where Josh Kerr broke the world mile record. Thursday saw a bid confirmed to stage the 2029 World Athletics Championships, following an impasse between the club and the stadium owners. Further reminders that West Ham’s home will never be fully their own, 10 years after departing the Boleyn Ground.

Such were the terms Sullivan, Gold Sr and Brady agreed for a stadium that fans continue to resent, where Sullivan is unlikely to be made to feel welcome.

Sports.title: Lucy Bronze backs Uefa’s stance on boycotting Fifa for ‘good of the game’
Sports.content:
Lucy Bronze has backed Uefa’s stance on boycotting all Fifa competitions for the “good of the game” and to safeguard football for future generations.

On Thursday Europe’s governing body doubled down on its threat – including next summer’s Women’s World Cup – amid the furore surrounding the Fifa president Gianni Infantino and his shelved plan for a privately funded Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.

“The message that we stand by … is ‘for the good of the game’. The players who play in those competitions, the European players, we stand by our beliefs and what the right thing is for our game,” the 34-year-old Chelsea and England right-back said.

Bronze was speaking before Saturday’s pre-season friendly against Auckland FC at Eden Park. She was responding to a question by the New Zealand Herald whether it would be disappointing not to play in Fifa competitions.

She added: “If that means boycotting competitions, then that has to happen. It’s for the future of the game and not just for me today and tomorrow, it’s for all the little girls or little boys who come after us to make sure that they’re in a good place, when the game is moving forward in decades to come, not just tomorrow.”

Next summer’s tournament in Brazil could be the England defender’s fourth senior World Cup. The Lionesses have reached at least the semi-finals of her previous three. Her first global competition coincidentally came in New Zealand, when she helped England reach the semi-finals of the 2008 Under-17 Women’s World Cup.

Uefa’s threat of a boycott could have an impact on September’s Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland which is set to get under way in under a month’s time, with England due to line up in Group B alongside Brazil, Canada and Tanzania.

Meanwhile, Channel 4 has confirmed it will air the knockout stages of the Women’s African Cup of Nations live, with the quarter-finals and semi-finals to be streamed on its YouTube channel. The final to be shown live on E4. It will mark the first time that a UK broadcaster has shown the tournament live.

Elsewhere, the Football Association has appointed Sian Massey-Ellis as its new senior manager for women referees. Massey-Ellis became only the second woman to join the Premier League officials list in 2010 and has officiated at 150 top-flight matches, as well as five Women’s FA Cup finals. She was first female to officiate in a men’s FA Cup final.

Sports.title: Norway’s Klaveness tells Fifa president Infantino to resign: ‘There is no trust now’
Sports.content:
The Norwegian FA will ask Gianni Infantino to resign with immediate effect after his doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Norway is the first federation to call directly for the Fifa president to step down after a series of controversies that came to a head with the crisis engulfing his Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.

The decision was made at a meeting of the Norwegian Football Federation board (NFF) on Thursday night. Norway has consistently taken a lead in efforts to scrutinise Fifa’s governance and recent events have taken any faith in its leadership beyond the point of no return.

“We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now,” the NFF president, Lise Klaveness, told the Guardian. “We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in a worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

“We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”

The NFF is expected to formally write a letter requesting Infantino’s resignation in the coming week. Norway was among a handful of countries not to back his re-election as president next March, although several European federations have withdrawn their endorsement in the past week.

“We understand that we’re one country, but it’s our position,” Klaveness said. “It’s just one step further for us. We did not vote for him in 2023 but we hoped we would support him, he was elected and the reason why we were so clear in our statements was to really give the signal that we wanted him to implement the good reforms he was part of. But he didn’t, and now we will ask him to resign.”

The NFF agreed to demand a full review into the package of reforms passed upon Infantino’s ascent to the presidency in 2016, which were intended to extricate Fifa from the corruption crisis that had previously dogged the governing body. Klaveness said the investigation should ask “what was implemented, what was not, what should have been implemented and what we should also implement to make this a functioning organisation”.

Norway will also formalise a fresh complaint to Fifa’s ethics committee on three fronts, taking in the FFE scandal, the award of Fifa’s peace prize to Donald Trump and the Folarin Balogun affair at the World Cup. It will attempt to bring a number of major European federations on board for its submission in an effort to further increase the pressure on Infantino.

“We want the ethics committee to show their work transparently because this is a very big part of the issue,” Klaveness said. “There are all kinds of control mechanisms in place but they are not really holding the council and president accountable.”

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino leaves after attending the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations match between Malawi and Zambia in Rabat. Photograph: AP

In June, the NFF wrote to the ethics committee supporting a complaint by the advocacy group FairSquare, which centred on alleged breaches of political neutrality by Infantino. It will now make a new submission that asks for the three situations to be considered individually. “We will join them in one letter but they are very different cases and we want the ethical committee to treat them separately,” Klaveness said.

The NFF is understood to have particular concerns that the timing of Infantino’s FFE offer, which promised federations significant financial gains if accepted, may constitute an abuse of position at this proximity to a presidential election. It has also been observed that the FFE scheme, had it been passed, would have locked in commitments extending well beyond Infantino’s term.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to The Recap The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

As with its call for Infantino to step down, Norway is the first federation to adopt a public stance regarding the peace prize or the Balogun case. Fifa’s decision to suspend the USA striker’s red card during the World Cup, meaning he was free to face Belgium in the last 16, came after Trump had called Infantino to discuss the ban.

Uefa’s federations have stood together in backing a potential boycott of Fifa competitions, a stance Uefa reasserted on Thursday despite Infantino’s shelving of FFE. Klaveness said the move is not merely symbolic and is intended to bring swift results.

“There’s no point in Uefa standing in a war position for half a year,” she said. “That would not be good at all. Now it’s crucial that we do it because global football cooperation is at stake. It’s very good to see we have strong leadership in Uefa that knows now is crunch time for this case. We cannot sell out this core of football.”

The first competition in line for a boycott would be the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, which is due to start in Poland on 5 September, but Klaveness expects the continued turmoil to have been resolved by then.

“I hope and think it will not come to that,” she said. “A lot of water will go under the bridge before that. But this is why we ask Infantino to resign. It’s so unstable now that it’s a matter of time. He cannot recover this and we cannot put the sport on the spot. The biggest priority is to be together with Uefa and have this strong position.”

Klaveness and the NFF have held a consistent line in calling for scrutiny of Fifa’s operations since she assumed her position in March 2022. She has been vocal on human rights issues and governance standards within Fifa, criticising failings surrounding the Qatar World Cup and questioning the process that awarded Saudi Arabia the 2034 edition of the tournament.

Sports.title: England striker Ivan Toney charged with assault after Soho nightclub incident
Sports.content:
The England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged with assault after an incident at a nightclub in Soho in December last year.

Scotland Yard said the striker had been charged on 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm. Toney, who plays for the Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, is due to appear at Westminster magistrates court on 24 September.

The Sun newspaper reported in December that Toney had been arrested after an alleged head-butt. It claimed a fan recognised the footballer and grabbed at him while seeking a photograph with him before the incident.

On Friday the Metropolitan police said the charges related to an incident on 6 December at a nightclub on Wardour Street in central London, reportedly the now-closed 100 Wardour Street.

A spokesperson for Toney said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

Toney was at the centre of one of the most curious transfers on deadline day in August 2024 when he completed a late move from Brentford to Al-Ahli worth a reported £40m. He has also played for Newcastle United and his home town club Northampton Town, as well as several others on loan as he looked to establish himself.

Seen as a late bloomer in football terms, he had made only two Premier League appearances before his 25th birthday, but went on to score 67 goals in 128 appearances over the next three seasons at the top level.

He has played 10 times for England, scoring once in a friendly match against Belgium in 2024, and was part of the 2026 World Cup squad, making appearances against Argentina in the semi-final and in the win over France as England finished third.

Sports.title: Former Tottenham star Andros Townsend joins 17th club of his career - after his bizarre diet made him a viral sensation during the World Cup
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham star Andros Townsend joins 17th club of his career - after his bizarre diet made him a viral sensation during the World Cup

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Spurs star Andros Townsend has joined the 17th club of his career after signing for a team in the top-flight in Thailand.

Townsend, 34, has joined PT Prachuap after leaving fellow Thai side Kanchanaburi Power, who play in the second tier.

'The Thai adventure continues,' he wrote on Instagram.

PT Prachuap – based in Prachuap Khiri Khan province, 150 miles south of Bangkok – appeared to have leaked Townsend's imminent arrival two weeks ago, when they asked if anyone had a three-bedroom house available for the player to live in.

Townsend made 29 appearances for Kanchanaburi Power last season, scoring three goals.

He has previously played for Spurs, Newcastle, Palace and Everton, and moved to Thailand after a short spell with Turkish side Antalyaspor.

Andros Townsend has signed for Thai Premier League side PT Prachuap, the 17th club of his career

Townsend making the move comes after he worked for ITV as a co-commentator during the World Cup.

The ex-England winger went viral at the tournament for his unconventional diet – which includes eating raw steak.

He released a slew of videos promoting his all-natural diet including the steak, sardines and boiled eggs on a plane.

Townsend's aim was to stay healthy while staying in hotels throughout the tournament, while being denied access to cooking facilities and facing the constant temptation of fast food. 'Never let your circumstances dictate your health,' he says.

Townsend claims to have been eating raw meat for four years, dating back to his time when he was in the Premier League and would have had access to industry-leading dietary advice.

Townsend went viral during the World Cup for his bizarre diet, which includes eating raw meat

The former England and Tottenham star enjoys tucking into boiled eggs on his flights

Eating raw meat is a risk. There is potential for it to be contaminated with harmful bacteria, such as E. coli or Salmonella, or parasites.

There are 'safer' versions of raw meat, such as whole cuts, which restrict the chance for bacteria to get inside compared to ground meat. However, the bacteria can still exist on the surface.

Townsend says he has not had any health issues from consuming raw meat and defends his diet on the basis that he gets more nutrients.

Some nutrients, such as Vitamin B1, Vitamin B6, and Vitamin B12, can be partially degraded in cooking and so raw meat retains a higher concentration of them.

Sports.title: Newcastle identify former Tottenham midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg as the man to replace Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali
Sports.content:
Newcastle identify former Tottenham midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg as the man to replace Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali

Follow all today's transfer developments with Window Watch HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Newcastle United are interested in former Tottenham midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg.

The experienced Danish international has been identified as someone who could help smooth the transition from losing Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali from their midfield.

Though far from the headline signing Newcastle fans would have been hoping for, the 31-year-old knows the Premier League well and could provide the steadying hand for their two young additions Sean Steur, 18, and Aladji Bamba, 20.

Hojbjerg has 97 caps for Denmark and has been performing consistently well for Marseille. Newcastle had previously tried to sign him in 2022 from Tottenham for £30million.

He joined Marseille permanently last year, after an initial loan, for £17million and worked under Spurs boss Roberto de Zerbi. He has gone on to make 75 appearances and score eight goals for the French side in all competitions.

Newcastle sport director Ross Wilson has been working through an extensive list of names but at least knows that Hojbjerg could hit the ground running and provide Matthias Jaissle with another experienced head in the dressing room.

Newcastle have identified Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg (pictured) as their replacement for Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali

Newcastle have previously enquired about Lucas Bergvall at Tottenham, Felix Nmecha at Dortmund and Angelo Stiller of Stuttgart as they try to find the right blend for their midfield.

Guimaraes, 28, has been sold for £75million this week and will be confirmed as an Arsenal player over the weekend.

Wilson said: 'We didn't want to sell him. It was a world record fee for a player his age.

'What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, effectively told us he wanted to leave and move on.

'That doesn’t mean he can go but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. But there’s no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer — it wasn’t.

'But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen. It might have been in our plan to sign one player but we didn’t get him so we move on to another. We can only be honest about that.'

Sports.title: Freddie Flintoff leaves England Lions coaching job: Cricket legend announces departure after two-year stint - with role 'saving' him after life-changing Top Gear crash
Sports.content:
Andrew Flintoff has stepped down as head coach of England Lions after nearly two years to focus on his new role at Australia’s Sydney Thunder franchise in the Big Bash League.

Flintoff, who also plans to spend more time on his TV career and with his family, was not in the running to replace Brendon McCullum as England’s Test coach, and faced a potential clash between his Thunder and Lions work.

The 47-year-old, one of England's greatest and most popular cricketers of all-time, took charge of his country's second string team in September 2024 and previously credited the role with 'saving' him after his near-fatal Top Gear crash.

Flintoff was hailed for creating an impressive environment and helping to develop several talented young players, yet he is leaving the job with immediate effect.

He said: 'Unfortunately I’ve made the decision to step away from my role with the Lions.

'Not only have I enjoyed my time having the opportunity to work with the best young cricketers in the country, but have taken great pride in seeing them develop.

Andrew 'Freddie' Flintoff has stepped away from his role as England Lions head coach

Flintoff (pictured with former Test head coach Brendon McCullum) was praised for his work

'I’d like to thank the coaches and staff for all their passion, tireless work and support they give everyday.

'In particular, Ed Barney who I’ve loved working with and was so lucky to have as a performance director, and obviously Rob (Key) for trusting me with one of the most important roles in English cricket.

'I can’t wait to get started with the Thunder later in the year and see where coaching takes me.'

Flintoff's time with the Lions was the latest step on his coaching journey following his return to the game after his life-changing crash while filming Top Gear in December 2022.

Flintoff was airlifted to hospital after the incident having suffered serious facial and rib injuries before he faced a lengthy period recovering, where he initially refused to leave his house except for medical appointments.

Flintoff previously had little involvement in cricket following his retirement in 2010, focusing instead on a hugely successful TV career.

He joined the England Lions having also coached Northern Superchargers in The Hundred. Flintoff similarly spent time around England's senior team.

Speaking in 2025 on a Disney+ documentary about his career and recovery from the car crash, Flintoff opened up on how important his return to the sport had been.

'This sounds awful: part of me thinks I should have been killed,' he said. 'Part of me thinks I wish I had died. I didn’t want to kill myself, I won’t mistake the two things.

'I wasn’t wishing, I was thinking: that would have been so much easier. Now I try to take the attitude, you know what, the sun will come up tomorrow, and my kids will still give me a hug. I feel in a better place now.

'If one thing’s come out of it which is positive it’s being back in cricket. It’s probably the one thing that saved me.

'I’ve been welcomed back into that fold. It’s such a good place. I feel it’s safe. I have moments when I’m sat in a dressing room and I’m watching a game of cricket surrounded by cricketers and friends, and I’m able to forget.'

Flintoff (pictured in 2018) was involved in a near-fatal car crash while filming Top Gear

In the press release announcing his exit from the Lions, the ECB's performance director Ed Barney added: 'Fred has helped to transform the Lions environment into a programme that has had a major impact on young players.

'By creating an environment that both supports and pushes excellence at all times he has helped bring forward a new generation of young players.

'Coaches have also flourished alongside him, whether early in their coaching journey or with decades of experience, and he has consistently maximised the expertise around the group.

'We wish him the best in the next stage of his coaching career and look forward to a time he returns to the English game.'

The former England and Sussex all-rounder Mike Yardy will step in to take charge of next week’s four-day match at Beckenham between Pakistan and a Professional County Club Select XI.

Sports.title: Lucy Bronze becomes the first England footballer to back FIFA boycott as pressure mounts on Gianni Infantino: 'It is for the good of the game'
Sports.content:
England defender Lucy Bronze has become the first footballer from the nation to publicly back UEFA's potential World Cup boycott if Gianni Infantino doesn't leave FIFA.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Thursday that UEFA would maintain its boycott of the competition until the controversial chief is removed from his position.

European football's governing body issued a statement reiterating that it had lost confidence in the FIFA president in the wake of his aborted World Cup sell-off.

UEFA previously said that Infantino's proposal would have to be withdrawn and that it would need assurances that such 'attempts to disfigure the game this way will never be made again' before it lifted its self-imposed ban.

However, it is believed that – as things stand – anything less than Infantino's head would not be enough to ensure the likes of champions Spain, England, France and Germany take part in four years' time.

And Bronze has spoken out in support of the movement, with the Women's World Cup set to take place in Brazil next year.

Lucy Bronze (left) has become the first England player to back UEFA's World Cup boycott while Gianni Infantino (right) is in charge of FIFA

Bronze said that a boycott 'has to happen' if it means doing the 'right thing' for football

'The message that we stand by … is "for the good of the game",' England regular Bronze said via The Guardian. 'The players who play in those competitions, the European players, we stand by our beliefs and what the right thing is for our game.

'If that means boycotting competitions, then that has to happen. It's for the future of the game and not just for me today and tomorrow, it's for all the little girls or little boys who come after us to make sure that they're in a good place, when the game is moving forward in decades to come, not just tomorrow.'

The 2027 World Cup could be Bronze's fourth, though there are currently doubts over whether that competition will go ahead.

On Wednesday night, FIFA announced Infantino had the backing of members of the body’s council after crisis talks in Morocco.

The beleaguered Swiss had summoned officials to his hotel as part of what appears to be, for now, a successful attempt to cling to power.

He had faced a major backlash since plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup emerged but amid widespread outrage and opposition, those plans were dumped. Following the hotel summit FIFA issued a statement saying execs had given their 'full support' to Infantino while acknowledging 'mistakes' in the dropped plan.

FIFA said they have now apologised in a letter to the various football associations and that a ‘review’ will be carried out.

UEFA’s initial statement on Saturday had branded Infantino's proposal to flog commercial and event operations as a ‘shabby, back room, opaque deal’.

UEFA repeated that it has lost confidence in FIFA president Gianni Infantino and reiterated its threat to boycott the World Cup

After Infantino’s apparent vote of confidence, they added: 'UEFA’s associations were very clear about the conditions attached to their non participation in FIFA competitions.

'First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

'These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino’s presidency. That position holds.

'Yesterday’s announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing.'

Sports.title: Former Man United star Nicky Butt reveals he is BANNED from his local tip after blazing row with staff
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt has revealed he is banned from his local tip following a bizarre row with a member of staff.

Butt, 51, says he got into a blazing confrontation with a worker at the tip who prevented him from entering because he thought his Range Rover was a commercial vehicle as the seats were down.

The former England star claims the attendant then chased him after he defied his orders and drove into the site, thought to be the Woodhouse Lane Recycling Centre in Altrincham.

Butt said on The Good, The Bad and The Football Podcast that the incident had left him 'raging'.

'I've got a lot of c**p from the house, bit of cardboard . . . I missed the bin man last week, so I've got a few smelly bags,' he said.

'So I put the windows down, obviously my seats were down and apparently I'm not going in because of it.

Nicky Butt has revealed he got into a bizarre row with an attendant at his local tip

'He said to me, "Your windows are blacked out because you're sneaking stuff into it, into the tip." And I went, 'No, it's standard, mate''.

Butt added: 'I thought, well, I'm there now, I'm gonna go for it. So I've got up the ramp, I see this bloke getting up . . . trying to chase me up the hill, but he's got his walkie-talkie out.

'So I've literally got up the top, throw all the bags out, and I'm going back down the hill, and he's going mad at me. Anyway, I'm banned from the tip.'

Butt appears on the podcast with former Man United team-mate Paul Scholes, and comedian and television presenter Paddy McGuinness.

The ex-United stars have caused controversy on the show after being criticised for their opinions on Lisandro Martinez.

Butt won the Champions League, six Premier League titles and three FA Cups at Old Trafford. He left in the summer of 2004 to join Newcastle in a deal worth £2.5million.

Since his retirement, Butt has been chief executive of League Two side Salford City and also served as head of Man United's academy for five years.

Sports.title: Newcastle did NOT want to sell £75m Bruno Guimaraes - but 'very emotional' captain asked to leave for Arsenal, reveals transfer chief
Sports.content:
Newcastle did NOT want to sell £75m Bruno Guimaraes - but 'very emotional' captain asked to leave for Arsenal, reveals transfer chief

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson says the club 'didn't want to sell' captain Bruno Guimaraes.

The 28-year-old midfielder is set to leave the Magpies and join Arsenal for a fee of £75million, although confirmation of the move has not been officially announced yet.

Guimaraes' seemingly impending departure comes following a tough summer for Newcastle, who have already seen Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali exit during the transfer window while head coach Eddie Howe resigned last week, with Matthias Jaissle officially appointed as his replacement on Wednesday.

Speaking to reporters at Newcastle's pre-season training camp in Spain, Wilson said: 'We didn't want to sell Bruno. It wasn't in the plan to sell Bruno. None of us — or ownership — wanted to sell Bruno.

'He's our captain, he was very, very important to us and the debate over his price — it's a world-record fee for a player of his age.

'What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, effectively told us he wanted to leave and move on.

Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson has said the club 'didn't want to sell' captain Bruno Guimaraes (pictured)

'That doesn't mean he can go but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. But there's no point in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer — it wasn't.

'But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen. It might have been in our plan to sign one player but we didn't get him so we move on to another. We can only be honest about that.'

Sports.title: Revealed: Defiant David Sullivan believes he is being 'bullied' into staying away from West Ham stadium as owner, 77 - who is accused of sexual misconduct - prepares to face crowd after explosive Panorama allegations
Sports.content:
Revealed: Defiant David Sullivan believes he is being 'bullied' into staying away from West Ham stadium as owner, 77 - who is accused of sexual misconduct - prepares to face crowd after explosive Panorama allegations

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

David Sullivan plans to defy advice to stay away from West Ham’s first home game of the season because the club’s co-owner, accused of multiple counts of sexual misconduct, feels he is being ‘bullied’ into missing it, Daily Mail Sport understands.

The 77-year-old, the club’s largest shareholder, resigned as co-chair in June ahead of the airing of a BBC Panorama and Times investigation in which seven women accused Sullivan of predatory behaviour, which he strongly denies.

The operators of the London Stadium recommended to West Ham that Sullivan not attend the match against Portsmouth in the Carabao Cup on Saturday over fears of potential fan unrest while the club’s fan advisory board said his presence would cause ‘offence and upset’.

That feeling is shared by insiders who believed the 77-year-old’s resignation would signal a fresh start for the club, with many staggered that Sullivan plans to be there. One staff member told Daily Mail Sport they had planned to attend the Portsmouth game but would now stay away due to the ‘circus’ and added that the club ‘cannot be serious about wanting to do well if this is what is planned for the season ahead.’

Sullivan is understood not to have made a final decision but sources close to the co-owner told Daily Mail Sport that he’s worried about the state of the team and lack of transfer activity heading into their first season in the Championship in 14 years and feels he needs to watch the game live. They also said Sullivan feels he’s being ‘bullied' by 'keyboard warriors’ into staying away.

Sullivan was accused in June of preying on a string of women, some in their teens, during his time as a newspaper chief stretching back to the 1980s as seven women came forward to give detailed accounts of predatory behaviour they had experienced, including pressuring them for sex or oral sex by suggesting it would help their careers. Sullivan described the allegations as ‘factually incorrect and entirely false’.

David Sullivan believes he is being 'bullied' into staying away from West Ham amid allegations of sexual misconduct

Sources close to Sullivan also claimed he’s received numerous messages from fans urging him to attend despite his presence at matches last season sparking continued protests from spectators against his ownership, including marches, boycotts, sit-ins, black balloons and thousands of fans brandishing red cards.

The Panorama investigation revealed that Sullivan had been banned from contact with West Ham women’s and youth teams for the past three years.

London Stadium’s operator has asked to be made aware of any planned Sullivan visits so it can implement its own safety measures. West Ham are said to have told the operator that it does not consider there to be an ongoing safeguarding risk associated with Sullivan attending the stadium.

Until recently, it appeared as though Sullivan’s grip on West Ham was loosening when it was announced in June that Vanessa Gold, daughter of former co-owner David, had agreed to sell part of their stake in the club to fellow shareholder Daniel Kretinsky. The move that would have seen the Czech billionaire overtake Sullivan as leading shareholder.

Last week, however, a new announcement confirmed that Gold had accepted a new offer from a consortium led by former Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley for her shares. Staveley agreed to buy a 25.1 per cent stake for £150million, which values the club at around £600million, and would still leave Sullivan as the leading stakeholder.

Staveley, though, has reportedly also made an offer to Sullivan, who is believed to be open to selling his stake in the club but values it at much more.

Sports.title: Man Utd contacted by Newcastle after launching Lewis Hall transfer enquiry
Sports.content:
Man Utd contacted by Newcastle after launching Lewis Hall transfer enquiry

Newcastle have sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer, with Bruno Guimaraes also set to leave, and attention has now turned to Manchester United target Lewis Hall

View 2 Images Newcastle don't want to sell Lewis Hall (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Newcastle have made it clear to Manchester United that Lewis Hall is not for sale this summer at any price. United are keen to sign a left-back in this window and have kept an eye on Hall for some time, but it seems Michael Carrick won't get his man this summer.

‌



United prioritised central midfield in the early stages of the window, with Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos arriving from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively for a combined £87million.

‌



Left-back is now a position on the agenda, with Carrick wanting competition for Luke Shaw, who impressed last season but has a chequered injury history. Academy graduate Harry Amass would be allowed to leave for the right price, while last summer's signing Diego Leon has failed to kick on so far and Tyrell Malacia left on a free transfer.

‌



Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui can both play left-back if needed, but Patrick Dorgu has shone further forward, convincing United to go back into the market.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

United thought they could take advantage of the turmoil at Newcastle this summer, with Eddie Howe being replaced by Matthias Jaissle. But the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and the pending exit of Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal has worked against them.

‌



Sky Sports reports that Newcastle have told United in no uncertain terms to look elsewhere. The Magpies first communicated their stance two weeks ago and consider the matter to be settled.

Newcastle's hierarchy are under pressure to steady the ship following the exits of Howe, Gordon, Tonali and Guimaraes. Sporting director Ross Wilson has taken the approach of publicly explaining the £75m sale of Guimaraes to Arsenal.

"What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, he effectively told us he wanted to leave and move on," he said.

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes' exit has strengthened Newcastle's stance on Lewis Hall (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"That doesn't mean he can go, but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. There's no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer - it wasn't. But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen."

Unlike Guimaraes, Hall is not agitating for a move. The 21-year-old joined Newcastle for £35m from Chelsea three summers ago and has been a regular fixture on the left side of defence.

Article continues below

With Hall appearing to be a dead end, United could turn their attention to Racing Santander's Jorge Salinas, who is considered to be a viable alternative. The 19-year-old is highly rated and has a €16m (£13.7m) release clause, although United could face competition from Barcelona. Bologna's Jhon Lucumi, who is valued at €25m (£21.7m) is another option.

Sports.title: FA announce changes after tragic death of ex-Arsenal footballer aged 21
Sports.content:
FA announce changes after tragic death of ex-Arsenal footballer aged 21

Former Arsenal youngster Billy Vigar suffered a significant brain injury back in September last year, with changes now being put in place by the Football Association

View 2 Images Billy Vigar passed away in September (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

The Football Association (FA) have announced that solid walls around the perimeter of pitches have been banned following the tragic death of Billy Vigar. The former Arsenal youth player died from a head injury after colliding with a wall last season.

The incident occurred with Vigar playing for Chichester City against Wingate & Finchley FC back in September. The 21-year-old collided with a concrete wall surrounding the pitch, resulting in a significant brain injury.

Vigar was part of Arsenal’s youth sides before moving to Hastings United in 2024. He signed with Chichester City last summer, a few months before his death.

The wall at Wingate & Finchley FC has now been removed, with the FA confirming a review of pitch surroundings for non-league grounds . The findings of the review have now been released.

It has been confirmed that the FA: "no longer permits solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers around pitches across the National League system for men [steps 1-6], and the Women's National League [tiers 3-4]".

UEFA could boycott 5 tournaments in next 11 months after new Gianni Infantino statement READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Article continues below

In a statement, the FA added: "Any existing solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers must be removed as soon as reasonably practicable, or covered with suitable protection if they cannot be removed for structural reasons. We have informed the clubs at this level that will be required to take action as a result of these changes.

"Matches may continue to be played at affected grounds during this period; however, clubs should assess the safety of their pitch perimeter barriers on an ongoing basis, and where alterations to these structures have been recommended during this review, they should develop a plan to complete any such alterations within a reasonable timeframe."

Non-league clubs will be helped with funding the changes with the money coming from both the FA and the Premier League. The Press Association reports that 160 of the 900 clubs who play at the levels have been contacted over changes that will have to be made to their stadiums.

View 2 Images The FA have announced changes following the youngster's tragic death (Image: Getty Images)

The FA added: "The initial phase of the programme is already underway, and we will continue to provide full support to the clubs involved in this process.”

Following the announcement, a PFA spokesperson said: “Following the tragic death of Billy Vigar last year, we again highlighted these concerns and made clear our view that the lack of progress and leadership on this issue had been unacceptable.

"As part of working groups set up by the FA following Billy's death, we pushed for the FA's Stadium Accreditation criteria to be amended to ban these types of walls so that there is a clear and centralised policy for clubs to follow.

"Given that, it's a welcome step that the FA's regulations have now been changed to reflect that position.

"However, it will now be important for progress on the removal of such walls - and effective mitigation of risks ahead of their removal - to be properly monitored, and for clubs to be given the support they need so that these changes can happen as soon as possible. Player safety must always come first."

Sports.title: Meet the University of Birmingham student seeking European Athletics Championships glory on his home track
Sports.content:
Meet the University of Birmingham student seeking European Athletics Championships glory on his home track

Jake Minshull trains on the Alexander Stadium track three times a week, providing him with local knowledge he hopes to be able to use to his advantage when he takes on the best the continent has to offer.

View Image Jake Minshull celebrates winning 400m hurdles silver in the Commonwealth Games

Rising star Jake Minshull is out to show there is no place like home at next week’s European Athletics Championships in Birmingham.

‌



The 21-year-old 400m hurdler is currently studying for a human sciences degree in the second city and hails from nearby Coventry. He trains on the Alexander Stadium track three times a week, providing him with local knowledge he hopes to be able to use to his advantage when he takes on the best the continent has to offer.

‌



He said: “It pretty much feels like a home event and it feels like I know the place pretty well. I know what the weather is going to be like there. I'm ready for it. In my second year [of university], I was finding it quite full on with all the training and found myself running from one thing to the other, so I split my third year.

‌



“I'm organised and I do quite well in putting certain efforts in one bit and then applying myself in another section. It probably takes a certain type of person to do both to a high level.”

Minshull won 4x400m bronze at the World Relay Championships in May and added to his burgeoning reputation at the recent Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, picking up a 400m hurdles silver medal he ‘wasn’t meant to get’.

‌



Minshull said: “It was pretty surreal. I've been training for moments like that and to get one is pretty special. In my head I thought I could get a medal, but there's a bit of a difference between thinking it and actually doing it.

“It's given me a big confidence boost ready for Europeans. I definitely want to get a few more moments like that. I wasn't meant to get a medal at Commonwealths, so let’s see if we can do the same at Euros.”

Chief among his rivals will be Germany’s Emil Agyekum and Norway’s Olympic champion and world record holder Karsten Warholm. Minshull, part of a 98-strong Novuna GB & NI squad in Birmingham, said: “It's a pretty stacked field. It's mad how many guys there are in this event at the time.

Article continues below

“The obvious one to look at is Karsten. I like to think that I'm a similar athlete to him in the way that our stride patterns work and how we attack a race. It would be pretty cool if I could race him.”

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca wants Chelsea star to replace Rodri as Barcelona move advances
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca wants Chelsea star to replace Rodri as Barcelona move advances

Barcelona have seen an opening bid for Manchester City midfielder Rodi turned down on Friday - but the La Liga giants are expected to return as they close in on the World Cup winner

View 3 Images Barcelona have launched an opening offer for Man City midfielder Rodri

Enzo Maresca has earmarked Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez as his top option to replace Rodri this summer.

‌



Barcelona have seen an opening offer of £38.5million rejected out of hand by City, who want closer to £60m. However, with just one year remaining on his contract and coming off a serious knee injury, City are open to selling at the right price.

‌



And Maresca, who is going into his first season as Pep Guardiola ’s replacement, sees Fernandez as the perfect replacement for the World Cup Golden Ball winner.

‌



The Italian worked with Fernandez during his time as Chelsea boss and according to the Independent, City are already exploring a possible move for the Argentinian.

Inside Bruno Guimaraes' dream Arsenal transfer six years in making for Mikel Arteta READ MORE :

Fernandez is yet to report for Chelsea this summer after playing a huge role in Argentina’s rollercoaster ride to the World Cup final. The 25-year-old scored crucial goals in the knockout stages, including a screamer in the dramatic comeback against England in the semis.

However, he arguably cost his nation the chance of lifting a fourth world title after he inexplicably picked up two yellow cards in a matter of minutes.

‌



Chelsea paid £106m for the midfielder in 2023 and would want to make a profit on that, if they were to entertain an exit this summer.

Fernandez was sanctioned earlier this year after his desire to leave the London club was made public. Ex-boss Liam Rosenior was also forced to strip him of the vice captaincy before he was sacked for a disastrous run of results.

View 3 Images Chelsea want a reported £120m for Enzo Fernandez (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

‌



New Blues boss Xabi Alonso hasn’t been able to train with the talismanic midfielder during his short tenure, but made it clear he wants him to remain at the club.

Speaking in July, Alonso said: "Yes we have spoken. But as you can imagine what we have spoken remains private,” and then when pressed if he wanted Fernandez to stay, he replied “yes”.

City have already smashed their own transfer record this summer, signing Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for a whopping £116m. But with the exit of Bernardo Silva and the expected one of Rodri, more cover is required before the Premier League campaign begins.

‌



They have also been heavily linked with Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, who shone at the World Cup with Morocco, but his £86m valuation has led talks to an impasse.

View 3 Images Enzo Maresca worked with Fernandez during his time as Chelsea boss

Speaking after City’s most recent pre-season friendly, Maresca admitted the club still had work to do in order to replace a number of senior players.

‌



“Fortunately this is a squad that doesn’t need to do many things,” he told media at a press conference ahead of Wednesday’s clash with K-League All Stars.

“At the same time, we already know the squad lost some important players with experience with Bernardo, John [Stones], Nathan [Ake]…different players. For sure, there are things we need to do.

He added: “The reason I said there are things to do is because the transfer window is open and when it is open, anything can happen. It is August and then from September, when it’s closed, it is completely different.”

Sports.title: Man Utd legends called out by former team-mate as Roy Keane in firing line
Sports.content:
Man Utd legends called out by former team-mate as Roy Keane in firing line

Roy Keane and several other Manchester United legends have been called out by a fellow Red Devils hero

View 3 Images Javier Hernandez has called out his former team-mates for criticising Michael Carrick

Roy Keane, Gary Neville and Paul Scholes have been called out by their former Manchester United team-mate Javier Hernandez for comments about Michael Carrick. Carrick did a remarkable job at the helm after being appointed as United’s interim head coach back in January.

‌



He managed to secure a third place Premier League finish and qualification to the Champions League, which was largely unthinkable under his predecessor Ruben Amorim earlier in the season. That has since seen the 45-year-old be appointed as the club’s permanent head coach ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

‌



Yet, while many United fans and, evidently, the club have been pleased with Carrick’s tenure up to now, the former Red Devils midfielder has faced considerable criticism from the same people he shared a dressing room with during his 12-year stint as a player at Old Trafford.

‌



Roy Keane seemingly holds some bitterness towards Carrick, having made personal jibes, while Paul Scholes took to social media to have a dig at his former midfield partner following a loss to Newcastle. Gary Neville also cast doubt over Carrick's credentials for the role.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd finally announce sixth summer transfer as statement confirms next steps READ MORE :

Recently appearing on Rio Ferdinand Presents, Hernandez was asked for his thoughts about Carrick being at the helm and replied: "I love it, I love it.” Ferdinand then pointed out that several of the pair's former team-mates had been far less complimentary about Carrick.

‌



"I don’t know why. I really don’t know why. There’s a fine line between criticising someone’s job, because you have to, and then your own opinions," replied Hernandez.

"I’m very surprised, mostly because you know Carrick more than I do. You spent so much time with him, not only as a teammate at the club but also with the national team. Carrick was always a man who never had a problem with anyone.

View 3 Images Roy Keane has made some harsh comments about Carrick (Image: ITV)

‌



"The most civilised, calm person. So I don’t understand. How are you going to criticise a manager who is giving you results?

"He put your team back into the Champions League, so he deserves the consequence of that: stay, try to bring him players and give him the project. If it doesn’t work, it doesn’t work. But he took the team from low and put the team back into the Champions League."

Hernandez also spoke openly about his departure from United in 2015, admitting he felt the club had changed following the exits of Sir Alex Ferguson and David Gill in 2013.

‌



View 3 Images Michael Carrick has transformed Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

He said: "It was very hard. Because if you gave me the chance to stay at United for most of my career, I would have taken it. The team that I played the most games for, even more than my hometown team in Mexico, is United.

"I would have taken a bullet for that team. It’s my team, Manchester United. But things weren’t the same. It’s not that I left the club that I was with; I left a different environment. It wasn’t the same club.

Article continues below

"With the departure, obviously, of Sir Alex Ferguson, but also David Gill and all that family structure. When I say family, it doesn’t mean that it was all nice, but there were values.

"I was very sad. Don’t get me wrong. I would have retired at United and I would take a bullet for that team. But it wasn’t the same team as the team that embraced me and gave me my first opportunity."

Sports.title: Arsenal star's gesture to Bruno Guimaraes ahead of £75m transfer comes to light
Sports.content:
Arsenal star's gesture to Bruno Guimaraes ahead of £75m transfer comes to light

Arsenal are preparing to confirm the £75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes after the soon-to-be former Newcastle captain completed his medical - and his shirt number seemingly been leaked

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes will join Arsenal for £75million (Image: Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes is set to wear the No.39 shirt for Arsenal after academy star Louie Copley moved to a new number. Arsenal are preparing to confirm Guimaraes' arrival from Newcastle after the two clubs agreed a fixed fee of £75million to end the transfer saga.

‌



The 28-year-old said his goodbyes at Newcastle's training camp in Spain before completing his medical with Arsenal and signing a four-year contract. His signing still hasn't been announced, although the Gunners have dropped a clear hint on their website.

‌



Copley, who wore the No. 39 shirt in each of Arsenal's first two pre-season friendlies as well as in training sessions, has had his squad number changed to 38. It's a telltale sign that Guimaraes is now a Gunner and has taken his favourite number.

‌



The midfielder has worn 39 throughout his club career, including for former clubs Lyon and Athletico Paranaense. Guimaraes likes to wear the number because his dad's taxi cab in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil was #039.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Inside Bruno Guimaraes' dream Arsenal transfer six years in making for Mikel Arteta READ MORE :

Tottenham respond as Arsenal consider shock transfer for Spurs skipper Cristian Romero READ MORE :

Whether the decision was Copley's is unknown, although he did wear No.38 when captaining Arsenal's under-21 side last season. Unfortunately for Copley, who's just 19 and highly regarded at London Colney, he suffered an injury just minutes after coming on as a half-time substitute during the Gunners' 3-1 loss against Real Betis in a friendly on Wednesday.

‌



Mikel Arteta said post-match: "It doesn't look good, the mechanism is not too positive, the symptoms that he already has either. Let's hope that tomorrow [Thursday] the news is better than we hope."

Guimaraes will become Arsenal's most expensive signing of the summer, with the Gunners having also brought in Christos Tzolis for £34m and Illan Meslier on a free transfer. The Brazilian is expected to partner Declan Rice in midfield once the season gets going.

Who should Arsenal sign next? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Louie Copley's number has been changed on the Arsenal website

By leaving Newcastle, Guimaraes becomes the third key player to depart St James' Park this summer as well as manager Eddie Howe. New Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle said: "I met him quickly, but the decision was already made. It was a nice conversation.

"He's a fantastic player and a great human being. It's tough but for him now it's the next challenge and we need to deal with it at a later stage. We trust the players who are here already, but we will also see some changes."
