World.title: Seven killed after Thai student opens fire at home and school
World.content:
At least seven people have been killed and 23 injured after a 14-year-old boy opened fire at his home and school on the outskirts of Thailand's capital, Bangkok.

The gunman - a student at the Debsirin School in Nonthaburi - killed his grandparents and five teachers before taking his own life, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told reporters. The attacker still had "more than 30 bullets left" when he turned the gun on himself, Anutin added.

Nine of the injured people remain in a critical condition, authorities say.

The shooting - the second at a school in Thailand this year - has renewed pressure on the government for greater action on gun control.

Police were deployed to the scene during the active shooting, which began just after 10:00 local time (03:00 GMT).

National police chief police Gen Kittiratt Phanphet told reporters that forensic officers had found the gunman's shots were quite accurate, with several hitting vital spots on the body.

The prime minister said the attack was "well prepared" with "clear steps and clear goals".

A female seventh grader, still in school uniform, told the BBC she was standing in front of her teacher when the woman was shot.

"She was talking to me when [the gunman] showed up and shot her," she said.

"I couldn't see anything but a [cloud] of dust."

Still in her uniform, with her mother by her side, she explained how the shooter stalked from room to room.

"I had to climb over the school fence to escape with other friends."

Her mother says the girl thought she might die. "[She said] 'I thought I'd never see you again'."

Another student told Reuters news agency that he had thought the sound of gunshots were firecrackers going off.

"There were many shots: bang bang bang. Then it went quiet. Then it started again."

Students and school staff were seen fleeing from the scene, and those waiting outside the Debsirin School looked visibly distraught.

Authorities warned people to stay away from the area and for those trapped in the building to hide and wait for rescuers.

In a post on social media, the school later shared a call for blood donations.

Other schools in the vicinity suspended classes so students could return home early.

World.title: Spain to impose border controls against Italy as row over Ceuta migrant influx intensifies
World.content:
Spain will impose border controls on all air and sea travel from Italy as a row between the two EU countries intensifies.

The measures - coming into force at midnight (22:00 GMT) and lasting for a month - come a week after Italy introduced similar restrictions following an influx of about 78,000 migrants from Morocco into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta.

On Friday, Spain demanded Italy reverse its checks by Sunday. Rome said they would stay until at least 15 August - when, according to it, Spain "expects a new wave of migration" to hit Ceuta.

The crisis has pitted Spain's socialist leader Pedro Sanchez against Italy's conservative leader Giorgia Meloni - who has long called for stricter EU migration rules.

Italy does not share a land border with Spain. Its government said last week that decision to temporarily suspend the âborder-free Schengen arrangement was to prevent any of the migrants who had entered Ceuta from travelling on to Italy.

Madrid dismissed this position, saying it was based on "spurious arguments" that lacked any basis in fact because the migrants who entered Ceuta had no way of entering the Schengen area.

In its response to the Spanish threat earlier on Friday, Italy's government said it would not accept "ultimatums". It added that it did not intend "under any circumstances to reconsider the decision to suspend the application of the Schengen Agreement for third-country nationals arriving from Spain, at least until August 15th and in any case until security and terrorist risks for Italy have been completely eliminated".

Italian officials have said local authorities carrying out checks do "everything possible" to ensure maximum comfort for both Spanish and other European citizens arriving in Italy from Spain.

Rome has also reiterated that Spanish citizens are exempt from additional checks when arriving in Italy, with these extra steps only for non-EU residents.

However, El Pais reported that several airport terminals have seen long queues and waiting times in recent days, with passengers arriving from Spain directed to a specific line for checks.

The counter-measures Madrid decided to impose on Friday would include passport, nationality and visa checks for Italian passengers and visitors from other countries arriving from Italy "amid the persistent irregular migratory pressure" the country was experiencing, a statement from Spain's government said.

Checks would stay in place until 7 September "unless a change in the circumstances that led to its adoption warrants modifying that period".

World.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign defence pact
World.content:
Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan have signed a joint defence agreement, saying an attack on one of them would be seen as an attack on all three.

The pact was announced at a meeting between Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in the Saudi city of Mecca.

After the US and Israel attacked Iran on 28 February, Tehran and its allies struck targets in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states and disrupted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a major oil shipping channel, and the Red Sea.

The Mecca agreement has drawn a sharp reaction from Tehran, where an senior member of parliament said it would not help Saudi Arabia.

"The Saudis should know that a paper agreement with Turkey and Pakistan does not bring them security, just as years of unilateral milking of the Americans did not bring them security," Ebrahim Rezaei, a member of National Security commission, wrote on his X.

Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had already announced a joint defence pact last year.

The new Mecca Joint Defence Agreement sees three of the world's most powerful Muslim nations come together to offer mutual defence guarantees.

It aims "to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three States shall be regarded as an attack against them all", a joint statement reads.

"It further provides for the enhancement of all aspects of defence co-operation among the three States."

Although the pact pledges mutual support, it provides no specifics on the obligations of each party. A Turkish official quoted by Reuters news agency said the pact was "purely defensive in nature".

Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey each bring different qualities to the table, with each wanting something different out of it.

For the Saudis, this gives an extra level of security in a region whose security architecture has been upended by the US and Israel's war with Iran.

Last month, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels â who control much of the north-west of the country - announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and targeted Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

World.title: Spanish police arrest 78 people in bust of 'one of largest' smuggling networks
World.content:
One of the largest criminal networks smuggling drugs and people in the western Mediterranean has been dismantled, authorities have said.

Europol said 78 people were arrested in Spain and Algeria in a bust of the network, that is also linked to other criminal activities including "violent robberies, extortion, illegal detentions, and money laundering".

The group moved synthetic drugs from Spain and Portugal to Algeria, then used the return journey to smuggle migrants and weapons to the Spanish mainland and island of Ibiza on "ghost speedboats".

Some of the items seized included 18 high-speed vessels valued at â¬5m (Â£4.2m), guns, more than â¬25,000 (Â£21,400) in cash and 15,000 MDMA pills.

The sting, led by Spanish police, involved searches in 17 locations in Spain, including Alicante, AlmerÃ­a, Cartagena and Murcia.

Europol said the group had "evolved from drug trafficking into a duel-flow criminal enterprise designed to maximise profits" with outbound routes from Spain and Portugal to Algeria.

"The smuggling focused on synthetic drugs (such as MDMA), firearms, and explosives. Along routine routes from Algeria to Spain, the group smuggled migrants, charging up to â¬12,000 (Â£10,200) per person," Europol's statement said.

"In just one trip, over 50 migrants could be smuggled. All in all, profits from migrant smuggling alone are estimated to be more than â¬24m (Â£20m)."

The network also provided services to other organised crime groups, "facilitating the movement of illicit goods and people across the Western Mediterranean".

"Investigators believe the network coordinated multiple trafficking flows. Synthetic drugs, and sometimes people, were moved from France and Spain to Algeria, while cannabis resin, weapons, and migrants were transported from Algeria to Spain."

Often, the group used a fleet of high-powered speedboats to conduct rapid maritime operations. This included "ghost speedboats" which are designed to avoid registration and detection, which are prohibited in Spain.

"The group used these boats to organise transfers in international waters near the Spanish coastline," Europol said. "Once the cargo or migrants were handed over at sea, other network members arranged onward transport by land.

"Migrants were often carried in overcrowded boats without lighting or life jackets, frequently under extreme weather conditions.

"Investigators believe suspects perpetrated sexual assaults, physical abuse, and placed migrants in inhuman conditions in makeshift housing."

The suspects were primarily of Algerian origin and had connections to criminal groups in France, Belgium, Portugal, Italy and Poland.

Other objects seized in the police sting included satellite phones, GPS devices, encrypted communication tools and satellite dishes.

The announcement comes a week after roughly 78,000 migrants fled into the Spanish North African territory of Ceuta that was blamed on online rumours about an open border.

Most of the migrants returned to Morocco but between 3,000 and 5,000 remain in the territory, the exclave's leader Juan JesÃºs Vivas said.

World.title: Kidnapped rare Serbian eagle freed into wild after rescue
World.content:
A rare eastern imperial eagle has been rescued from animal traffickers and released back into the wild in Serbia after months in captivity.

After leaving the nest last year, Feliks was caught in Syria by poachers who eventually demanded a ransom - which was refused.

After protracted talks the bird was taken to a wildlife centre in Beirut, Lebanon, where he recuperated for more than half a year before his repatriation on a Serbian military plane.

The protected species is critically endangered, but conservation work since 2017 has brought the population in Serbia from one pair up to 29 pairs this year, according to the Bird Protection and Study Society of Serbia (BPSSS).

In July 2025, just as the young raptor first flew the nest, experts tracked him for conservation purposes as he flew towards the Middle East.

"At that point, we started to worry because we could see that he was heading towards an extremely unsafe region," Uros Stojiljkovic of the BPSSS told the AFP news agency.

When the bird's tracking signal was lost in October, initially it was thought the tracker was faulty.

But it soon became clear Feliks had been abducted and eventually was put up for sale by poachers.

World.title: Mexico and Peru restore diplomatic relations after asylum row
World.content:
Mexico and Peru have agreed to re-establish diplomatic relations following a row over the granting of asylum to a former Peruvian prime minister who was charged for a 2022 coup attempt.

In a joint statement released on 7 August, Lima and Mexico City said "historic ties of brotherhood, friendship and cooperation" prompted the reconciliation.

The two countries also reaffirmed "their respect for international law and the principles of the Charter of the United Nations".

Relations broke down after former Peruvian Prime Minister Betssy ChÃ¡vez sought asylum in the Mexican embassy in November 2025.

World.title: Meta fined $567m in largest child safety ruling against social media giant
World.content:
A US judge in New Mexico has ordered Meta to pay another $567m (Â£421m) for its failure to warn the public about dangers its platforms posed to children, marking the largest fine against the company over child safety.

Judge Bryan Biedscheid said the social media giant is a "public nuisance" akin to air pollution and that it must put the money in a fund aimed at reducing future harms.

Thursday's ruling is in addition to $375m in fines Meta was already ordered to pay in the case, for a total of $942m.

Judge Biedscheid compared Meta to a factory, with advertising and content as its product and "the psychological harm and sexual exploitation of children to be the pollution that must be abated".

A spokesman for Meta, which owns and operates Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Threads, said Thursday: "We disagree with the ruling and will appeal."

"We work hard to keep people safe on our platforms and have been transparent about the challenges of identifying and removing bad actors and harmful content," they added.

"We remain confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts."

Regarding the earlier $375m verdict in the case, Meta had said it intended to appeal the ruling and gave a similar explanation. It was the first time that a state had successfully sued Meta over child safety issues.

Meta is currently facing thousands of lawsuits in the US over similar issues. In addition to the New Mexico rulings, Meta earlier this year lost a landmark case in Los Angeles which found it could be held liable for building addictive platforms.

Bruce Daisley, a former European vice president of Twitter (now X), told BBC Radio 4's Today programme the New Mexico fine, while large, was "a drop in the ocean" for Meta.

In its latest financial results, the social media giant posted $61bn in revenue from April to June - up 28% on the same period a year ago.

"But it's an indication that we are moving to a stage where social media is going to be tackled around the world," he said.

Meanwhile, former safeguarding minister Jess Phillips told Today she believed US court challenges against big tech could enable the UK to take tougher action - without fearing it may damage UK-US diplomatic ties.

World.title: Trump again tries to limit US birthright citizenship with new executive orders
World.content:
Donald Trump is trying again to scale back birthright citizenship in the US, weeks after the Supreme Court shot down his previous attempt to eliminate the right.

The president signed two executive orders on Thursday, including one that expands the existing definitions of non-citizens whose children are not eligible for birthright citizenship.

The second order bans so-called birth tourism, the practice of pregnant mothers coming to the US to give birth so that their babies will be citizens.

"This should have happened years ago, but we're taking care of it now," Trump said from the Oval Office, criticising the Supreme Court's rejection of his previous bid to end the 150-year-old policy.

"My Administration has guarded against the risks posed by malign foreign actors who attempt to swindle American citizens by taking advantage of the generosity of our Nation," the first executive order says.

That order prohibits the automatic citizenship of babies born in the United States to two non-citizen parents where one of the parents is: a member of a foreign terrorist group, a foreign government employee, has attempted to gain citizenship through fraudulent means, or is living in US territories where citizenship is not conferred by federal statute.

Birthright citizenship for people born in US territories such as Puerto Rico is codified by federal statute.

Trump and members of his administration have repeatedly railed against birth tourism, including accusing Russian and Chinese adversaries of taking advantage of birthright citizenship to infiltrate the US.

While announcing the executive orders from the Oval Office on Thursday, Trump said that hundreds of thousands of babies have been born through birth tourism in the US.

World.title: EFCC returns recovered N125 million to Lagos land fraud victim
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has handed over N125 million recovered from an alleged land fraud suspect to a Lagos businessman, Akinsewa Akiode.

According to a statement on Friday by EFCC spokesperson Dele Oyewale, the money was presented to Mr Akiode on Thursday by the commission’s Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 in Ikoyi after an investigation into a petition he filed over the disputed property transaction.

The statement stated that Mr Akiode alleged that Olufemi Fashehun collected N125 million from him for the sale of a 550-square-metre parcel of land at No. 10, Kudirat Abiola Way, Oregun, Lagos.

He later discovered, however, that the property had been the subject of litigation since 2011, a fact the seller allegedly failed to disclose before collecting the money.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The EFCC said its investigation showed that Mr Fashehun had been served with several court processes, including injunctions restraining him from carrying out any construction on the property, but did not disclose the pending litigation before completing the transaction.

The commission noted that Mr Akiode eventually lost both the property and the structures he had begun putting up on the land, prompting him to seek its intervention.

After concluding its investigation, the EFCC said it recovered the full N125 million from the suspect and returned the money to the petitioner through Sterling Bank drafts.

The handover is the latest in a string of restitutions by the anti-graft agency. Just over two weeks ago, the commission returned N108 million recovered during an investigation into an alleged fraud involving two former employees of Greenwich Planet Sun King Nigeria Limited.

In October 2025, it also handed over three houses, two vehicles and N1.1 million recovered from a convicted fraudster to one of his victims in Ibadan after a Federal High Court ordered the assets forfeited.

Speaking at Thursday’s ceremony, the Acting Zonal Director of the EFCC’s Lagos Zonal Directorate 2, Bawa Kaltungo, said the commission would continue to investigate economic and financial crimes, recover illicit proceeds and ensure victims receive restitution where possible.

The EFCC did not state whether criminal charges have been filed against Mr Fashehun over the alleged fraud.

World.title: EFCC’s over-sabi and 2027 question: Is Tinubu being misled by his inner circle?, By Yushau A. Shuaib
World.content:
After the bishops’ recent closed‑door meeting with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Cardinal John Onaiyekan made a striking claim: that presidential aides are shielding the President from the true suffering in the country, presenting a false “rosy picture,” and that Tinubu already appears desperate about winning the 2027 election.

As a writer and observer of governance, I share that concern. A president who controls the instruments of state, commands a united party, and faces a divided opposition has little rational cause for electoral anxiety — unless overzealous handlers are manufacturing threats where few exist.

The question therefore deserves to be asked plainly: what exactly is President Bola Ahmed Tinubu afraid of?

The EFCC’s freezing of the Osun State Government’s accounts barely a week before the July 2025 governorship election — citing a court order later reversed by the President himself — was not merely a legal misstep. It was a political signal of ‘over‑sabi’ — that familiar Yoruba expression for excessive, misdirected overzealousness — gone disastrously wrong. It also raised a question that goes beyond Osun’s finances and cuts to the heart of governance in Abuja: are these the deliberate choices of a confident presidency, or the panicked manoeuvres of handlers who have convinced the President that 2027 is a battle he might lose?

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Because by any honest reading of Nigeria’s political landscape, the evidence for such fear is astonishingly thin.

Tinubu enters the 2027 cycle with structural advantages unmatched in recent democratic history.

He controls the executive machinery of the Federal Government with unusual cohesion. The CBN and FIRS — custodians of national treasury and revenue — and the full architecture of anti‑corruption agencies operate within a presidency facing no internal rebellion. The security services — police, DSS, and the military — answer to the Commander‑in‑Chief. INEC operates within a constitutional framework that any well‑resourced incumbent can navigate with relative ease.

Why should he entertain fear? His party, the APC, has absorbed opposition defections at a rate that has reshaped the electoral map. Several governors elected on opposition platforms in 2023 have since crossed over, weakening the institutional backbone of any credible challenge. The PDP, Labour Party, and other formations remain fractured — much like 2023, when the split between Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso arguably delivered the presidency to Tinubu on the platter of gold. Has he forgotten that blessing in disguise?

Tinubu won the 2023 election under conditions far more hostile than anything he faces today. President Muhammadu Buhari was not enthusiastic about his candidacy. Vice President Yemi Osinbajo, Senate President Ahmed Lawan, ministers, and other APC heavyweights were either rivals or reluctant supporters. Yet Tinubu prevailed.

He now enters 2027 with those internal rivals neutralised and with the incumbency advantage he lacked in 2023.

So why are his handlers suddenly desperate — even flirting with anti‑democratic impulses?

Should a president who survived 2023’s turbulence now need anti‑corruption agencies freezing a state’s accounts one week before an election to prove loyalty?

Governance under Tinubu is mixed — but not devoid of genuine achievements. Abuja, under the politically abrasive but undeniably effective Nyesom Wike, has witnessed accelerated infrastructural development: roads, housing schemes, and urban renewal projects visible to anyone who drives through the city. One may dislike his crude politics, but his performance as minister rivals the El‑Rufai era. Had these — and other ministerial achievements — been properly documented and consistently communicated, wouldn’t they have formed a persuasive counter‑narrative to critics?

The Ministry of Information and National Orientation has also done strategic work in countering the internationally amplified “Christian genocide” narrative — a framing that ignored the Muslim communities devastated by banditry and terrorism in the North‑West and North‑East. Doesn’t the lobbying that produced a more balanced posture from Washington — including under President Donald Trump — reflect a sophistication in foreign‑policy communication that deserves amplification?

The administration has increased military remuneration, strengthening loyalty to civilian command. The foiling of a reported coup attempt further consolidates military alignment with the presidency.Do these achievements justify political panic?

One under‑analysed dimension of Tinubu’s political arithmetic is the legacy of the Muslim–Muslim ticket. The Tinubu–Shettima pairing was controversial in 2023, with critics warning it would alienate Christian voters. Yet, paradoxically after the victory, the administration has appointed Christian technocrats to some of the most economically sensitive ministries and key security portfolios — alongside many Yoruba appointees. Whether by design or necessity, hasn’t the Muslim–Muslim ticket ended up delivering significant Christian representation at the apex of federal governance?

Retaining Shettima for 2027 follows the same logic: consolidate the Muslim North — especially the core North that delivered decisive margins — while Christian appointments counterbalance the optics. It is a defensible strategy. But doesn’t it require sophisticated communication — which has not always been forthcoming?

Back to Osun: The real danger. The EFCC’s freezing of Osun’s accounts days before an election was legally arguable but politically indefensible. The timing made it impossible to interpret as anything other than partisan interference. The President‑ordered reversal after the alleged court order only confirmed what the optics had already declared.

The damage is not to Governor Ademola Adeleke or the opposition party. The damage is to President Tinubu. It invites the central question every overzealous enforcement action provokes: did the President authorise this — and other similar actions, including judicial manoeuvres?

If yes, it suggests a president anxious about 2027 despite overwhelming structural advantages — or one willing to compromise institutional integrity for marginal electoral gain. If no, it suggests something equally dangerous: that agencies are acting in his name without his knowledge, and that the presidency is unable to control institutions under its authority.

Neither interpretation flatters the presidency. Both are politically corrosive.

Nigeria has seen this pattern before. Weaponising anti‑corruption agencies does not strengthen incumbents. It delegitimises institutions, hardens opposition resolve, generates sympathy for targeted figures, and provides ammunition to international observers already sceptical of Nigeria’s democratic governance.

Does the arithmetic of intimidation ever favour the intimidator?

Tinubu is not a political novice. He is one of the most strategically sophisticated political minds Nigeria has produced. The Lagos model — whatever its imperfections — demonstrates his ability to build and sustain political structures over decades.

Which makes the question more urgent: who is advising him that these manoeuvres are necessary? Are they genuinely trying to secure his re‑election? Or are some exploiting his perceived anxiety for their own selfish interests?

Because the greatest threat to a Tinubu second term is not Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, or Kwankwaso. It is the growing perception that a confident presidency is behaving like one that is not.

Yushau A. Shuaib is the author of MNI Versus MNIPR in NIPSS on Tackling Institutional Bullying. [email protected]

World.title: NPFL: Shooting Stars, Inter Lagos to kick off season with South-West derby
World.content:
The Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) will get back underway on 28 August with a South-west derby between Shooting Stars and newly promoted Inter Lagos after the fixtures for the 2026/27 season were unveiled on Friday.

The fixtures were released during the league’s Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Ibadan, setting the stage for another campaign featuring returning clubs, newly promoted sides, and several intriguing opening-weekend encounters.

The curtain-raiser will see five-time champions Shooting Stars host Inter Lagos under the floodlights at the Lekan Salami Stadium, Ibadan, on Friday, 28 August.

The remaining Matchday One fixtures are scheduled for Sunday, 30 August.

Former title contenders Rivers United begin at home against Plateau United, while Doma United welcome Sporting Lagos.

In Ilorin, Kwara United will launch their campaign against Kano Pillars at the Rashidi Yekini Main Bowl Stadium

Elsewhere, Barau FC host Nasarawa United in Kano, while Abia Warriors entertain Kun Khalifat.

Last season’s fourth-placed team, Ikorodu City, will begin their campaign at home against returning side Ranchers Bees, while Bendel Insurance face Warri Wolves in a South-South derby.

Rangers welcome Katsina United in Enugu, while Niger Tornadoes take on former champions Enyimba in Minna.

The opening fixtures promise an early test for several clubs, with supporters hoping their teams can make a positive start in what is expected to be another fiercely contested NPFL season.

World.title: Court orders Dana Air to pay passenger N5.5 million over 11-hour flight delay
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Lagos has ordered Dana Airlines Limited to pay a passenger N5.5 million in damages and legal costs over an 11-hour delay of a domestic flight, holding that the airline failed to justify the prolonged disruption.

In a judgement delivered on 25 May, Justice Yellim Bogoro ruled that Dana Air breached its contract of carriage by failing to transport Babajide Idowu as scheduled from Abuja to Lagos on Flight 9J-356 on 5 July 2018.

A certified true copy of the judgement obtained by PREMIUM TIMES on Friday showed that the court awarded Mr Idowu N5 million in general damages and N500,000 as solicitor’s fees.

Mr Idowu filed the suit in November 2019 through his lawyer, Lekan Ikuomola of Ayodeji Babajide and Lekan Partners.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He argued that Dana Air repeatedly postponed the flight and left him stranded at the Abuja airport for about 11 hours without explaining the reason for the delay.

He told the court that about 70 passengers were affected.

The claimant asked the court to declare that the airline breached its contract of carriage and sought compensation under Section 48(2) of the Civil Aviation Act, 2006, which incorporates the Montreal Convention into Nigerian law.

He also sought damages for psychological trauma, solicitor’s fees and litigation costs.

During the trial, Mr Idowu testified that although he eventually arrived in Lagos at about 11:10 p.m., neither the airline nor its officials gave passengers any reason for the repeated postponements.

According to him, it was only months later, after his lawyer exchanged correspondence with Dana Air, that he learnt the airline attributed the delay to regulatory safety checks.

Dana Air denied liability and filed a counterclaim.

Its Legal Officer, Chigozie Igbonugo, told the court that the delay resulted from safety advice issued by the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA).

He said passengers were informed through email notifications and airport announcements, adding that the airline’s conditions of carriage did not guarantee exact departure times.

Court’s findings

According to the documents, Mr Bogoro said there was no dispute that the flight was delayed.

“The defendant never denied that there was delay but has tried justifying the delay within the ambit of the permissible protocols for delay,” the judge declared.

The judge noted that once an airline accepts a passenger’s ticket, it assumes a contractual obligation to transport the passenger as agreed.

He was, however, not persuaded by Dana Air’s explanation for the disruption.

Although the airline maintained that the delay resulted from NCAA safety directives, Mr Bogoro found that it failed to produce any documentary evidence to support that claim or show that it had taken reasonable steps to avoid the delay.

“I have not found where the reason for the delay was communicated to the plaintiff,” the judge held, adding that the burden rested on the airline to prove its defence.

Relying on Section 48(2) of the Civil Aviation Act and the Montreal Convention, the court held that airlines are liable for damage caused by delays unless they can show they took all necessary measures to prevent the damage or that it was impossible to do so.

Mr Bogoro concluded that Dana Air failed to discharge that burden and declared that the airline breached its contract of carriage with Mr Idowu.

The court also accepted Mr Idowu’s claim that the prolonged delay caused him psychological trauma and awarded damages accordingly.

Counterclaim dismissed

The court also dismissed Dana Air’s counterclaim, in which the airline sought a declaration that it did not breach the Civil Aviation Act, the Nigerian Civil Aviation Regulations or the Montreal Convention.

Dana Air had asked the court to award it N10 million in general damages, arguing that the suit and media reports about it tarnished its reputation, reduced patronage and caused financial losses.

Mr Bogoro rejected those claims, holding that the airline failed to establish that Mr Idowu instigated the media reports or that the publications resulted in any measurable financial loss.

“There is no evidence led by the counterclaimant showing the defendant in counterclaim either instigated or initiated the media report,” the judge said.

He added that court proceedings are public and can be reported by journalists without the involvement of the parties to the case.

The judge also found that Dana Air failed to produce evidence linking the publications it relied on to any decline in patronage or financial hardship. He consequently dismissed the counterclaim in its entirety.

How the dispute began

According to court documents, Mr Idowu booked Flight 9J-356 from Abuja to Lagos, scheduled to depart at 12:33 p.m. on 5 July 2018.

Days before the trip, Dana Air began notifying him of changes to the departure time. The flight was first moved to 2:04 p.m. before being postponed several more times.

Mr Idowu told the court that throughout the day he repeatedly approached the airline’s sales and boarding desks to find out why the flight had been delayed. He said airline officials appealed for patience but did not explain what caused the disruption.

After arriving in Lagos, he sought compensation from the airline. When those efforts failed, he petitioned the then Consumer Protection Council, now the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC).

The dispute remained unresolved, prompting him to file the suit in November 2019.

The ruling adds to a growing body of Nigerian court decisions affirming passengers’ rights in disputes arising from delayed and cancelled flights.

Under the Civil Aviation Act, which incorporates the Montreal Convention into Nigerian law, airlines may be held liable for damage caused by delays unless they can demonstrate that they took all reasonable measures to prevent the disruption or that such measures were impossible.

The Nigerian Civil Aviation Regulations also require airlines to keep passengers informed during delays and provide appropriate care, including refreshments and communication, depending on the length and circumstances of the disruption.

World.title: Court jails four over $5.2 million money laundering scheme in Lagos
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Lagos has convicted and sentenced four persons to prison for their roles in a money laundering scheme involving more than $5.2 million.

Trial judge Friday Ogazi delivered the judgement on Wednesday after the four defendants pleaded guilty to charges filed by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

EFFC’s spokesperson Dele Oyewale named the convicts in a press statement on Friday as Bamidele Emmanuel, Abdullah Yusuf, Funmilayo Garuba and Gbenro Ademola.

They were separately arraigned on two counts of money laundering under the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to the EFCC, investigations showed that the four sold their personal information to one Afeez Animashaun, who allegedly approached them at Mushin Market in Lagos, where they carried out their businesses.

The anti-graft agency explained that the personal details were subsequently used to register four companies—College Compass Eduguide Nigeria Limited, Hortifresh Solutions Nigeria Limited, Eduboost Innovation Nigeria Limited and Fixit Hardware and Tools Nigeria Limited.

The EFCC alleged that corporate bank accounts opened in the names of the companies received a total of $5,296,691 in January 2025.

The prosecution comes amid sustained efforts by the EFCC to curb the use of shell companies and proxy bank accounts to launder illicit funds.

In recent years, the commission has repeatedly warned Nigerians against selling or surrendering their personal information for company registration or banking purposes, saying criminal syndicates often exploit such details to facilitate financial crimes, exposing their owners to prosecution.

One of the charges against Mr Emmanuel accused him of retaining $826,691 in a Wema Bank account between 1 and 31 January 2025, funds prosecutors said he reasonably ought to have known were proceeds of unlawful activities.

All four defendants pleaded guilty when the charges were read to them.

During the proceedings, the prosecution lawyer, Bilkisu Buhari, reviewed the facts of the cases and urged the court to convict the defendants and impose appropriate sanctions.

Sentences

In his judgement, Mr Ogazi convicted all four defendants on the second count of the charges.

Mr Emmanuel was sentenced to four months’ imprisonment, followed by three months of community service. He was also ordered to forfeit N1 million to the Federal Government.

Ms Garuba received four months’ imprisonment and 15 months of community service. The court also ordered her to forfeit N1 million to the Federal Government within 72 hours.

Mr Yusuf was sentenced to four months’ imprisonment, three months of community service and ordered to forfeit N800,000.

Mr Ademola was sentenced to four months’ imprisonment, three months of community service and directed to forfeit N700,000 to the Federal Government within 72 hours.

The judge further ordered the convicts to partner with the EFCC in public awareness campaigns on the dangers of indiscriminately selling or sharing personal information with others.

World.title: Lagos govt arrests 27 over alleged vandalism of newly built Festac-Alakija bridge
World.content:
The Lagos State Government has arrested 27 persons for allegedly vandalising a newly constructed bridge linking Festac Town and Alakija, saying the suspects removed key structural components of the facility.

The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, disclosed the arrests in a post on X on Friday after a midnight enforcement operation carried out beneath the bridge.

Mr Wahab stated that investigations showed that the suspects allegedly removed iron rods, steel reinforcements, cables and other materials critical to the bridge’s structural integrity.

He described the incident as a serious threat to public safety and government infrastructure.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Investigations revealed that suspected hoodlums had deliberately vandalised critical structural components of the bridge by removing iron rods, steel reinforcements, cables, and other supporting materials essential to the integrity of the infrastructure,” he said.

According to the commissioner, the suspects were arrested during a joint overnight operation involving operatives of the Rapid Response Squad (RRS) and the Kick Against Indiscipline (KAI) task force.

“The operation led to the arrest of 27 suspected hoodlums, who will be prosecuted in accordance with the extant laws of Lagos State,” he noted.

The latest arrests come months after the Lagos State Police Command arrested an 18-year-old suspect for allegedly vandalising reflective road studs installed on the Third Mainland Bridge.

Police said the road safety installations were removed from the bridge, warning that attacks on public infrastructure endanger motorists and impose additional costs on the government.

Mr Wahab explained that the state government would continue to crack down on vandalism and other offences that threaten public infrastructure.

“The Lagos State Government remains committed to protecting public infrastructure and will continue to take decisive action against individuals or groups engaged in acts of vandalism, environmental infractions and other criminal activities that threaten the safety and wellbeing of residents,” he said.

The commissioner did not disclose the identities of the suspects or indicate when they would be arraigned.

World.title: IGP explains appointment of CP for Osun governorship election
World.content:
The Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, on Friday said the Nigeria Police Force appointed Samuel Erale as the Commissioner of Police (CP) in charge of security during the forthcoming 15 August governorship election to restore confidence in the command’s neutrality.

Mr Disu said the subtantive CP, Ibrahim Gotan, was asked to step aside after political parties raised concerns about the neutrality of the Osun State Police Command, stressing that the decision was not a disciplinary action against him.

The Whistler reported that the IGP disclosed this on Friday in Abuja during a meeting with civil society organisations on election security in Osun State, led by the Executive Director of YIAGA Africa, Samson Itodo.

He said the police took the decision as a confidence-building measure to reassure political parties and other stakeholders that the force would remain neutral before, during and after the election.

The IGP said the decision followed rising political tension and violence in the state, with police intelligence linking some of the unrest to rival cult groups allegedly associated with political actors.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Certain groups of politicians or parties have been complaining that they no longer trust the Commissioner of Police. So the Commissioner of Police was asked to stand aside, while the Electoral Commissioner of Police took over,” Mr Disu said.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Mr Erale, the Electoral Commissioner of Police, had consequently assumed responsibility for election security in the state, while the Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of elections is expected to join the operation.

The development also follows weeks of political controversy over the conduct of the police command, including allegations of partisanship by political parties and civil society groups.

The Accord Party had demanded the removal of Mr Gotan, while civil society organisations also protested in Osogbo over what they described as concerns about the neutrality of the police ahead of the election.

The controversy intensified after the arrest of the Secretary to the Osun State Government, Teslim Igbalaye, and others during a police operation at his residence over alleged electoral offences.

The state government and supporters of Governor Ademola Adeleke criticised the operation, describing it as politically motivated, while the police maintained that it was part of an investigation. Mr Igbalaye was subsequently released.

However, barely 24 hours after Mr Igbalaye’s release, the Command announced the deployment of Mr Erale to oversee the state election and security of the state.

Against this backdrop, Mr Disu said the decision to replace the commissioner was intended to prevent the controversy surrounding the command from undermining confidence in the electoral process.

Concerns of partisanship of federal agencies regarding deepened on Wednesday when the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) blocked an Osun State Government account domiciled at First Bank.

In response to public outrage about the development, President Bola Tinubu, whose party, the All Progressives Congress, is fielding a candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, against Governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party in the forthcoming governorship election, intervened on Thursday, ordering the EFCC to lift the freeze order on the state’s account.

World.title: Osun Election: IGP assures voters of adequate security as Yiaga identifies 13 high-risk LGAs
World.content:
The Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, has assured residents of Osun State of adequate security ahead of the forthcoming governorship election, saying the force has put in place extensive measures to protect voters, electoral officials and other stakeholders throughout the electoral process.

Mr Disu gave the assurance on Friday during a stakeholders’ engagement on election security with civil society organisations, amid growing concerns over rising political violence in the state.

Also, a civil society organisation, Yiaga Africa, identified 13 of the state’s 30 local government areas as high-risk locations, citing persistent attacks, political tension and at least 34 deaths linked to election-related violence recorded over the past year.

During the meeting, the IGP urged eligible voters not to be intimidated by security concerns but to come out in large numbers to exercise their constitutional right to vote.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the police would provide security before, during and after the election to ensure a peaceful and credible process.

“We want the people of Osun State to come out and vote without fear. The Nigeria Police Force is fully prepared to secure the election and ensure that every eligible voter can exercise their democratic rights safely,” he said.

Police deploy officers to over 3,000 polling units

The police chief disclosed that security personnel would be deployed across more than 3,000 polling units in the state, with at least four officers assigned to each.

He added that additional security arrangements had been put in place to respond swiftly to any security threats that might arise during the election.

Mr Disu also revealed that an Assistant Inspector-General of Police would soon relocate to Osun to coordinate election security, strengthening the existing command structure ahead of the poll.

He explained that the police had already made strategic changes in the state’s security leadership after violence escalated.

According to him, the former Commissioner of Police in Osun was directed to step aside to allow another officer to oversee election security operations.

The IGP attributed much of the violence in the state to pre-existing cult-related rivalries that had become intertwined with political competition.

“We have issues of cultism in Osun already. It became easier for different parties to attack each other using the existing animosity in the state,” he said.

Mr Disu stressed that no political ambition was worth the loss of lives.

“No election is worthy of losing anyone because elections will come and go,” he said, while appealing to political parties, candidates and their supporters to conduct their campaigns peacefully and respect the rule of law.

Yiaga warns of insecurity, identifies flashpoints

Earlier, the Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, Samson Itodo, described the Osun governorship election as one of the most significant off-cycle elections in recent years because it would be the last major governorship election before the 2027 general elections.

He said the poll presents an opportunity to rebuild public confidence not only in Nigeria’s electoral management system but also in election security.

“The Osun election is strategically important because it is the last major election before the 2027 general elections. It is a unique opportunity to inspire public trust, not just in the management of elections, but also in election security,” he said.

Mr Itodo warned that insecurity and any perception of bias by security agencies could undermine the credibility of the election and weaken public confidence in democratic institutions.

According to him, Yiaga Africa’s election risk assessment identified 13 local government areas as high-risk due to recurring killings, violent attacks and heightened political tension.

He said the pattern of violence had evolved from coordinated shootings across several communities to politically motivated abductions and attacks on public institutions, including local government secretariats.

The organisation’s monitoring, he said, recorded about 44 violent incidents between June 2025 and June 2026, resulting in approximately 34 deaths.

Among the identified hotspots, Osogbo and Irewole LGAs were categorised as critical-risk areas, while Iwo, Boripe, Ife Central and Ife East LGAs were listed as high-risk local government areas requiring an enhanced security presence.

Mr Itodo said one of the greatest concerns expressed by citizens was the perceived neutrality of security agencies during elections.

He urged the police and other security agencies to remain professional and resist any attempt by political actors to influence their operations.

“The public wants to see institutions demonstrate neutrality so they can have confidence in the electoral process. An election marred by insecurity or perceived security bias could undermine public trust and the legitimacy of the outcome,” he said.

CISLAC calls for impartial policing

Also speaking, the Executive Director of the Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre (CISLAC) and Head of Transparency International Nigeria, Auwal Rafsanjani, pledged the support of civil society organisations for security agencies in ensuring peaceful elections.

He said civil society groups were not opponents of government, but partners committed to strengthening Nigeria’s democracy.

According to him, political tension ahead of the 2027 general elections makes it imperative for security agencies to act professionally and impartially.

“The safety and security of Nigerians during elections is extremely important. Our role as civil society is to support the security agencies so they can perform their responsibilities without bias or actions capable of eroding public confidence,” he said.

Mr Rafsanjani expressed confidence in the leadership of the IGP, saying his record would help guarantee credible election security.

He added that civil society organisations had developed recommendations to promote peaceful, violence-free, and internationally credible elections, stressing the need for continued collaboration between security agencies and non-state actors to safeguard Nigeria’s democracy.

The Osun governorship election is scheduled to hold on Saturday, 15 August, when eligible voters across the state’s 30 local government areas will elect a governor for a fresh four-year term.

The election is one of Nigeria’s off-cycle governorship polls, held outside the general election calendar due to judicial decisions that altered the tenures of previous administrations.

It is also regarded as the final major standalone election before the 2027 general elections, making it an important test of the country’s electoral and security institutions.

The contest is expected to be keenly fought, with incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party seeking re-election after leaving the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

His main challenger is Bola Oyebamiji (AMBO) of the All Progressives Congress (APC), while Najeem Salaam is contesting on the platform of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).
