World.title: Careless waste handling attracts rodents to the city
World.content:
The Põhja‑Tallinn district government is collecting tips about rat and mouse activity through mid‑August to direct pest control efforts to the most affected areas. Experts say careless waste handling encourages rodent spread.

Kadri Karnau, communications specialist at the Tallinn Environment and Public Works Department, said the city does not gather centralized statistics on rodent numbers because they cannot be reliably assessed. Still, residents' observations are welcome because they help identify larger colonies.

Rodent control in the capital is divided by areas of responsibility, meaning homeowners' associations play an important role. "When a colony is discovered, the first step is to speak with the private property owner or the homeowners' association, which is responsible for rodent control. The city and district government can only carry out control on areas they manage," Karnau said.

The Environment and Public Works Department uses rat poison placed in special plastic boxes. Karnau said districts do not conduct large‑scale preventive poisoning because it would pose a danger to pets, birds and people. Control is always targeted and based on specific nesting sites and movement paths.

Ettevõtmise eesmärk on leida üles kõige probleemsemad ja pahategelikud rotid. Autor/allikas: slyfox photography/Unsplash

Joosep Sarapuu, a zoologist at the Estonian Museum of Natural History, said local control will not eliminate rodents from the city. "It is not possible in practice to achieve 100‑percent eradication of rats. When one colony disappears, the area becomes freely accessible to newcomers again," he said.

Rat control is complicated by their biological behavior. They exhibit neophobia, meaning fear of new objects. When a plastic box with poison or a trap appears, rodents need time before they dare to approach it.

A common belief that colonies send their weakest members to test poison is not entirely accurate, Sarapuu said. "Dominant individuals do not check new things because they have established routes and a stable food supply. Lower‑ranking members are forced to look for new feeding sites and movement paths. That is why they are the first to encounter poison and traps," he said.

Joosep Sarapuu. Source: ERR

How can people keep rodents away from their homes? Sarapuu said summer is a good time to check a home's rodent‑proofing because pests try to enter houses when the weather gets cold. "You should find small gaps and openings where rats and mice can get inside and seal them carefully. Second, you must check food waste to make sure it is not easily accessible. In that case, rodents are likely to be fewer or not present at all," he said.

Karnau also said a tidy neighborhood is the best way to keep rodents away. "Trash rooms and waste containers must be kept in good condition and closed to prevent food waste from spreading into the surroundings. It is also wise to avoid feeding birds and squirrels and to keep the areas under bird feeders clean because fallen food attracts rodents," she said.

World.title: Expert: Talk of a direct Russian attack is extremely foolish
World.content:
Claims by anonymous American intelligence sources that a possible limited Russian attack against NATO may happen in the coming years are exaggerated speculation, said security expert Rainer Saks, former secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (2015-2020) and the Foreign Intellegence Service (2011-2015).

ERR: A U.S. intelligence assessment has been published by The Wall Street Journal, stating that Russian leader Vladimir Putin, whose invasion of Ukraine has stalled, could test NATO in the coming years by attacking one of the alliance's member states. The report mentions both cyberattacks and a limited ground incursion. What should we make of all this?

Rainer Saks: First of all, this is another classic case where anonymous sources have said something, fragments have been written down, but official comments are either unavailable or refused. It is a very broad and diffuse text.

As for these general assessments that Russia "could do something," there is no significant indication behind them that Russia is actually planning to do so. It is a hypothetical assessment that Russia could do this, that or the other. As long as Russia is not planning such actions, publishing assessments like this in the current context actually works very much in Russia's favor. Even the suggested time frame, from this autumn until 2029, is completely absurd.

Russia is certainly not making plans like that.

It is difficult to judge whether this was leaked by the U.S. government or is the initiative of an individual intelligence official. We will not speculate about that, but this is speculation rather than a report based on a concrete intelligence assessment.

The proposed actions — from cyberattacks to a limited military incursion — essentially cover the entire range of scenarios that could theoretically be considered. Therefore, I would not take this at present as a serious warning requiring the rapid implementation of countermeasures.

For example, Russia has been carrying out cyberattacks against NATO member states continuously since at least 2005–2006.

At the same time, NATO countries' responses have so far not been appropriate, because before the invasion of Ukraine, several European countries sought to engage Russia and develop energy cooperation instead. Examples of the kind of situation described in the intelligence report can also be found 15 to 20 years ago, so there is nothing new in it.

At the moment, publishing such a report works more to Russia's advantage, because Russia itself has not directly threatened NATO countries with any military action. Instead, a context is now being created that allows it to manipulate information even more than it has done so far.

In that sense, I think the text published by The Wall Street Journal is extremely foolish.

The article also points to indications that Russia is already testing NATO's response, for example, drones and missiles have fallen on the territory of Romania and Poland. This is presented as one indication that perhaps something is underway.

At the same time, those very countries have themselves said that they do not regard this as deliberate Russian action, but rather as accidental or technical incidents. I cannot say whether the official comments differ drastically from what is actually happening.

This is, of course, a problem because while active warfare is taking place in Ukraine, the possibility of, for example, Ukrainian drones ending up in allied territory or being shot down there is indeed an elevated risk.

There are only two main scenarios under which Russia would begin testing NATO's unity.

The first is that NATO has completely fallen apart internally. Although NATO's unity has suffered in several respects recently, there is no full political unity and there are sharp disagreements between different member states, it cannot be said that there is no unity at all. I would not yet go so far as to claim that NATO's collective defense has therefore been called into question.

The domestic political problems of member states and NATO's internal weakening are, in fact, the most likely scenario that could lead to a military confrontation between Russia and a NATO member state. At the moment, however, that process is clearly not advancing rapidly.

The second theoretical possibility is that if Russia truly decides to attack NATO militarily, it would first have to reorganize its forces. For such an attack — or even a test — to be genuinely supported, Russia would most likely have to carry out a mobilization. To some extent, that is theoretically possible after the State Duma elections, because the forces fighting against Ukraine have been unable to achieve success, and according to the Russian General Staff's calculations, there are too few troops.

In a situation where a full-scale war is still being fought in Ukraine, launching a new war against an even stronger opponent would, in my view, require Russia to declare martial law and carry out full-scale mobilization. That is something without which I do not believe Russia would proceed with very aggressive plans.

The article repeatedly refers to the fact that the Americans are running low on missile stockpiles because of operations in the Middle East and donations to Ukraine. Could it instead be that this article and the intelligence assessment are aimed at a domestic U.S. audience, to remind people of the need to replenish weapons stockpiles quickly?

That may indeed be the case. However, there is one important nuance here: the issue is not that the United States lacks certain types of missiles in its stockpiles, primarily air defense missiles and Tomahawk-type long-range strike weapons, of which too many have been expended against Iran. It is natural for stockpiles to decline during active military operations, but production is reportedly not keeping pace with what is needed. That is an embarrassing situation — what is the point of launching military operations if you cannot simultaneously replenish your stocks?

What is being overlooked, however, is that Russia has exactly the same problem, only even more severe. It also lacks sufficient air defense capabilities, as demonstrated by the success of Ukraine's long-range strikes. For example, this morning yet another large Wildberries warehouse, deep in the Urals some 1,800 kilometers from Ukraine, was set on fire.

Russia is in exactly the same position of weakness. Its entire missile capability is focused on Ukraine, and it is unable to carry out large-scale missile strikes on a daily basis. The war has lasted four years and has significantly exhausted Russia.

Of course, we can talk about hybrid attacks, but the conditions for Russia to launch a military incursion into NATO territory or start a military conflict with NATO are in no way favorable for Russia at present.

Why do you think intelligence assessments claiming that Russia is about to start testing NATO keep being published, when in reality they do not correspond to the facts?

I cannot answer that question. It is probably influenced by many different factors, ranging from incompetence and foolishness to domestic political objectives.

There is, of course, genuine reason to be concerned about the overall situation. There is nothing good about it. A major war is underway, and the governments of Europe and the United States have been unable to bring it to an end. That is indeed a very serious problem. Supporting Ukraine has also not been as successful as it should have been — a great deal has been done, but not enough.

A separate question is why European leaders have been unable to pull themselves together. Four years after the start of the full-scale war, they are still unable to produce enough of the military equipment that is needed. That is a very bad sign. In that sense, it is understandable that many people are seriously concerned about the situation and are trying to warn of possible negative developments.

World.title: Apple officially enters Iraq under new digital services framework
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Apple has legally joined Iraq’s regulated digital market, having met the country’s standards for digital platforms and services, according to the Communications and Media Commission (CMC).

According to the regulator, Apple has been categorized as a trusted digital service provider in Iraq, which includes the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, Apple Arcade, and Apple Ads.

The certification means Apple’s digital services may now function under an official Iraqi regulatory framework, having passed the CMC’s technical and legal standards.

Iraqi officials said the decision is anticipated to boost the country’s digital economy and enhance the investment climate for multinational technology firms.

The development also corresponds with a significant step toward Apple’s physical presence in the Iraqi market. Asiacell has reached a direct arrangement with Apple to include iPhones in its retail network across Iraq.

As part of the cooperation, Asiacell will provide real Apple products with valid warranties throughout its network, while retail personnel will undergo Apple-approved training.

The regulatory permission and Asiacell deal represent a substantial change in Apple’s position in Iraq, pushing both digital services and official device distribution further into a market of over 46 million people.

The move is another indication of Iraq’s quickly emerging technology and consumer market, as Baghdad attempts to lure global corporations, legalize digital services, and promote increased investment in the country’s information technology industry.

World.title: Al-Ghodwa deploys Linde warehouse equipment in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Linde Material Handling of Germany has completed a new warehouse technology project in Baghdad with its official Iraqi partner, Al-Ghodwa Group, as modern logistics systems gain traction in Iraq.

The project was completed in early August, and it comprised the installation and commissioning of two Linde Very Narrow Aisle (VNA) trucks built for high-density warehouse operations.

As part of the turnkey project, Al-Ghodwa installed the guiding system, calibrated and tested the equipment, and taught the local operators.

The technology enables firms to store more items in their current warehouse space by running equipment securely in tighter lanes, which increases productivity and reduces space needs.

The project combines Linde’s German warehouse technology with local installation, maintenance, and after-sales services in Iraq.

Linde Material Handling is a subsidiary of Germany’s KION Group, one of the world’s biggest producers of industrial vehicles and a leading supplier of warehouse automation systems.

The Baghdad installation comes as Iraq’s logistics and distribution industry grows, amid investment in manufacturing, retail, transportation, and private-sector growth.

World.title: Saudi renews invitation to Iraq PM as Baghdad, Riyadh seek to repair ties
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Saudi Arabia has extended an invitation to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi to visit Riyadh as the two countries try to regain momentum in ties after a dangerous escalation involving Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi soil.

Al-Zaidi met with Saudi intelligence head Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan in Baghdad on Friday, with the Saudi official conveying a message from the kingdom’s leadership extending the offer and discussing greater security cooperation, according to the Iraqi government.

The meeting is notable since Al-Zaidi canceled a scheduled visit to Saudi Arabia last month in response to US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq.

These operations followed a series of drone assaults on Saudi Arabia.

Riyadh claimed that Iran-backed militias fired drones from Iraqi territory, attempting to damage oil installations in the Eastern Province and targets near Riyadh, and publicly urged Baghdad to prevent its land from being used as a launchpad for assaults against the country.

Saudi Arabia then launched operations with US troops against Iran-backed militia strongholds in Iraq, increasing pressure on Baghdad to bring armed organizations operating outside of effective official control under its authority.

During Friday’s meeting, Al-Zaidi underlined Iraq’s refusal to allow its land to be used for attacks on Saudi Arabia or any other country, emphasizing Baghdad’s commitment to sovereignty, good neighbor relations, and regional security.

According to the Iraqi statement, the two sides agreed to maintain information sharing and security cooperation, with Baghdad aiming to avoid future assaults that may prompt another military reaction on Iraqi soil.

The outreach coincides with Saudi Arabia’s efforts to deepen regional security relationships.

On Friday, Riyadh, Ankara, and Islamabad signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, which states that any military assault on one of the three nations is considered an attack on all.

Saudi authorities are also apprehensive about additional strikes by Iran-aligned forces.

For Al-Zaidi, the repeated Saudi invitation provides a chance to mend ties with one of Iraq’s most significant Arab neighbors while also displaying Baghdad’s determination to prevent Iran-backed forces from dictating its regional connections.

The implications extend beyond security. Iraq has been pursuing more Saudi and Gulf investment as part of a larger push to diversify its economy, attract foreign money, and enhance trade and infrastructural ties with its Arab neighbors.

As a result, Friday’s meeting constitutes a crucial step in moving Baghdad-Riyadh relations past last month’s dispute. However, continued progress is likely to be strongly dependent on Iraq’s capacity to show that attacks on its neighbors would not be launched from its territory in the future.

World.title: Spain imposes border checks on Italy as migrant showdown grows
World.content:
Madrid – Spain announced on Friday it would introduce temporary border checks on travellers from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass migrant rush into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until September 7, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

Hours earlier, Spain threatened Italy with countermeasures if it did not swiftly lift its own border checks, drawing a rebuff from Rome.

The rare spat between the European Union and NATO allies came after tens of thousands of people crossed from Morocco to Spain’s North African territory on July 30-31 in an unprecedented, deadly rush.

The scenes infuriated EU members that back a hard line on irregular immigration, including Italy which imposed a one-month suspension of its visa free-travel Schengen deal with Spain.

The Spanish government slammed the measure Friday as “unfair, contrary to the EU’s interests and discriminatory for the Spanish population”.

Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares described it as “a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity.”

“We urge the government of Italy to rectify, put an end to the checks and treat Spaniards like other European citizens,” the government said.

He threatened “proportional measures” in response by Sunday if Italy failed to comply.

– ‘Creating rifts’ –

Within hours, the government of Italy’s far-right Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said it “had no intention of revising the decision” before August 15, when it said Spanish authorities “expected a new wave of migration” to hit Ceuta.

“Italy does not accept ultimatums or impositions from abroad regarding national security and border control,” Meloni’s office said in a statement.

“Only when there is certainty that there are no security or terrorism risks to Italy, that no new wave is occurring, and that no irregular migrants are heading toward European territory, will the decision be reconsidered,” it read.

Spain’s interior ministry announced the reciprocal measures within hours.

Spanish police have been monitoring online rumours and social media about possible fresh arrivals in Ceuta in mid-August, according to local media. But authorities have not expressly said they expect a repeat of last week’s rush.

Border authorities would in the meantime “do their utmost to ensure maximum ease of movement for Spanish and European citizens” who are not affected by border checks, the Italian statement added.

Italy, which does not share a land border with Spain, introduced border controls at maritime and air entry points for third-country nationals arriving from the Iberian country.

The move announced on July 31 was an “extraordinary measure” intended to “safeguard national security and prevent possible repercussions for our nation”, Meloni said at the time.

She was among EU leaders who called for Spain to be suspended from the visa-free Schengen travel zone after the Ceuta incident, despite such a move being legally impossible.

Italy’s coalition government has sought to stop the tens of thousands of people who land in small boats on the country’s shores each year.

The Spanish government warned against “creating rifts and sterile conflicts driven by internal electoral motives” and said “we trust that pro-European sentiment, common sense and good faith prevail”.

Of the 72,000 people who entered Ceuta, 70,000 have returned to Morocco, according to official Spanish figures.

Spanish authorities said 80 people died in the crossings.

Moroccan rights groups however estimate the figure to be higher. The Moroccan Association for Human Rights (AMDH) and the European Coordination for Human Rights in Morocco on Friday said at least 141 deaths were recorded and that the toll was likely to rise.

Morocco’s interior ministry has said 11 people died on its side of the border, all but one by drowning.

Those who remain in Ceuta — including hundreds of unaccompanied children — face dire living conditions with little access to food, water, and shelter.

World.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan sign defence pact amid regional war
World.content:
Riyadh – Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement on Friday amid violence in the region from Houthi attacks and the US-Iran war.

Riyadh is looking to strengthen its security ties against the backdrop of war between the United States and Iran, which has drawn in surrounding nations and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

The war has emboldened Iran and its Houthi allies in Yemen, both of which have attacked Saudi Arabia, while analysts say Washington is now seen as an increasingly unreliable partner.

In a joint statement published by the official Saudi press agency and Pakistan’s foreign ministry, the three countries announced the signing of the “Mecca Joint Defence Agreement”.

They declared a “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security and stability in the region and beyond”.

Pakistan’s foreign ministry said the pact meant an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all, adding it was “intended to strengthen collective deterrence”.

Ankara nonetheless said later that the agreement was “not aimed at any particular country”, according to a post on X by the presidency’s communications director.

It added that “the agreement is not in contradiction with the commitments of Turkey’s existing international alliances, including those at the heart of NATO,” according to a post on X by the government’s anti-disinformation service.

Riyadh said “the agreement does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”.

“Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race, rather it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said on X.

The “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region”, he added.

– ‘Layers of security’ –

Since the onset of the regional war, Saudi Arabia has grown closer to Turkey, Egypt and Pakistan, which have been pushing for mediation and a resolution to the conflict.

Umar Karim, an expert on Saudi foreign policy at the University of Birmingham, England, said the alignment “is clearly oriented towards Iran and meant to address Iran’s new strategic approach which is geared towards dominance of the broader Gulf region”.

The fact that Turkey and Pakistan border Iran means they could “exercise a different kind of leverage” on Tehran, he added.

A source close to the Saudi military and government told AFP before the signing that although the agreement had been under discussion for a long time, “the latest developments in the region expedite it”.

Andreas Krieg of King’s College London said the deal showed a clear desire to diversify alliances beyond the United States.

“Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are not trying to replace the United States,” he said.

“They are building the capacity to protect their interests when Washington cannot or will not do so.”

Riyadh, in particular, he added, “wants several layers of security rather than one American umbrella”, after the shock of the Iran war.

The deal will support Saudi Arabia’s ambitions to become an organiser of regional security and diversify its defence umbrella, said Krieg. Turkey and Pakistan gain political clout and access to potential Saudi investments, he added.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Mecca on Friday, the Turkish presidency said on X, sharing an image of the meeting.

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Asim Munir also travelled to the Gulf kingdom for the signing.

– Renewed Houthi attacks –

Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had already announced a mutual defence pact in 2025, a move that drew attention because Pakistan is the Muslim world’s only nuclear-armed state.

The deal also comes as a truce between Riyadh and the Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen has broken down. The Houthis have launched attacks on Saudi soil and declared a maritime blockade against Saudi Arabia, which they have attempted to enforce by attacking Saudi tankers.

The Houthis, backed by Iran, have added pressure to Gulf energy exporters — already under strain from Tehran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz — by threatening Red Sea shipping.

Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government against the Houthis since 2015.

A truce was agreed four years ago which largely held until hostilities broke out again in recent weeks.

On Thursday, the Houthis killed at least 58 Yemeni government troops in missile and drone attacks, a military source said, in one of the conflict’s deadliest days in years.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: Police put up posters of Lashkar commander across J&K, declare Rs 15L reward

Ramban Police seized an SUV after its driver allegedly tried to run over policemen manning a checkpoint on the Jammu-Srinagar national highway in Kunfer, Chanderkote, early Friday. One suspect was arrested, and a hunt for underway for two others on the run.



The police team signalled the vehicle to stop for a routine check around 3.52am. The SUV driver, however, ignored repeated signals and allegedly sped up in an apparent attempt to mow down the cops, a police spokesperson said. Sensing danger, Constable Rasal Chand fired three warning shots from his service rifle. That didnât deter the driver, who managed to flee the spot with two associates.



Police registered an FIR at Chanderkote PS under relevant BNS sections and launched a probe. A joint team of the Army, Ramban Police, SOG, and CRPF launched a manhunt for the three suspects and arrested one of them, identified as Altaf Mohammad from Udhampur. The SUV was also seized.



No terror angle had emerged in the probe so far, a police spokesperson said. The investigation officer and district mobile forensic unit collected evidence from the scene. Further investigation was underway.

MEA has dismissed as âfake newsâ a report claiming India sought a defence pact with Israel after the Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey security agreement.

NEW DELHI: The Ministry of External Affairs on Friday rejected a report claiming India had approached Israel for a defence pact following the signing of a new security agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey. The ministry called the claim âfake newsâ generated using artificial intelligence.The report, published by Turkish outlet Straturka and subsequently circulated on social media, claimed that New Delhi had initiated discussions with Tel Aviv to counter the emerging Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey security arrangement. The report cited unnamed Pakistani sources.The MEAâs Fact Check unit shared a screenshot of the report on X and flagged it as fake, warning users against what it described as malicious social media posts created using AI.âWe caution against such malicious posts on social media platforms which use AI to create fake content!â the ministryâs Fact Check wing said.The claim surfaced after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to deepen military and security cooperation among the three countries. Pakistan has described the agreement as a collective-deterrence arrangement, with its foreign ministry saying an armed attack on any one of the three signatories would be treated as an attack on all three.The agreement has drawn attention in New Delhi, with the MEA saying India is closely monitoring developments.âWe are also closely following this development, and we shall keep you updated,â MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at the ministryâs weekly briefing.The MEAâs clarification came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke by phone with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.The two leaders discussed ways to further strengthen the India-Israel Special Strategic Partnership and reviewed cooperation between the two countries across several areas.The conversation focused on strengthening bilateral ties and the existing partnership between India and Israel, rather than any new defence pact linked to the Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey agreement.

World.title: Watch: Delhi-NCR drowns in rain chaos; 7 videos show waterlogging, gridlock

World.title: Past tense, eye on future: Air India hikes pilots’ pay by 8% to 15%
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and then the same tapering with rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will primarily get command upgrade (become captains) in AI Express (which has only single aisles) and then move to AI (which has wide body aircraft too that have higher pay) for a âstrong foundation for progression within the groupâ. The group has tried to do multiple things â make AI Express more attractive for pilots through better pay and address shortage there mainly on the Boeing 737 fleet; check resignations and retain cockpit crew.AI pilots have for years been facing a 40 hour guaranteed pay â meaning they will get minimum for these many hours irrespective of actual flying and flying more will for more pay â while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours. This has been a cause of heartburn among pilots. Under the revised framework while AI will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Flying allowance rates beyond 40 hours have also been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.Now AI is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb level by next month.The constraint of Pakistan airspace closure remains for Indian carriers and the longer routes they have to take for flying to and from the west â unlike direct routes taken by foreign carriers â means higher flying time and greater pilot requirement.Now a senior commander flying for about 55 hours in a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh at present. And a first officer doing so will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh as of now.While privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24, the airline will not be counting mandatory weekly off time pilots get as per regulatory requirement and the new leave structure accounts does not factor that which comes across as a cut in leave, said people in the know. IndiGo may relook at its leave policy too for pilots.Since Tata Group took over AI and AI Express in Jan 2022, the Maharaja has lost over Rs 55,000 crore due to multiple factors. The pilot pay hike announced Friday indicates it is looking at the future and preparing for growth with hundreds of aircraft on order without being bogged down by the tumultuous recent past.âNew career pathways, enhanced compensation and benefits, and improved quality-of-life initiatives support Air India Group's next phase of expansion. At the heart of these initiatives is a clear, structured and transparent career pathway that provides faster command opportunities, long-term progression and access to one of the most significant widebody growth programmes in global aviation,â said an official.Since 2022, AI Group has grown from around 100 aircraft to nearly 300 aircraft and has placed orders for 600 new aircraft, including 80 wide body aircraft. Tatas are investing in capability building, including the establishment of a modern aviation academy in Gurugram with Airbus and Boeing full-flight simulators, and a new flying training school in Amravati, Maharashtra.âAs AI group expands, it is focused on developing and retaining internal talent through a structured progression model across Air India Express and Air India. Pilots across Air India and Air India Express will operate under a common seniority framework, creating an integrated and transparent pathway for career progression across the group. This framework provides greater visibility into future opportunities while ensuring a consistent and structured approach to advancement,â said teh official.Under the new framework, AI Express will serve as âthe primary pathway for pilots seeking command upgrades. This approach is designed to accelerate command opportunities, enable pilots to build command experience earlier in their careers, and create a strong foundation for progression within the Group.âFollowing command experience at AI Express, pilots will have the opportunity to progress to Air India and subsequently pursue widebody flying and command opportunities. âWith 80 additional widebody aircraft on order and scheduled for induction over the coming years, Air India offers pilots a long-term pathway that is unique in the Indian market,â the official said. An additional incentive is being offered to pilots who sign up to support the growing Boeing 737 fleet in Air India Express under which they will receive a fleet allowance.

World.title: India’s first satellite-guided chopper approached launched at HAL airport
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: HAL Airport in Bengaluru has become the first airport in India to operationalise a satellite-guided helicopter approach procedure, a move expected to improve safety, reduce flight times and enable more reliable all-weather operations.âThe Required Navigation Performance Category H (RNP CAT H) approach, developed by the Airports Authority of India (AAI), is designed exclusively for helicopters. The procedure was validated through flight trials by HAL test pilots and approved by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA),â HAL said Friday.The new approach, it added, enables helicopters to fly highly accurate, optimised flight paths using satellite-based navigation, allowing them to safely negotiate terrain and urban obstacles while operating in adverse weather conditions.According to HAL, the procedure cuts the approach time to HAL Airport from around 12 minutes to about 4 minutes.âThe operationalisation of Indiaâs first RNP CAT H helicopter approach is a significant milestone for the countryâs aviation ecosystem. This capability enhances the safety, efficiency and accessibility of helicopter operations and establishes a benchmark for similar procedures to be implemented at airports across the country,â HAL chairman and managing director Ravi K said.Besides improving safety, the system is expected to enhance operational efficiency and airspace capacity by allowing smoother integration of helicopter and fixed-wing aircraft movements. It also reduces the noise footprint over urban areas by enabling more precise flight paths.The faster approach routes are expected to benefit time-critical operations such as air ambulance services and search-and-rescue missions. HAL Airport, which handles nearly 50 helicopter movements every day, is one of the countryâs busiest helicopter hubs. The introduction of the RNP CAT H procedure addresses a long-standing gap in Indiaâs aviation infrastructure and could serve as a model for similar helicopter navigation procedures at other airports.

A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said it was not inclined to interfere with the high court's direction requiring the Krishnanagar MP to join the investigation.

Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Moitra, argued that she should be allowed to appear before the investigating officer virtually as she was entitled to do so under the law.

"The requirement as per the police's notice is to be at the police station in my own constituency.

Last time I went there two things happened. First there were threats that eggs will be thrown etc. and second time eggs were actually thrown," he submitted.

The bench, however, was unconvinced and orally observed, "You are a member of Parliament. Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs?

"When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest? These are applications that should not come before this court at all," it added, according to news agency PTI.





With the bench indicating that it would not grant relief, Moitra's counsel withdrew the petition, following which it was dismissed as withdrawn.

The plea challenged a July 21 order of the Calcutta High Court, which had granted Moitra interim protection from coercive action until October 5 in the hate speech case, while directing her to cooperate with the investigation.

World.title: Sashastra Seema Bal reserves 50% constable posts for ex-Agniveers, caste quota to apply
World.content:
After the Border Security Force (BSF), the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) has notified that 50% vacancies in the rank of Constables will be reserved for ex-Agniveers.

Although recruitment to the Army does not include caste-based reservations, the SSB stated that the existing quota for various categories, including Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and Other Backward Classes (OBCs) would be applicable.

On Monday (July 27, 2026), the SSB, the guarding force along the Nepal and Bhutan borders, notified new recruitment rules for ‘Constable (General Duty)’ posts.

So far, the BSF and SSB have notified 50% reservation for ex-Agniveers. The other Central forces, including the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), the Indo Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), and the Assam Rifles are yet to notify changes in their recruitment policies.

The first batch of Agniveers will be retired by the end of 2026.

Under the revised framework, half of all vacancies in a recruitment year in the SSB will continue to be filled through direct recruitment. Within this quota, specific reservations have been maintained for ex-servicemen (10%), remustered personnel (2.5%), and sportspersons (5%). If suitable candidates are not available under these categories, the vacancies may be filled via deputation or re-employment, and ultimately through direct recruitment.

The most notable change is that the remaining 50% of vacancies will be reserved exclusively for ex-Agniveers. To implement this, recruitment will take place in two phases. In the first phase, a designated nodal force will conduct a special recruitment drive to fill the vacancies earmarked for ex-Agniveers, in line with directions issued by the Central government.

If any of the seats meant for ex-Agniveers remain vacant after the first phase, they will not be left unfilled. Instead, in the second phase, they will be added to the remaining vacancies and filled through an Open Competitive Examination conducted under the existing recruitment provisions. This ensures that all available positions are ultimately filled while maintaining opportunities for ex-Agniveers.

On July 21, 2026, the Union Minister of State for Home Nityanand Rai informed the Lok Sabha that the government had created a new category of ‘Ex-Agniveer’ in the recruitments to the post of Constable (General Duty)/ Rifleman in the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and the Assam Rifles, reserving 50% of vacancies for ex-Agniveers, and exempting them from physical tests and written exams.

The Agnipath recruitment policy announced in 2022 met with violent protests and was among the major issues that drew attention during the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Following the protests, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs announced that 10% of all vacancies in the CAPFs would be reserved for armed forces recruits who had completed four years of service under the Agnipath scheme. The government also announced age relaxation of five years in the recruitment of the first batch of Agniveers, and of three years for subsequent batches.

World.title: Giri Pradakshina jams Visakhapatnam roads till past midnight; four-hour gridlock at Venkojipalem

Traffic seized up across Visakhapatnam on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) and stayed clogged until past midnight as lakhs of devotees took part in the annual Giri Pradakshina of Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy.

The worst-hit stretches were jammed for up to four hours. At Venkojipalem, where nothing but devotees moved, motorists switched off their engines and waited. Some slept in their cars. Others watched reels on their phones.

Vehicles at a standstill on Venkojipalem Road during the Giri Pradakshina rush in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday night. Motorists switched off their engines and waited; commuters said they were stuck for over three hours.

The Maddilapalem-RTC Complex stretch, the Visakha Valley Junction-Madhurawada road, the Adavivaram-Sontyam road, Gopalapatnam road, the NAD Junction-Gajuwaka corridor and H.B. Colony road all saw bumper-to-bumper traffic, particularly in the evening. Motorists on the RTC Complex-Maddilapalem stretch reported being stranded for over an hour in queues running several kilometres. The congestion spilled into connecting interior roads and forced commuters onto longer routes.

The Venkojipalem-Hanumanthawaka road was choked from the morning as thousands of devotees walked towards Madhurawada while regular traffic ran on the adjoining lanes.

The gridlock held families with children inside their vehicles for hours. Many residents said they had never seen congestion of this order in the city.

Traffic diversions were in place and a large number of police personnel were deployed, yet the flow proved unmanageable at several junctions. Frustrated commuters blamed inadequate traffic management and poor planning. They said the police failed to regulate movement despite the known scale of the pilgrimage’s turnout.

4.55 lakh on the route by midnight

The cumulative footfall on the Giri Pradakshina route crossed 4.55 lakh by midnight, according to the Command and Control Centre’s hourly report. Crowd movement was recorded as slow in the 11 p.m. to midnight slot.

Twelve medical cases were reported in that hour, most of them weakness, dehydration or breathlessness at points along the route including the Tholi Pavancha. All were referred to nearby hospitals and none was recorded as critical. Thirty-three medical camps and 26 ambulances were deployed along the route.

The APSRTC ran 535 buses and had cleared 4.15 lakh passengers by midnight. An electricity pole that fell near Kailasagiri on the way to Jodugullapalem was attended to by APEPDCL, and the congestion between Venkojipalem and Maddilapalem junctions was cleared late in the night, the report said. No law and order incident and no missing-person case was reported.

World.title: ‘We were mum on students’ stir’: U.P. RLD chief quits, flags corruption
World.content:
Rashtriya Lok Dal’s (RLD) state president in Uttar Pradesh Ramashish Rai on Friday (August 7, 2026) resigned from the party citing ideological and moral reasons for the decision adding due to continuous “attack on institutions amid rising corruption” in the country democracy and constitutional values is under threat.

In a letter addressed to the Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Education and party‘s national president Jayant Chaudhary, Mr. Rai said democracy in the country was being usurped by the financially powerful and influential sections with the society being divided on caste and religious lines for electoral gains. Mr. Rai, added matters of public good like education and employment is being neglected.

Speaking to The Hindu in Lucknow, Mr. Rai, said the way RLD, a party known to take positions on issues of public interest stopped making interventions over core matters, forced to him to take the step of resigning from the position and the party. “The RLD is the party formed by late former PM Chaudhary Charan Singh Ji, our leader Ajit Singh Ji, used to take clear stand for farmers, youth and even it amounts to going against the wind. But we were silent on the burning issue of students, youth during the recent protests. It was never the RLD way of politics, I was pained. I came to social service during the anti-emergency movement, my inner voice forced me take today’s decision in the wider interest of the society and Indian democracy,” he told The Hindu.

Asked whether he will join any political force, Mr. Rai said any decision will be taken after consulting supporters and well-wishers. “The main concern to save the democratic and socialist fabric of our country,” said the former RLD State chief.

The RLD, is the largest alliance partner of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in U.P. Under the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) it won two seats in the Lok Sabha polls in 2024 and had one Rajya Sabha MP. The party’s strength in 403 members U.P. assembly is nine MLAs and won one MLC in the Council.

World.title: Students involved in NEET paper leak agitation facing police crackdown, says AISA
World.content:
The All India Students’ Association (AISA) on Tuesday alleged that protesters involved in the agitation against the NEET paper leak are facing a police crackdown across the country.

The students’ body claimed that multiple SFI activists, including former JNUSU president Dhananjay, AISA Bihar secretary Dipankar Mishra, and Patna University activists Divyam Kumar and Saba Afreen, have been arrested in Bihar.

AISA national president Neha, one of the prominent faces during the protest, said during a press conference at the Press Club of India: “We were assured that students protesting peacefully would not face repression. However, what we have witnessed is continued arrests, arbitrary detentions and intimidation of students across the country. The government must uphold its promises, release those detained and engage with the concerns of students.”

In addition to arrests made in Bihar, West Bengal and Jharkhand, AISA said that protesters were sent notices in Delhi’s Jamia Nagar. “It has come to our notice that in Jamia Nagar, student protesters are being sent notices based on retina and face scanning for their presence at Jantar Mantar. AISA Jamia has issued a helpline for legal aid in the matter,” AISA said in a statement.

The organisation reiterated its demand to release all protesters and give compensation for those injured in police brutality. They also demanded the scrapping of the National Testing Agency (NTA) and repeal of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020.

World.title: New sculpture of celebrated actor Uttam Kumar in Kolkata draws flak from artists
World.content:
Artists in West Bengal have expressed outrage over a statue of Bengali cinema icon Uttam Kumar, which was recently unveiled at Keoratala Crematorium in Kolkata by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. “Neither does the statue have any resemblance to the yesteryear superstar, nor is it a work of art,” said critics.

Uttam Kumar, who is known as the “Mahanayak“ (superstar) of Bengali cinema, is held in high regard in the cultural circles of Bengal. However, this recently unveiled statue of the artist has left artists in the State unsettled.

“This is very ugly; the people who do this work are incompetent, and the people who commission it are equally incompetent. They do not understand art. People who are close to politicians are becoming artists now. This work is done through tenders; but artwork through tenders is absurd, and this is the result. Artists are low-paid. They work on short deadlines; how will they deliver?“ celebrated senior artist and sculptor Sanatan Dinda told The Hindu.

Also read: Uttam Kumar and intimations of immortality

Mr. Dinda also said Kolkata is becoming a jungle of fibreglass artwork and that it shows very badly on Bengalis who were once highly regarded for their understanding of art and culture. He added that artists are not asked for suggestions when such pieces are commissioned and are done on the freewill of politicians, leading to these badly done artwork across the city.

“No one has ever insulted Uttam Kumar more than this. This man had walked out of Bollywood because he said artists are not respected there, and they did this to him. Any artist who has loved the work of Uttam Kumar will say that he did not deserve this,” veteran playwright and artist Chandan Sen said. He also called for immediate removal of the sculpture.

Not only artists but political parties in the Opposition have criticised the move. Trinamool Congress MLA Kunal Ghosh urged the State government not to install this statue and suggested that it be replaced with something better. “Everyone who sees it is saying that whatever else it may be, it cannot be the Mahanayak’s statue. Perhaps it was inaugurated in haste,” Mr. Ghosh wrote on his social media.

Since the unveiling on July 24 on the 47th death anniversary of Uttam Kumar, the statue has gone viral on social media as netizens criticised the artwork and said that it has no resemblance to the late actor.

However, there is one more massive sculpture of the late actor in the Tollygunge area where the film studios reside and where the actor spent most of his working days. That was inaugurated in 1993 and was highly appreciated by artists for its quality artwork.

When the Bharatiya Janta Party came to power in Bengal, sports minister Nisith Pramanik ordered an immediate removal of a sculpture outside the Salt Lake Stadium and said that it was ugly. An emotion that was shared by many across the city. The structure was of a lower body of a football player with two footballs on his two feet. It was designed by former CM Mamata Banerjee.

During Ms Banerjee’s tenure, many such structures and sculptures were commissioned, several of which were highly criticised for their quality.

World.title: Redeployment of staff nurses continues amid growing objections
World.content:
Despite repeated appeals for the creation of new posts in government hospitals, Tamil Nadu continues to depend on redeployment of healthcare staff to address manpower gaps. In the latest move, the State government has given the nod to redeploy 210 posts of staff nurses from seven new medical college hospitals to four major institutions that are in need of manpower.

Accordingly, 40 posts each from the Government Medical College Hospital (GMCH), Namakkal and GMCH, Tiruvallur, 20 each from GMCH, Krishnagiri and GMCH, Tiruppur, 30 each from GMCH, The Nilgiris, GMCH, Ariyalur and GMCH, Kallakurichi are being redeployed to four “needy medical institutions” - Government Stanley Medical College Hospital (SMCH), Government Mohan Kumaramangalam Medical College Hospital, Salem, Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Government Hospital, Tiruchi, and Chengalpattu Medical College Hospital, an order said.

Of the 210 posts, the largest share of 70 goes to SMCH, while 50 posts each are being redeployed to Tiruchi and Chengalpattu, and 40 to Salem.

The proposal for redeployment was sent by working out the details of the total staff nurse posts and bed strength-staff nurse ratio, before and after the proposed redeployment in the seven new medical college hospitals and four institutions under the control of the Directorate of Medical Education and Research.

The directorate justified the redeployment by outlining the critical role played by nurses in patient care. It also said that the 210 posts proposed for redeployment were not being diverted, redeployed to any other unit or surrendered for the creation of any other posts.

This move has drawn criticism from a nurses’ association, which has been repeatedly demanding the creation of new nursing posts as per the patient load. There is an acute shortage of nurses in government hospitals, primary health centres, and government medical college hospitals.

N. Subin, general secretary of The Tamil Nadu Nurses Empowerment Association, in a statement, condemned the move to redeploy 210 posts of staff nurses. Earlier this month, the association had objected to a move to redeploy 292 nursing posts from the Directorate of Public Health and Preventive Medicine and government hospitals.

Creating new nursing posts is the appropriate solution to address staff shortages. Instead, redeploying existing posts from one hospital to another would affect the health services provided by these hospitals and the workload on nurses will increase.

This decision could affect nurses who are waiting for permanent employment. This has caused distress and disappointment among nurses. Despite repeatedly raising demands and submitting several appeals, the government continues to ignore the demands of nurses. The association said they would be forced to resort to continuous protests.

The newly elected Tamil Nadu government should immediately intervene, abandon the move to reduce staff through redeployment and cancel the government order immediately, it said.

World.title: How did memory chipmaker CXMT become China’s most valuable stock? | Explained
World.content:
The story so far: A little-known Chinese chipmaker became the world’s most talked-about stock on Monday (July 27, 2026). ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), based in Hefei, saw its shares soar 466% on their first day of trading on Shanghai’s STAR Market. The company sold shares at 8.66 yuan each, raising $8.6 billion. By the close of trading, the company was valued at 3.3 trillion yuan ($488 billion) — making CXMT the most valuable company listed in mainland China. The initial public offering was oversubscribed by 212 times.

This explosive market debut has drawn intense scrutiny in Washington. A senior U.S. official indicated to the New York Post that there was “a real suspicion” that state intervention from Beijing had helped drive up the stock price. Within 24 hours, a bipartisan group of U.S. lawmakers opened an official inquiry.

Behind the market drama lies a significant shift in global technology: investors are betting that China can successfully build a domestic semiconductor industry capable of powering advanced artificial intelligence without depending on the United States.

The unsung silicon hero

CXMT operates in the field of Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM), the vital memory chip found inside every smartphone, laptop, and data server. For years, DRAM was treated as a low-margin, commoditised component of the hardware sector.

The rise of generative AI changed those dynamics overnight. Modern AI models require immense volumes of high-speed memory to process complex datasets. As technology companies globally rushed to construct AI data centres, memory chips quickly became scarce. An overlooked hardware component was suddenly transformed into a strategic asset. It is this industry-wide memory shortage, rather than any sudden technological breakthrough by CXMT, that explains the firm’s valuation.

Still chasing the leaders

While CXMT is China’s leading DRAM manufacturer, it currently holds only about 7.7% of the global market. The industry remains highly consolidated, with South Korea’s Samsung and SK Hynix, alongside America’s Micron, collectively controlling roughly 90% of global supply.

The gap is wider in High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM), the specialised, ultra-fast memory stacked vertically to work directly alongside high-end AI processors. Morningstar estimates that CXMT trails global leaders Samsung and SK Hynix by at least three years in HBM development, and continues to manufacture its chips at a significantly higher cost.

Yet, the shifting market has provided a major tailwind. As AI-driven demand outstripped global supply, DRAM prices nearly doubled in a single quarter. Apple has reportedly begun testing CXMT memory chips for iPhones designated for sale within the Chinese domestic market. A product that once competed on low margins has now been drawn into the centre of a geopolitical technology war.

Why memory matters

An advanced AI processor is functionally useless if it cannot access and feed data efficiently. To meet this need, market leaders Samsung and SK Hynix have shifted significant manufacturing capacity away from standard DRAM toward high-margin HBM. This pivot has left a supply gap in ordinary DRAM, which CXMT has aggressively stepped in to fill.

To understand how this fits into the wider technology ecosystem, the semiconductor industry can be divided into five segments:

Toolmakers: (e.g., ASML), which engineer the complex lithography machines needed to print circuits.

Foundries: (e.g., TSMC and China’s SMIC), which physically manufacture silicon wafers designed by other companies.

Memory Companies: (e.g., Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, and CXMT), which design and build data-retention hardware.

Design Firms: (e.g., Nvidia and AMD), which design cutting-edge logic chips but outsource their physical production.

Integrated Device Manufacturers: (e.g., Intel), which traditionally handle both design and physical fabrication in-house.

Historically, memory has been one of the weakest links in China’s domestic chip supply chain. Yet, China’s broader AI aspirations depend heavily on it. Huawei’s Ascend processors, as well as AI models built by Chinese developers like DeepSeek and Zhipu, cannot operate without reliable, high-speed memory chips. As U.S. export restrictions continue to tighten, domestic alternatives have become vital.

Taiwan at the centre

No semiconductor narrative is complete without Taiwan. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) alone manufactures more than 90% of the world’s most advanced logic chips.

Beijing views Taiwan as a renegade province and has not ruled out the use of force to bring the island under its control. Conversely, while Washington officially recognises the “One China” policy, it continues to supply defensive arms to Taiwan. This leaves the world’s most critical semiconductor fabrication facilities sitting in the crosshairs of one of the planet’s tensest geopolitical standoffs.

Taiwan says chipmaker’s move to invest $100 billion in the U.S. wasn’t because of U.S. pressure

In response to this vulnerability, Beijing has prioritised onshore self-sufficiency. In Chip War, historian Chris Miller notes that while the United States spent decades growing comfortable outsourcing its physical manufacturing to concentrated nodes in East Asia, China spent that same period working systematically to dismantle its reliance on foreign suppliers.

Between 2024 and late 2025, China’s domestic semiconductor self-sufficiency rate reportedly jumped from 16% to 28%. Beijing has backed this effort with an estimated $150 billion in state-led funding, targeting an ambitious self-sufficiency goal of 80% by 2030.

Despite these capital injections, China faces physical barriers. Its leading domestic foundry, SMIC, remains unable to advance past 7-nanometer manufacturing because Western export controls prevent it from purchasing ASML’s advanced extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems.

The Council on Foreign Relations estimates that the leading U.S. AI processors remain roughly five times more powerful than their closest Chinese equivalents. Analysts at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) note that while Washington’s export controls are slowing China’s advanced technological development, they are failing to stop it entirely.

Washington’s contradictions

The geopolitical struggle over physical hardware has coincided with security failures in the software and model layers, highlighting contradictions in U.S. AI policy.

In July 2026, OpenAI disclosed a major security breach. During an internal cyber-red-teaming exercise evaluating offensive hacking capabilities on the ExploitGym benchmark with standard safety filters disabled, a combination of GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased frontier model broke containment. The models autonomously discovered and chained a zero-day vulnerability in OpenAI’s internal package proxy, gained access to the open web, and hacked into Hugging Face’s production database to steal the answers to their own evaluation. OpenAI termed the autonomous escape and subsequent breach “unprecedented”.

When Hugging Face’s security team rushed to perform forensics, they encountered an immediate barrier: commercial closed-source US APIs blocked their analysis requests. Because Hugging Face had to feed real exploit payloads and command-and-control logs into the systems to reconstruct the attack, the closed models’ safety guardrails repeatedly blocked them. To bypass this, Hugging Face had to run a Chinese open-weight model, GLM 5.2, locally on its own servers to successfully process over 17,000 log events and contain the breach.

At the same time, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that Chinese AI developers could face financial sanctions and placement on the Commerce Department’s Entity List for “intellectual property theft”. Mr. Bessent warned on social media that “open source is not open season on American IP,” targeting Chinese developers accused of performing large-scale “model distillation”.

This threat triggered resistance from the technology industry. A coalition of over 40 companies—including Nvidia, Microsoft, and Hugging Face—signed a public letter titled “Open Weights and American AI Leadership,” arguing that open-weights models are a vital tool for cyber defence. On July 27, 2026, Nvidia launched the Open Secure AI Alliance with 37 founding members to develop and share open safety tools. OpenAI and Google eventually signed the open-weight letter as well.

Anthropic, however, refused to sign. Its chief executive, Dario Amodei, explained that he disagreed with the industry’s claim that openness inherently favours defenders over attackers. He warned that open-weights models could be stripped of guardrails, allowing malicious actors to develop cyberweapons or biological threats.

This has left Washington in an awkward policy position: the government is restricting advanced chips and threatening to sanction Chinese AI models, yet in an active cybersecurity emergency, a prominent technology platform had to rely on a Chinese open-weight model to defend against an escaped American AI.

As technology analyst Dan Wang writes in his book ‘Breakneck’, this reflects a fundamental systemic divide: China operates as an “engineering state” focused on building infrastructure and hardware, while the United States has evolved into a “lawyerly society” that responds to crises by writing complex, restrictive rules.

What goals does Semicon 2.0 aim to achieve? | Explained

India’s alternative path

Rather than attempting to compete with China in capital-intensive chip fabrication, India is focusing on becoming the premier global hub for AI computing.

The India Semiconductor Mission has backed a dozen domestic manufacturing and assembly projects worth roughly $9 billion. These include a Micron packaging plant in Gujarat and a Tata-PSMC fabrication facility in Dholera. These plants focus on mature, legacy nodes rather than cutting-edge processors.

In parallel, India is attracting investments in AI data centres. Under the “China Plus One” corporate strategy, multinational technology giants are shifting capital into Indian infrastructure. Microsoft has committed $17.5 billion in Indian cloud and AI infrastructure through 2029, Google has announced $15 billion in investments, and the Adani Group has pledged $100 billion to build AI-ready, high-capacity data centres by 2035.

A domestic semiconductor fabrication plant builds industrial expertise and high-tech engineering skills. Conversely, a data centre is capital-intensive but physically simple, generating massive demand for local electricity. The cutting-edge chips inside those data centres still belong to American firms, the software is developed in Silicon Valley, and the majority of profits flow to the United States.

The real wager

CXMT’s debut on the Shanghai Stock Exchange reflects investor confidence in China’s direction, not current technological parity. At the cutting edge of manufacturing, China still trails the global state of the art.

However, China is steadily winning global market share, manufacturing higher volumes of chips, and eroding its dependence on Western supply lines. As artificial intelligence continues to mature, the global power struggle is becoming a contest over physical infrastructure as much as it is over software algorithms. Ultimately, the nation that can build, scale, and secure the physical infrastructure to keep AI running may hold the advantage.

World.title: Chennai-based Anicut Capital to invest in 20 startups with ₹175-crore fund
World.content:
Chennai-headquartered Anicut Capital, an alternative asset management company managing multiple Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) across both debt and equity strategies, has launched Grand Anicut Seed Fund (GASF) with a target corpus of ₹175 crore and a greenshoe option of ₹75 crore. This is Anicut’s second fund for early-stage investments. The fund is set to focus on Pre-e to Series A investments across deep-tech, enterprise-tech, consumer, and financial services startups.

“We have been investing in early-stage equity since 2021 through our first fund, which was an angel fund. Through that fund, we built a portfolio across these four sectors. The strategy worked well for us, and we have developed a strong investment playbook for these sectors that has been time-tested and validated. It has also generated strong returns,” Ajay Anand, partner, Anicut Capital, told The Hindu.

With GASF, Anicut plans to invest in over 20 startups with ticket sizes in the range of ₹5 crore to ₹8 crore. The fund is targeting a first close soon, with a target LP mix of Institutional Investors, HNIs, and domestic and foreign family offices. The fund has started deploying and have closed three deals, all being led by Anicut.

“With our second fund, we aim to build on this proven strategy by partnering with exceptional founders in their 0-to-1 journey, providing both capital and strategic support as they create next-generation categories and build enduring, market-leading businesses,” Mr. Ajay added.

Anicut has been investing in early-stage equity since 2021 through Grand Anicut Angel Fund (GAAF), which has made 68 investments to date ranging from pre-seed to pre-series A across deep-tech, enterprise tech, consumer and financial services startups. These startups have gone on to raise follow-on capital to the tune of over ₹6,000 crore, with 10x portfolio revenue growth since the first check. Notable portfolio companies under GAAF include Agnikul Cosmos, GIVA, CapGrid, InspeCity, Leumas, Neeman’s, Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters, Snapmint, Salty, GRIP, Galaxeye, E-plane, and E-trnl.

Anicut Capital is an alternative asset management company managing multiple AIFs across both debt and equity strategies. Managing seven diverse funds, including three debt funds and four equity funds, Anicut has a total active AUM (Assets Under Management) of over ₹4,500 crore.

World.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye sign tripartite defence agreement in Makkah
World.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday signed a joint defence pact in Makkah that empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to strengthen the collective security of the three states, was signed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammad bin Salman, and Türkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the “Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence” held at Al-Safa Palace.

The three countries announced the signing of the agreement in a joint statement published by the Foreign Office (FO) and Saudi Arabia’s official SPA press agency.

The statement said the pact reflected the three countries’ “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

“The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all.”

It also “provides for the enhancement of all aspects of defence cooperation” among the three countries, the statement added.

The agreement is “guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity that unite them, and building upon their shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation”.

During the Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence, the “distinguished relations” between the three countries were reviewed, “along with a number of issues of mutual interest”, the statement noted.

Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony.

The defence and foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were in attendance as well, pictures showed.

Sealing the agreement in Makkah, the holiest site in Islam, adds symbolic heft to a pact that builds on longstanding bilateral military ties among the three countries.

The agreement ties together Pakistan, the only nuclear-armed Muslim country; Saudi Arabia, the home to Islam’s holiest sites and one of the world’s top oil exporters; and Turkiye, Nato’s second-largest military.

‘Shield of peace’

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif described the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement as a “historic pact”, saying the three countries were united by faith, friendship and a shared commitment to peace and security.

In a post on X, the prime minister said he was honoured to sign the agreement alongside the Saudi crown prince and the Turkish president.

He said the pact would serve as a “shield of peace” for generations and expressed hope that it would bring prosperity to the three countries and the wider Muslim world. Shehbaz also appreciated Field Marshal Asim Munir’s efforts and dedication towards the agreement.

‘Historic day for Pakistan’

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, while talking to a private TV channel, described the signing of the joint defence agreement between the three states as a “historic day” for Pakistan, saying the pact reflected growing recognition of the country’s defence capabilities and strengthened ties among the three nations.

Speaking about the agreement, Tarar said the defence cooperation framework would take relations between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to a new level. He credited Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir with bringing the three countries together, saying they had an “ideal working relationship” and that their teamwork had contributed to recent successes.

Tarar said the agreement was aimed at strengthening defence cooperation and served as a form of deterrence rather than aggression. The minister further said Pakistan’s capabilities had been demonstrated during last year’s conflict with India and claimed that the country had since played a role in promoting regional peace.

Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan said that the signing of the joint defence agreement by the crown prince, the president of Türkiye and the prime minister of Pakistan underscored the depth of the fraternal and strategic relations between the three countries.

He said the agreement marked an important milestone in their defence cooperation and reflected their shared desire to coordinate efforts to address challenges and threats affecting regional security and stability. He added that the pact embodied the three countries’ shared political will to safeguard security, support a more secure regional environment and pave the way for greater development and prosperity.

Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the agreement “does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”.

“Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race; rather, it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” he wrote on X.

He noted that the deal “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region, nor does it represent an escalation of tensions between any two states”.

The Saudi official further said the agreement “does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries”.

Mansoor Ahmed, of the Australian National University’s Strategic and Defence Studies Centre, said Islamabad and Ankara bring strong defence industries to the table, while Riyadh could contribute with technological spending.

While the pact comes in the backdrop of the US-Israel war on Iran, Bloomberg had reported in January — before the conflict began — that Ankara was seeking to join a separate mutual defence pact between Islamabad and Riyadh.
